      Grant Criteria 
      The 2 Billion Trees program aims to motivate and support new tree planting projects. Over the course of 10 years, by 2031 up to $3.2 billion will be invested in tree planting efforts to support provinces, territories, third-party organizations and Indigenous organizations plant two billion trees across Canada. Grant Value:Up to $40 million per fiscal year; ORUp to 50% of eligible project costs for regular applicants or up to 75% of eligible project costs for Indigenous-led projectsTurnaround Time: Approximately 6 months. Eligible Applicants: A municipal or local government or one of their agencies, or a regional municipal organization;A not-for-profit organization registered in Canada, such as a charitable organization, volunteer organization, community, professional, industry or other association, land conservation organization, or non-government organization;A for-profit organization (legally incorporated or registered in Canada);An Indigenous organization (for-profit and not-for-profit) or community; andOrganizations looking to be project aggregators. Potential aggregators should describe their concept of operations in their project description. Ineligible Applicants:Individual landowners;Provincial and Territorial Governments;Federal Government Departments; andCrown Corporations.Eligibile Expenses:Salaries and benefits, and employee recruitment and training;Professional, technical, and capacity building services;Community and landowner engagement;Purchase or lease of land for nurseries to grow seedlings;Translation, production, printing, publication and distribution, and media services;Contractors, such as for tree planting and silviculture;Materials and supplies, such as seeds and trees for planting;Transportation;Facilities;Machinery and equipment;Travel expenses including accommodation and venue expenses; Honoraria and ceremonial costs where Indigenous recipients or Indigenous partners are involved; andOverhead expenditures, provided that they are directly related and essential to the conduct of the project, up to 15% of eligible expenditures. Eligible Projects: Contribute to incremental planting and associated management of trees and forests. Activities must be in addition to that which would occur without the initiative, and not legally required, such as following commercial activity or as a condition for impact assessment approval;Contribute clear benefits in terms of net carbon sequestration and greenhouse gas emission reduction in the period up to 2050, and seek to minimize GHG emissions in the early years. Examples of carbon sequestration considerations include: Selecting planting sites where no or minimal vegetation removal is required;Purchasing seedlings from local nurseries and minimizing the distance travelled for planted, monitoring and maintenance, thereby reducing transportation emissions;Limiting intensive site preparation activities, such as salvage harvesting after an insect infestation, trenching, or vegetation removal, all of which can cause substantial emissions early in the project;Reducing the use of pesticides/herbicides; and Limiting equipment use.Seek to achieve human well-being and environmental co-benefits;Contribute to planting that is ecologically suitable or otherwise appropriate for its location, given site conditions (this includes not planting on sites that naturally would be non forest ecosystems, such as natural grasslands or wetlands); and Result in permanent additions to forests, improve existing forests, or allow for permanent protection of forests.Ineligible Projects: Projects that help organizations that have a legal obligations to regenerate forests, such as a legal obligation to regenerate after harvesting under sustainable forest management regimes; andProjects that regenerate forests on private lands as part of business-as-usual commercial forestry activities.Program Details: Max funding through the Tree Planting streams is $40 million per fiscal year, for a maximum of 8 fiscal years (for a total of 320 million); The maximum that NRCan contribution for eligible project costs is 50% of eligible expenditures;For Indigenous-led projects the 2BT Program will consider up to 75% of eligible costs for the tree planting projects;Apply by January 16, 2025, for a decision by July 2025;Apply by May 15, 2025, for a decision by November 2025;Apply by September 18, 2025, for a decision by March 2026;There are currently 3 streams under the 2 Billion Tree Program:Mass Planting Stream;Small-Scale Planting Stream;Urban/ Suburban Stream;Mass Planting Stream: Must plant an average of 500,000 seedlings/trees per calendar year (January to December) in each year in which planting occurs. Projects can include Long-Term-Planting Work;Allow for planting to occur across multiple sites, as long as the average number of trees planted per calendar year, in years which planting occurs, is equal to or greater than 500,000;Can include forest or tree restoration portions of work involving riparian zones, habitat restoration and
other ecosystem improvement projects;Cannot be located in urban and suburban areas;When preparing a Mass planting Stream proposal, please consider the following: Choice to pursue afforestation, reforestation or both;choice of seed sources, variety of tree species of trees planted and their ability to survive and grow in the climate that may exist over the next century; co-benefits resulting from chose tree plating activities including permanence.Small-Scale Planting Stream:Must plant an average of 50,000 trees per calendar year (January to December) in each year in which planting occurs;Allow for planting to occur across multiple sites, as long as the average number of trees planted per calendar year, in years in which planting occurs, is equal to or greater than 50,000;Can include forest or tree restoration portions of work involving riparian zones, habitat restoration and other ecosystem improvement projects;Cannot be located in urban and suburban areas;Must have clearly defined planting sites;When preparing a Small-scale Planting Stream proposal, please consider the following: Choice to pursue afforestation, reforestation or both;choice of seed sources, variety of tree species of trees planted and their ability to survive and grow in the climate that may exist over the next century; co-benefits resulting from chose tree plating activities including permanence.Urban/ Suburban Stream): Must plant an average of 10,000 trees per calendar year (January to December) in each year in which planting occurs;The program recommends collaborative project proposals in order to meet this threshold, as needed;Allow for planting to occur across multiple sites, as long as the average number of trees planted per calendar year, in years in which planting occurs, is equal to or greater than 10,000;Must be located in and around urban areas, population centres or communities;Must have clearly defined planting sites;When preparing a Urban/Suburban Stream proposal, please consider the following:Choice of seed sources, variety of tree species of trees planted and their ability to survive and grow in the climate that may exist over the next century;Co-benefits resulting from chosen tree planting activities including permanence.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices: Ongoing funding is encouraged, and applicants are encouraged to apply for more than one fiscal year;Eligible Best Practices:This program covers up to 50% of eligible project costs or 75% for indigenous-led projects;This program is not retroactive;The program allows for additional support from other federal and provincial programs up to 100% of total project costs.Forms:Program Webpage: click  hereEligibility Assessment Page: click hereProgram Guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program aims to promote entrepreneurship in Indigenous communities and increase the number of viable businesses owned by Indigenous people through non-repayable grants of up to $99,999, issued through designated Aboriginal Financial Institutions (AFIs) located across the country. Program details are determined by the AFIs, and may vary from location to location, but in general, the funds may be used to support proposals for starting, acquiring, or expanding a business, and to leverage other sources of funding. Consult your local AFI for application instructions (see "Forms" for directory link).Grant Value: Up to $99,999 for Individual Indigenous entrepreneurs; andUp to $250,000 for eligible Indigenous community businesses.Turnaround Time: 2-8 weeksEligible Applicants:Indigenous individuals;Businesses owned and controlled by Indigenous people;Indigenous and non-indigenous organizations and associations (except those with a religious or charitable purpose); First Nations and Inuit communities and governments;Canadian owned and controlled banks, credit unions, and trust companies;Private equity providers;Provincial and federal crown corporations; andMunicipal governments, labour organizations, and post-secondary institutions. Note: Eligibility criteria may vary between AFIs. Many AFIs only serve Indigenous individuals, businesses, and organizations in their local area.Eligible Projects:Projects may involve starting, purchasing, expanding, or modernizing a business, and must create measurable benefits, including but not limited to additional revenue, new markets, and/or new job opportunities;Examples of eligible activities include: Advertising campaigns, trade shows, seminars, and conferences; Research; Process and product development; Productivity improvement; and Investment in new technology and/or systems.Ineligible Projects:Community infrastructure projects that are unrelated to commercial enterprise;Purchase of land, buildings, and/or investment property; andBusiness activity related to pawn shops, payday loan firms, gaming operations, and/or the production/distribution of alcohol, tobacco, and sexually exploitative materials.Note: Be sure to consult your local AFI for a more detailed list of eligibility criteria.Program Details: Application requirements vary slightly between AFIs. In most cases, the first step is to submit an application form and business plan;Financial support for the creation of the business plan is available from most AFIs;Applicants must provide proof of their ability to cover at least some of the project costs (usually 10% of the total);Project financials and performance may be monitored for up to three years after the funding agreement is issued; andTo proceed with an application, consult the AFI directory to find an Aboriginal Financial Institution near you. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:This program can be combined with funding from provincial sources;Because application processes vary between institutions, it is essential to find an AFI near you, and review the instructions for their version of the program;Indigenous business owners in BC can access this funding through the Business Equity Program at Tale’awtxw Aboriginal Capital Corporation.Eligible Best Practices: Most AFIs do not allow the funding to be used retroactively.Forms:Program website: click hereDirectory of Aboriginal Financial Institutions: click here

    Updated on 2025/03/28

grants.grant_criteria: AccelerateIP offers intellectual property (IP) training, 1 on 1 mentorship. This program also covers some costs for IP legal strategy support as well as costs for legal implementation support. The program has 3 streams: 1.) Education & Awareness 2.) Strategy 3.) Implementation. Eligible organizations must have fewer than 500 full-time employees and must have innovative technology or be in the tech sector. The intent of this program is to increase access to education, skills development, mentorship, and professional support for startups to protect, implement and leverage their intellectual property.
grants.best_practices: Process Best Practices:The program allows funding to be used in conjunction with other sources of funding so long as the applicant still contributes 25% (or 10% for Indigenous applicants) themselves;For applicants applying to multiple streams, the program advises the applicant to complete Stream 2 first. This way they will have a stronger strategy before applying to Stream 3;Applicants have the option to add a mentor or a BAI member as a collaborator to help with the application process. Collaborators are able to access all the information entered during the application process, they are not impacting the selection process;If startups in Stream 2 are not sure which services they need, it is recommended that startups apply to Stream 2- Tier 1 mentorship services and/or the IP Certification program prior to applying to Tier 2.Eligible Best Practices:If startups in Stream 2 are not sure which services they need, it is recommended that startups apply to Stream 2- Tier 1 mentorship services and/or the IP Certification program prior to applying to Tier 2; andIf the applicant has an existing external IP mentor, they are still eligible so long as the mentor is eligible and working at a partner or collaborator organization associated with the program.

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program funds research projects that explore the adoption and/or adaption of new and existing technologies to the agricultural industry in Alberta. The aim of the program is to increase discovery, development and application of agricultural products, processes, practices,  services and technologies.Grant Value: Non -Capital Expenses: Up to 60% for post-secondary institution or a for-profit legal entity;Up to 80% for non post-secondary institutions.Capital expenses covered up to 25%.Turnaround Time: The program does not have a fixed turnaround time for processing applications. The time it takes to review an application is contingent upon the number of applications currently under consideration and the amount requested.Eligible Applicants:An Industry Organization;A Municipal Government or an agency of a Municipal Government;A Post-Secondary Institution;A Primary Producer;A for-profit legal entity, including research companies and businesses offering custom services, consulting, or general service to agricultural clients; orAn applicants approved by RDAR.Ineligible Applicants:Federal government and its agencies and institutions; andReligious organizations, churches, and similar organizations.Eligible Activities:Investments in primary research that is aligned with the provincial needs of the sector;Producer public-private collaboration on research and research priority-setting;Demonstrating and evaluating new agricultural practices and technologies in the Alberta context;Sharing and disseminating research knowledge, including through events such as workshops and symposia;Supporting farms and firms to develop or adapt new or improved product processes or practices that add value;Strategic investment in the use and development of clean and sustainable processes/technologies;Developing highly qualified personnel;Facilitating public-private partnerships for the development of innovation centres;Commercialization activities; andOther activities related to research and development and knowledge transfer.One or more of the following activities must be part of the proposed project:Organizing, hosting, facilitating, attending, or presenting at KTT(Knowledge Translation and Transfer) events such as:group, in-person events such as workshops, seminars, or classes;web-based events such as webinars;on-site activities such as field tours, demonstrations, demonstration sites; andconference/tradeshows specifically for KTT and not for sales/marketing; andDeveloping and distributing KTT products such as a factsheets, videos, publications and podcasts.Ineligible Activities:Normal and ongoing operating and maintenance activities; Activities that do not provide a direct benefit to the Sector;Activities which provide tax credits or rebates;Scale-up of new technologies beyond pilot stage;Commercial marketing activities for products and technologies created through the research project;Ongoing website updates and/or maintenance; andNew buildings, expansions, or structural modifications.Eligible Expenses: Salaries and benefits of scientific and technical personnel who conduct the eligible activity;Costs for fee-for-service providers or contributors deemed essential to the project;Costs of supplies, equipment rentals and land rentals directly required for the eligible activity;Stipends and benefits for students who conduct the eligible activity;Reasonable travel expenses directly related to the project;Rentals, leases of venues, technology, and equipment directly related to the project;Costs related to surveys, information gathering, and performance reporting;Commercialization expenses (ie: patent, intellectual property); andCosts of risk, welfare, economic, and environmental assessments.Note: Capital purchases of equipment and technology under $500,000 inclusive of all associated costs, directly required for the eligible activity will be covered.Ineligible Expenses: Any expenses not directly related to the research project;GST, HST, PST;Costs of in-kind contribution;Costs incurred outside the project term laid out in the funding agreement;Expenses paid to any Government of Canada department or agency;Expenses related to hosting celebratory events (ie: food, alcohol, etc.);Costs related to commercial product development;Website hosing/domain registration;Travel expenses for individuals that are not Project team members;Costs associated with complying with assurance programs;Normal ongoing administrative and operational costs;Purchase of common items that can be used for multiple purposes (ie: cellphones, digital cameras, etc.);Lease of office furniture, space, and/or equipment;Costs of equipment attached to a building, such as sinks, walls, doors, plumbing, framing and flooring;Repair and/or maintenance of existing infrastructure; andIndirect overhead costs.Program Details:Intake is ongoing, and applications may be submitted any time while funding remains;Applicants are invited to submit a Letter of Intent;Applications are reviewed by scientific and industry experts, and assessed for feasibility, industry impact, collaboration and commercialization potential, and alignment with program priorities;In-kind contributions are not reimbursed under the program, but applicants may include them as part of their required contribution, subject to RDAR's approval;The payment schedule will be outlined in the funding agreement; andIf funds are not fully allocated, the remaining balance must be returned to RDAR.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Agricultural Clean Technology Program: Research and Innovation stream provides up to $2 million in funding to support the research, development, and demonstration of pre-market clean technology. The priority areas include green energy, precision agriculture, and bio-economy. The intent of the program is to promote sustainable growth and lower carbon emissions in Canada's agriculture and agri-food sectors.Grant Value: Up to 60% of project costs to a maximum of $2 million per project;The maximum amount payable to a recipient with multiple projects will generally not exceed $5 million.Note: Funding under this stream is repayable and non-repayable. andPersons with disabilities.Maximum funding across multiple projects will generally not exceed $5 million;Priority areas:Green energy and energy efficiency:Including but not limited to:Improvements on lighting, insulation, heating, refrigeration, and ventilation efficiency;Energy efficiency technology;Zero-emissions on-farm equipment and machinery; andEnergy generation technologies such as solar panels, heat pumps, and biodigesters.Precision agriculture - technologies to gather and process data to guide targeted actions that improve the sustainability, efficiency, and productivity of agricultural operationsIncluding but not limited to:Driver assistance and machine auto-guidance; andDecision support tools and technologies that improve in real-time input, use, and nutrient management.Bioeconomy - utilization of agriculture waste and by-products for energy and bio-product generationIncluding but not limited to:Biofuels and digestate production used as bioenergy, soil nutrients, and water;Manure management technologies;Agri-based products, such as:Bioplastics;Biomass-based construction products and car parts.Costs incurred from the date of the submission of a completed application are eligible;In-kind contributions are not eligible under the Agricultural Clean Technology Program;Payments for eligible project costs will only be made once a Contribution Agreement is signed;Applicants will be required to provide financial, progress, and performance reports, or other reports as detailed in the contribution agreement; andRepayable funding will be repaid over a period of up to 10 years following project completion.

      Grant Criteria 
      Through this program, primary and Indigenous producers, conservation groups, water purveyors and Indigenous communities will have access to cost-shared funding to adapt to climate change by investing in water infrastructure. Stream 3 offers up to $100,000 for agricultural water supply assessments, engineering studies or plans.Grant Value: Stream 3: 75% up to $100,000.Turnaround Time: Up to 60 days after deadline.Eligible Applicants: Activities 1 & 2: Irrigation/ Improvement districts & local/municipal governments including First Nations.Activity 3: Incorporated and individual producers;Agricultural and conservation groups;Irrigation/improvement districts and local/municipal governments that supply water to agricultural; andIndigenous Communities and Indigenous Producers. Ineligible Applicants: Non-agricultural individuals or groups;Provincial and federal governments; andCrown Corporations.Eligible Activities: Activity 1: Water supply assessment or feasibility studies in key agricultural areas to determine available water supply:In some areas of B.C., some streams or aquifers may be fully subscribed for licensing. Identifying streams or aquifers that are not fully subscribed may allow increase water supplied for agriculture; andIdentifying potential water storage sources could help alleviate future climate change induced drought.Eligible Costs: Consulting services by Qualified Professionals.Ineligible Items: Construction services. Activity 2: Engineering studies or plans for water purveyors to assess and determine opportunities for upgrades and expansion of existing purveyed water systems:Many purveyed water systems engineering studies or plans before any efficiency upgrades or expansion can occur.Eligible Cost:Consulting services by Qualified Professionals.Ineligible Items:Construction services.Activity 3: Dam engineering assessments, water release plans, dam safety reviews, redetermination of consequences classification or any professional consultative services under the Dam Safety Regulation:Dams are assessed for their risk consequence rating and may require upgrades to continue use. The cost of the engineering assessment and a design plan are often a financial barrier to producers.Eligible Costs:Consulting services by Qualified Professionals.Ineligible Items: Construction services. Ineligible Activities: Activities or costs incurred prior to approval;In-kind activities;Activities to support non-agricultural water use;Activities not directly related to agricultural water use;Purchase of farm equipment and related accessories or attachments (including tractors, skid steers and trailers);Activities that are not compliant with federal, provincial, or local/municipal regulations;Financial compensation for lost income, production or land or other associated losses due to water shortages, government orders, or other reasons;Activities to remove land from the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR);Purchase of land or easement;Regular or on-going operating or maintenance activities;Training or educational courses;Financing charges, loan interest payments, bank fees and related charges;Activities currently receiving funding from other funding sources; andGST and other taxes/credits reimbursed to applicant.Program Details:Deadline for application July 31, 2023;All projects must be completed by January 15, 2026;An initial payment (50%) will be made by IAF to all projects upon signing of their contribution agreement, however IAF may reduce this advance based on project/applicant risk;Interim and final payments will not be initiated by IAF until reporting requirements are satisfactorily met by the client; Interim and final payments will be made based on actual expenses reported and payments will be made in arrears;All reports require a final report and a minimum of 20% of approved funding will be retained by IAD, pending submission of final reporting; andIf permits are pending/under review but the application is otherwise complete, IAF will proceed to consider and adjudicate the application, however any approval will be conditional until all required documentation is received.

      Grant Criteria 
      Alberta agriculture and agri-food processing employers can access $5,000 to $30,000 (90% cost share) for HR training, consulting, and capacity building to improve recruitment, retention, and workplace practices through March 2027.Grant Value: Up to 90% of costs ($5,000 to $30,000).Turnaround Time:  To be confirmed. Eligible Applicants:Primary agricultural producers (must produce at least $10,000 in farm commodities annually);Agri-food processors that transform agricultural commodities into value-added products;Alberta industry organizations representing producers or processors:Commodity associations;Industry associations;Producer associations.Must directly serve primary agriculture or agri-food processing sectors;Must be based in Alberta; andOther indirect affiliations.Eligible Participants:Business owners and managers receiving HR coaching or training; andInternal HR or leadership teams improving workforce practices.Eligible Activities:Designing, reviewing, or modernizing HR and hiring policies;Designing or updating compensation strategies to support employee attraction and retention (excluding temporary foreign workers);Improving and standardizing employee onboarding processes;Developing reward and recognition strategies to strengthen workplace culture;Enhancing HR interview and selection practices;Implementing or improving HR information systems (HRIS);Developing HR policy manuals and employee handbooks, including role clarity;Developing and implementing Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategies;Integrating HR processes and documentation with payroll systems; andConducting employee surveys and feedback activities to support continuous improvement.Ineligible Activities:Activities unrelated to workforce or HR capacity;Duplicate projects already funded; andActivities outside agriculture or agri-food workforce improvement.Eligible Expenses:Training fees for HR capacity building; andConsulting fees paid to third-party consultants for eligible activities.Ineligible Expenses:Activities not related to HR improvement or workforce management;Costs already funded through another government program;Costs outside approved project scope; andNon-eligible business expenses unrelated to HR or workforce development.Program Detail:The program helps employers build self-reliance and HR expertise in Alberta agriculture and agri-food processing sectors by increasing HR knowledge and best practices;90/10 cost share program: 90% of eligible expenses covered by grant, 10% applicant contribution required; Up to 40% of approved funding provided upon application acceptance;Final payment based on project completion, paid invoices submitted to Agriculture for Life, less any advance funds;Applicants can apply more than once, but not for the same work - each application must demonstrate a different HR strategy or intended outcome;Applicants can engage facilitators and consultants to coach business owners on HR best practices, improving recruitment, retention, and reducing employee turnover;Projects must be completed by November 30, 2026. Final claims due December 14, 2026. andActivities aimed at established/traditional markets where the sector has been active for 5+ years (case-by-case discussion possible).Eligible Expenses:Costs are eligible as of April 1, 2026 and must be in the approved budget, tied to the work plan, reasonable/necessary, and within program limits;Salaries and benefits (normally not more than 25% of total project costs; must be additional to existing costs; timesheets/supporting docs expected);Contracted services (with contracts/payment terms/deliverables; includes translation/interpretation and project management for activities);Travel (project-related; includes transport, accommodation, per diems, etc., with specific travel rules/limits):Travel within Canada:Trip outside the traveller’s headquarters with no overnight stay: $100 CAD per day;Trip outside the traveller’s headquarters with an overnight stay: $400 CAD per dayTravel outside Canada:Trip outside the traveller’s headquarters with no overnight stay: $125 CAD per day;U.S. trip outside the traveller’s headquarters with overnight stays: $475 CAD per day;International (non-U.S.) trip outside the traveller’s headquarters with overnight stays: $575 CAD per day. Capital assets (limited—primarily displays for trade shows/promotional purposes; >$10,000 requires pre-approval); andOther direct project costs (examples: shipping, conference/registration fees, licensing fees, printing, translation, marketing costs for materials/plans, meeting room/AV rentals).Note: The complete list of eligible costs, including detailed breakdowns and requirements, is available on the program website.Ineligible Expenses:In-kind contributions (cannot be counted toward the applicant share);Performance pay/bonuses, severance, and certain “perk” benefits;Purchase of land, buildings, or equipment; banking charges/interest/credit card fees; business cards/season greetings/subscriptions; memberships in trade/professional orgs; retail listing/slotting fees; andCosts already reimbursed under another federal/provincial/territorial/municipal program; AAFC  covers up to 70% of eligible costs; applicants must contribute at least 30% in cash (in-kind contributions are not eligible);Minimum project size: $20,000 total eligible costs (minimum AAFC contribution of $14,000);Applications are accepted from February 13, 2026 until September 30, 2030 (may close earlier if funds are fully committed). Program ends March 31, 2031;AAFC expects results such as opening new non-traditional markets and increasing the volume/value of exports and interprovincial trade, with defined targets and performance indicators;Project duration should not exceed 18 months from the effective date of the signed contribution agreement;Key Funding Conditions:Applications must be complete before proceeding to assessment;Funding is only confirmed once a contribution agreement is signed;Costs incurred before the agreement is signed are not reimbursable;Only expenses included in the approved budget and work plan are eligible;Supporting documentation (invoices, proof of payment, contracts, timesheets, etc.) is required for all claims.Application process :Confirm eligibility (organization type, sector, SME status, market diversification focus);Prepare a project plan and a detailed budget aligned with eligible activities and expenses;Gather required documents (financial statements, incorporation documents, signing authority, etc.);Submit complete application online before the intake deadline;AAFC conducts a completeness review, followed by a program assessment;If approved, sign the contribution agreement before starting eligible reimbursable activities;Submit claims and progress reports according to the schedule outlined in the contribution agreement;AAFC reviews claims and issues reimbursement once approved;         December 24, 2025Additional Funding is available for Winter 2026 term (January-April).
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This federally funded program offers wage subsidies to agriculture employers looking to hire students for a work-integrated learning experience. The subsidy covers 70% of the student's salary, up to $7000. The program aims to strengthen connections between agriculture employers and post-secondary institutions, to bring diversity and new ideas to the industry, and to expose students to careers in agriculture they might not have previously considered. Accordingly, students may be in any field of study, and employers are encouraged to recruit students from under-represented groups.Grant Value:50% of the wages to a maximum of $5,000 for regular participants70% of the wages to a maximum of $7,000 for under-represented groups including women in STEM, Indigenous students, newcomers, persons with disabilities, visible minority as well as first-year studentsTurnaround Time: 2 weeks Eligible Employers:Registered Canadian business and not-for-profits in the agriculture industry, including:Primary growers;Industry associations;Research units;AgriTech firms;Agriculture start-ups;Veterinary clinics servicing farm animals/ livestockHorticulture; andAquaculture.Farm equipment dealerships;Input dealers;Agriculture-focused media agencies.Must be able to provide a quality learning experience to the student;Must have the capacity to pay the student for the duration of the placement, as the subsidy is administered at the end of the placement, after the final pay stub has been received; andWhere legally required, responsible for Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) or alternate workplace insurance coverage; andEmployers can apply with or with or without a candidate. Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal governments;Non-secular institutions;Post-secondary institutions;Federal and provincial Crown corporations; andNon-agricultural employers.Eligible Candidates: Must be enrolled in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution (undergraduate or graduate); Could be from agriculture and non-agriculture background;Undertaking a Work-Integrated Learning component by the student’s institution in connection with a course, degree, certificate, diploma, or other recognized program offered by the institution.Must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or refugee;Must be legally entitled to work in Canada; andMust have the placement recognized as a Work Integrated Learning component in connection with a course, degree, certificate, diploma, or program at their institution.Ineligible CandidatesInternational students;High school students;Students starting university/college the same semester.Students must have attended school the semester prior to the placement and must continue their studies in the same semester as the placement.Placement Details: Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between:Winter 2026 - January 1, to April 30: OPENSummer 2025 - May 1, to August 31 : CLOSEDFall 2025 - September 1, to December 31: CLOSEDCan be full- or part-time;Note: The program typically does not fund consecutive semesters if the placement stretches across multiple semesters.Can be a co-op, internship, field placement, or applied project;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.There is no limit on the number of placements an employer can apply for so long as the net new requirement is met.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:The program allows retroactive to May 1, 2025 for the Summer 2025 intake, if the candidate started before May 1, they may still be eligible for funding;This program can be stacked with provincial, territorial, and municipal government funds, provided these funds and the SWPP combined do not exceed 100% of the student's wages;This program cannot be stacked with other federal programs (ie: Canada Summer Jobs, Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy, etc.).Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Alberta-DT program supports digital SMEs by providing up to $50,000 to fund projects that enable businesses to build traction through customer acquisition, activation, retention, referral, and ultimately revenue. The aim of this program is to accelerate the growth of digital firms that rely on software development for their product or service offerings, in order to generate economic and social impact for Alberta.Grant Value: 50% up to $50,000Turnaround Time: 6 to 8 weeksEligible Applicants:Be a for-profit 'digital SME';An SME that relies on software development for 1 or more of its products and/or services and intends to rapidly scale in the global marketplace.Have fewer than 50 full-time employees;Have less than $1M annual reoccurring revenue;Have a founding team larger than 1;Demonstrate previous investment into the company by the founding team;Be an Alberta-based company:Physical and corporate operational presence in Alberta;Albertan ownership and incorporation;May otherwise be incorporated federally or in another jurisdiction AND extra-provincially registered in Alberta; ORBe a General Partnership, Limited Partnership, or Limited Liability Partnership AND registered in Alberta.Intent that operational benefits will flow primarily within the province.Have up-to-date corporate filings;Have not previously received Digital Traction funding;Be in good financial standing with Alberta Innovates and its subsidiaries InnoTech Alberta and C-Fer Technologies.Note: Applicants cannot concurrently receive funding from other Alberta Innovates Programs.Eligible Activities:Customer and/or client discovery;Digital market assessment and segmentation analysis;Data-driven, online market assessment testing;Product development based on client feedback;Advanced market assessment or segmentation analysis; andAdvanced sales and/or marketing strategies.Eligible Expenses:Costs incurred after the signing of the Investment Agreement;Costs incurred between arm's length entities (with no existing relationships);Wages and salaries for individuals working directly on the project:Up to $50/hour for T4 or contract employees; andUp to 50% of total funding for founder's salary costs (must have 15% equity in applicant company).Costs of materials;Acquisitions of software or information databases (prorated over the duration of project);Advertising costs for data-based marketing strategies for customer discovery purposes; Cost of sub-contractors at fair market rates;Additional direct operating costs beyond labour and materials; andAny other cost which Alberta Innovates pre-approves in writing.Program Details:The project must be completed within 1 year;The project start date should be at least 45 days from the application submission date;Businesses must provide a minimum 25% cash contribution; The project must outline 3 defined business milestones to be reached during the project to measure progress;Have the first milestone activities identified to a maximum of $15,000 (includes payment upon execution of agreement, up to $10,000);Individual milestones cannot exceed $20,000 to a maximum of $50,000 for all 3 milestones; Project milestones are based on business outcomes, with activities required to reach those milestones; TDAs will monitor the progress of the project and provide coaching to the business; Milestone activities are flexible and may be adjusted as the project progresses;An advance payment of up to $10,000 will be released once the Investment Agreement is signed by both parties; Further funding is disbursed at the completion of each milestone; andAnnual reporting to the program will be required for 5 years following project completion.The Ideal applicant will have:a minimum viable product (MVP) to test with customers;a minimum TRL 4 and at the Validating stage of development;not previously received Digital Traction funding;performed preliminary customer discovery work to inform the development;a digital technology employed in an innovative way and/or with proprietary features to allow for a competitive advantage over existing solutions;a digital technology that could scale up in one to two years, if successful;no significant capital or regulatory barriers, not addressed by the project, that may be better addressed by other funding resources;completed a lean canvas, business model canvas, or similar tools to demonstrate anunderstanding of the problem to be solved and the customer profile; anda traction roadmap or similar tool to demonstrate customer acquisition targets for the next three years and what is required to get to those targets.Note: If the application is rejected two times for an Alberta Innovates funding program, the applicant can no longer be eligible to apply for funding for that project/technology.

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program provides up to $15,000 for businesses in Alberta seeking new export opportunities in foreign markets. Applicants must be legal entities that have a minimum annual revenue of $250,000 and have between 1 and 499 full-time employees in Alberta. Applicants are to present an adequate market entry plan. Grant Value:For-profit applicants: 50% of eligible costs - $1,000 to $15,000 per year.Turnaround Time: 25 business days - applications must be received within two months after the first day of formal event participation.Eligible Applicants:Be one of the following organization types:For-profit SMEs, non-profits, municipalities, industry associations, tertiary education institutions, technical institutes, Indigenous communities, and economic development organizations operating in Alberta.For-profit organizations must:Be an incorporated legal entity in Alberta;Be operating and have a permanent establishment in Alberta;Present an adequate market entry plan; Must have at least 1 full-time employee and fewer than 500 full-time equivalent employees;Must have annual revenues of $250,000 - $25,000,000.Emerging technology companies may be eligible at a lower annual gross
sales amount of $50,000,This requirement may be waived for start-up companies with emerging technologies but will be determined on a case-by-case basis.Eligible Activities:Registration fees for participation at select tradeshows and/or events in the target marketFor International trades event, base entry registration fee may be reimbursed up to 50% up to a max of $1,000;Accommodation;International business travel;There is a maximum of two travelers who must be Alberta-based employees of the applicant organization:The organization’s first traveler will receive a $400 CAD per diem for the eligible days;The organization’s second traveler will receive a $200 CAD per diem for the eligible days.Translation of marketing materials.Note: Maximum of 2 employees per activity. Travelers must also be Alberta based.Ineligible Activities:International travel focused on investment, recreational and/or educational purposes;Projects that do not have a product or service to market;Travel for business meetings alone (without attending a formal trade event);Days involving business meetings only;Pre-commercial projects seeking research collaborations, proof of concept or demonstration partners;Trade show booth costs;Personal travel;Brokerage services;Ongoing operational activities or activities that are considered core to the applicant's business and not specific to
pursuing export opportunities in a new target market;Travel related to acquisitions or mergers;Travel and trade events taking place in Canada;Travel to countries with sanctions imposed by Canada; orTravel and trade events relating to expanding sales within international markets where a for-profit organization
already has a well-established presence (more than $150,000 CAD sale generated in target market and more than
15 per cent of the company’s total annual sales).Program Details:There is a maximum of two travelers who must be Alberta-based employees of the applicant organization:The organization’s first traveler will receive a $400 CAD per diem for the eligible days;The organization’s second traveler will receive a $200 CAD per diem for the eligible days.There is no limit on the number of days eligible for per diems; however, total annual funding for eligible applicant
organizations is capped at $15,000 CAD;Multiple formal trade events can be
submitted in one application if they occurred as part of the same trip;however, if applicant organization returns to Canada
between formal events, separate applications must be submitted.Once applications are received, they are assessed on a first-come first-served basis.

      Grant Criteria 
      Alberta employers can receive up to $7,500 to hire youth aged 15-24 for full-time or part-time positions. This wage subsidy covers 50% of wages for up to 6 months, helping businesses expand their workforce while providing employment opportunities for young Albertans.Grant Value: $7,500. $4,000 for 1-2 youth (minimum combined 400 hours total)$7,500 for 3-5 youth (minimum combined 750 hours total)Turnaround Time: 4–6 weeks. Eligible Employers:Registered for-profit businesses operational in Alberta for at least one year;Registered non-profit organizations; First Nations or Métis settlements; andOperational in Alberta for at least one year.Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial, or municipal governments;Public sector organizations (hospitals, health authorities, schools, post-secondary institutions);Provincial or federal crown corporations;Political parties; andholding companies whose main purpose is asset ownership. Eligible Candidates:Be 15–24 years old at the start of employment;Be a Canadian citizen or permanent resident;Be an Alberta resident and work in Alberta; andNot have worked with the same employer and in the same position prior to application.Note: Cannot be the business owner, board member, immediate family of the employer, or temporary foreign worker. Eligible Expenses:Wages and salaries;Employee training costs;Other costs directly related to employing youth. Program Details:Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis;Employers must submit an online application with business registration proof and position details;Businesses with multiple locations may submit one application per site, up to 10 sites;Candidates must be hired only after the employer’s application has been submitted and reviewed for eligibility;After employer approval, youth candidate details must be submitted (name, birthdate, email);CAREERS confirms candidate eligibility within 1–3 business days;Employer approval is typically issued within 4–6 weeks; andCandidates must be paid at or above Alberta minimum wage and employment must follow Alberta labour standards;Full-time, part-time, and seasonal roles may qualify. These positions are not eligible if they:Receive another wage subsidy or incentive;Are registered apprenticeship positions; andAre Co-Op positions delivered through CAREERS. Funding requires meeting minimum combined hours:400 hours for 1–2 youth;750 hours for 3–5 youth.Only hours worked after eligibility approval count;Partial payments are not available if minimum hours are not reached;If a candidate quits or is terminated, employers must still meet the required hours;Remaining hours may be completed by:Another eligible youth already on the application, orA newly hired eligible youth.After the minimum hours are completed, employers must submit a single claim that includes:Hours declaration;Pay stubs;Employer survey; andSkills assessment for youth who worked 200+ hours. Successful applicants may receive a Government of Alberta digital Work Readiness Badge. Payment is issued as a one-time EFT transfer; andAll hours must be completed and declared by September 30, 2027.

andWorking with public entities that provide access to capital and financing.Diverse and Skilled Talent Pools- activities in this area include: Recruitment campaign to repatriate Canadian talent to the Global Innovation Cluster;Development of curricula linked to industry needs and workforce integration programs for students;Development and promotion of specialized certifications in areas of technology leadership;Retraining programs for existing workforce;Assessment of Industry's workforce current or anticipated needs; andBuilding awareness of industry demand for skilled talent across stakeholder groups.Access to Innovation- activities in this are include: Support for access to specialized technical services;Installation of and access to dedicated laboratory or cutting-edge equipment; andAcquisition and assertion of jointly held intellectual property. Global Advantage- activities in this area include: Global Innovation Cluster promotion;Investment attraction to the general region of Global Innovation Cluster;Studies to identify new global markets for Global Innovation Cluster products and services;Participation in or leadership of trade missions to key markets;Development of regulatory or policy proposals to enhance technological advantage; andDevelopment and promotion of new international standards that incorporate the Canadian approach. Program Details: There are 3 streams under this program, the Project Stream, the System Stream and the Community Stream; Project Stream: This stream is designed to help individuals companies within the plant-based food, feed and ingredient ecosystem incorporate AI as a core business function;This requires collaboration with one or more entities within the AI ecosystem.Example of a project within this stream is a food manufacturer that wants to employ AI in the form of imaging technology and process automation for food safety and/or quality assurance.System Stream: This stream will focus on overall sector competitiveness and will require multiple partners from the plant-based food, feed and ingredient ecosystem; andAn example of a project within this stream is a consortium of plant-based food companies that are looking to iterate new products faster and improve consumer acceptance.Community Stream: This stream will help ensure that benefits of AI application in the plant-based food space are achieving societal benefits. This stream will focus on the nexus between plant-based foods and human health, as well as between plant-based foods environmental health; andAn example of a project in this stream could be a collaboration between national health advocacy agencies along with a number of plant-based food companies to use AI to design food products that help achieve certain health outcomes or to address health concerns.Protein Industries Canada will require all project participants to report on the IP assets generated by
their project, which may include patents, trade secrets, trademarks, copyright, data sets and other
types of intangible assets.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This program does not allow for funding to be used retroactively;All projects are required to pay a project administration fee to Protein Industries Canada. This fees will be 4% of the total eligible reconciled project cost; and This program can be stacked with other sources of funding. Forms and Links: Program Webpage: click here.Program Guidelines: click here.

      Grant Criteria

andProjects must benefit Northern Ontario (economic benefits accrue primarily in the region)Note: Retail/wholesale, construction, tourism, and service-based businesses are not eligible under this program.Eligible Activities: Activities that support increased capacity and competitiveness of Northern Ontario SMEs.Eligible Costs:Labour costs (wages and benefits);Machinery, equipment, and training fees;Leasehold improvements;Professional/advisory/technical services; andMarketing costs (design, promotional materials, trade shows) when part of larger project.Ineligible Costs:Regular maintenance and ongoing operations;Scheduled capital expenditures/asset replacement;Refinancing existing debt;Land and building acquisition; andCosts incurred before eligibility date. Program Details:The BGC program foster economic growth and competitiveness of Northern Ontario businesses through investments that support:Access to capital;Modernization of operations and management;Trade, exports, and new market access.Applicants must demonstrate : Sustainable business model (normally 2+ years of operations); andFinancial capacity to complete project and repay contribution.Benefits must accrue to Northern Ontario;The program requires applicant contributions toward total project costs;Funding repayment begins no later than 1 year after project completion;Applications are made through the client portal after discussing the project with one of FedNor Officers. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligibility Best Practices:Must demonstrate clear benefit to Northern Ontario’s economy (job creation, diversification, innovation, increased competitiveness);Quantify impacts where possible (e.g., jobs created/maintained, increased revenues, productivity gains);Activities must directly support business growth, productivity, or competitiveness; andBusinesses must align with priority sectors such as manufacturing, value-added industries, clean technology, bioeconomy, forestry, mining supply, and agri-food.Process Best Practices:Limited budget availability due to high demand, applicants must contact FedNor officers before applying; andProvide complete and up-to-date financial documentation. Forms: Program website: click hereApplication Portal: click here

and Must be transferrable/universal skills learned.For under 25 participants or under must apply through service provider in respective area; andFor over 25 participants must apply directly through the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities.Ineligible Training: Training that the employer legally has to provide itself;Executive training courses (MBA, CFA);Preparatory training courses (LSAT, MCAT, GMAT);Business Consulting services; Apprenticeship training; andTraining that displaces existing staff or replaces staff currently on lay-off.Note: The employer may deem many applications of over $25,000 ineligible depending on funding availability.Eligible Expenses:Tuition fees or fees charged by the training provider;Mandatory student fees;Textbooks, software, and other required materials;Equipment, clothing, tools;Examination fees; andTravel costs up to $500 (if the participant is traveling at least 24km each way).Eligible Training Provider:If the selected training is through a private trainer, then the training provider must meet the following requirements:Must have been in business and conducting training for at least 2 years at the time of application submission;Declare any conflict of interest between the employer, training participants and/or product vendor;Within the preceding 10 years, experience working in a profession relevant to the training being provided with:48 months of experience or teaching a program to prepare a student for the field (or a combination of the two); ORAt least 24 months of experience with one of the following qualifications:A Canadian bachelor’s degree (or equivalent foreign degree)A certificate of qualification issued under the Ontario College of Trades and Apprenticeship Act, 2009Status as a graduate of a college of applied arts and technology or registered private career college (or equivalent institution outside Ontario)Third-party regulatory requirements (if applicable)Program Details:Applications for 25 participants or under can apply through service providers; ORApplications for over 25 participants must apply directly through the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities (See Forms below).Applications are assessed by priority measured by these three tiers:1. Training results in a new or higher position and this is the employer's first successful application in the last 6 months;2. Training results in a new or higher position but this is not the employer's first successful application in the last 6 months OR training does not result in a new or higher position;3. Training per trainee is below $500 and lasts no longer than 1 week OR the training is required due to legislation, regulation or policy.

      Best Practices & Forms

      Regions
      All of Canada
    
    
      Industries
      Agriculture - Crop, Agriculture - Dairy, Agriculture - Livestock, Agriculture - Tree Fruit

          Open until filled
      
    
    
  





    
      




  

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canadian Agricultural Loans Act program guarantees loans of up $500,000 to farmers and agricultural co-operatives. The program is intended for direct producers in the agriculture sector that are seeking to purchase the purchase, repair, construction of buildings and machines. The purchase of tools, machines, and breeding livestock is also eligible under this program.Loan Value:Up to $500,000 for the purchase of land and the construction or improvement of buildingsUp to $350,000 for all other loan purposes, including consolidation/refinancingNote: maximum of lender's prime rate plus 1%Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Applicants:Must engage in one of the following:The production of field-grown crops, cultivated and uncultivated, and horticultural crops;The raising of livestock, poultry, and fur-bearing animals;The production of eggs, milk, honey, maple syrup, tobacco, fibre, wood from woodlots, and fodder crops;The production or raising of any other prescribed thing or animal.Must be one of the following organization types:Sole proprietors;Partnerships;Corporations; andCo-operative association.Must have a majority (50% + 1) farmer membership.The program allows farmers of all types to be eligible, including:Existing farmers;Beginning farmers (that is, less than 6 years of farming);Start-up farmers;Farmers taking over the family farm; andPart-time farmers.Note: Greenhouses are eligible under the programEligible Lenders:Chartered banks;Credit unions;Caisses populaires;Alberta Treasury Branches; andAny other organization designated by the Minister.Eligible Activities:Purchase of land;Construction, repair or alteration of any building or structure on a farm;Purchase, installation, alteration, major overhaul, or major repair to/of:Tools, implements, apparatus, and machines of any kind not usually affixed to real or immovable property;Machinery and apparatus for the generation or distribution of electricity, whether or not affixed to real or immovable property.Purchase of breeding livestock that will provide a long-term improvement to a farm operation including:Horses and other equinesCattle, sheep, goats, and other ruminants;Swine, poultry, bees, and fur-bearing animals;Any other prescribed animal.Erection or construction of fencing or works for drainage;Clearing, breaking, irrigating and reclaiming of land;Conservation of soil, prevention of soil erosion by the planting of trees and shelter belts;Repair or overhaul of fencing where the cost is $2,000 or more;Purchase and the planting of trees for syrup production and the purchase and planting of fruit trees, Christmas trees, and ginseng, where the cost is $2,000 or more;Construction of a road or driveway on a farm;Land transfer tax, survey, appraisal and legal costs relating to the purchase of additional land;Purchase of shares for inter-generational farm transfers; andConsolidation/refinancing of loans.Note: A loan for the purchase of shares in a farm or farming operation can be financed under the program for up to $350,000.  These loans can be amortized for up to 10 years.Ineligible Activities:Improvements to the family dwelling;Quota purchases of any kind;Operating loans and loans for the purchase of short-term feeder livestock; andConsolidation of a lender's ordinary loans.Program Details:Eligible amount of the loan:Existing farmers - Loans to existing farmers must not exceed the lesser of 80% of the appraised value of the property for which the loan was madeBeginning farmers - Loans to beginning farmers must not exceed the lesser of 90% of the appraised value of the property for which the loan was made.Application process:Approach an eligible lender as listed above;The lender will go through its loan application process and determine the financing best suited for the applicant;The lender may then register the loan with the CALA program through either the online loan registration system or by mailing the forms and registration fee in.Registration fee:0.85% of the amount of the loan;This fee must be submitted to the "Receiver General for Canada" at the time of loan registration.Administration fee:An administration fee may also be charged by the lender. For loans up to $250,000, the administration fee is capped at 0.25% of the amount of the loan (to a maximum of $250). For loans over $250,000, the administration fee is capped at 0.1% of the amount of the loan.Repayment terms:15 years for land purchases. Lenders may amortize loans for longer than 15 years provided a balloon payment is scheduled for the loan at the end of the 15 year period. The remaining loan amount could then be refinanced under the Canadian Agricultural Loans Act (CALA) for a further 10 years.10 years for all other purposes.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:The lender organization will go through the loan application process and determine the financing best suited for the applicant's needs, which may or may not include a loan under the Canadian Agricultural Loans Act program.Forms:Program webpage: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Canadian Agricultural Strategic Priorities Program (CASPP) provides funding of up to 75% of eligible expenses up to $1,000,000. Typically only non-profit organizations and Indigenous groups are eligible for the program. However, if for-profit organizations are able to deliver significant benefits to the sector or the public good, they may also be considered for funding. The program's strategic priorities include adopting or commercializing new technology,  advancing environmental sustainability, sector capacity building, and addressing emerging sector-wide issues. The intent of the program is to help the Canadian agricultural sector remain competitive.Grant Value: 50%-75% of eligible expenses up to $1,000,000Note: The program may normally contribute 50% of eligible project costs, but may contribute up to 75% if the project is a high priority for the agricultural sector or for the Canadian public.Turnaround Time: within 100 business days from the date of submissionEligible Applicants:Be either: Non-profit organizations and associations, cooperatives, and marketing boards;Indigenous groups.Be legal entities that can enter into legally binding agreements; andHave relevant projects that are Canadian or sector-wide in scope.Note: For-profit organizations are normally ineligible, but if the project delivers significant benefits to the sector or the public good, they may also be considered for funding.Eligible Activities:Adaptation to new technology:Coordinated approaches to adapt and take full advantage of emerging opportunties;;Test and adopt technology solutions in collaboration with research centres;Solving technical hurdles to overcome barriers to the adoption of new technology in Canadian agriculture;Develop more value-added products.Environmental sustainability:Support the development of environmental initiatives, increase resilency, and projects adopting or demonstrating environmental technology; Complement environmental sustainability and climate change activities under the sustainable Canadian agricultural partnership and other programs.Strategic development and capacity building:Support organizational capacity;Support transformation in the agricultural sector;Develop strategic planning initiatives that complement value chain roundtable, agri-food economic table and other discussions.Addressing emerging issues:Program is available to support the agricultural sector in responding to unforeseen circumstances that require identification and planning for future changes expected in the sector.Eligible Expenses:Administrative CostsOngoing or core activities and overhead expenses (fundamental operational activities) will be calculated at a flat rate of 10% of total project costs.Capital assets with a per-item cost of more than $100,000 will not be included in the calculation of administrative costs.Salaries and benefits;Only the wages and benefits of staff directly related to the project are eligible.Contracted services;Professional or specialized services for which a contract is entered into, such as inspection, consultant/expert services, installation, and Canadian Environmental Assessment Act 2012.Travel costs;Costs directly related to the project, such as: per diems (accommodations, meals, taxis, and incidentals); air, rail and ground transportation (to an out-of-city destination).Capital assets;Costs that are tangible assets that are purchased, constructed, developed, or otherwise required to complete the project;Expenditures for capital assets should not exceed 25% of total project costs.Other direct project costs.Costs that are for project-related deliverables, such as shipping, translation, marketing costs related to the production of materials/documents/knowledge transfer, and other costs that AAFC deems eligible.Note: All costs must be incurred after the Contribution Agreement is signed. A complete breakdown of Eligible expenses can be found hereProgram Details:Applicants may submit and receive funding for more than 1 project;Maximum funding cannot exceed $5 million over 5 years per applicant;The application process is comprised of 2 stages:Stage 1: Pre-screeningMust download and submit CASPP pre-screening summary;Only successful applicants will be invited to Stage 2.Stage 2: Full applicationIf the program requests additional information, applicants must submit the required documents/information within 30 days of the request.Advances in funding may be made available based on the program's assessment of the project risk;Applications must show how the activities support a competitve and market-oriented agriculture, agri-food and agri-based products sector that proactively manages ricks through: Supporting sustainable growth, adaption and sector prosperity; andSupporting the sector to be more innovative, safer and stronger.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Funding from this program may be used in conjunction with other sources of grant funding (Federal, Provincial, municipal, and other sources) so long as combined funding does not exceed 85% of eligible project expenses;This program does not allow funding to be used for costs incurred prior to the signing of the Contribution Agreement; andFor more information on eligible and ineligible costs, please see the Annex B section.Forms:Program webpage: click hereOnline portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The CanExport – Innovation (CXI) program offers funding to researchers from Canadian small and medium-sized businesses, universities and NGOs who aim to commercialize their technology abroad. The program assists companies pursuing international collaboration (e.g. for the purposes of R&D) and seeking to establish key partnerships in foreign markets.Grant value: 75% of eligible costs ($50,000) to a maximum of $37,500.Turnaround Time: Within 60 business daysEligible Applicants:Organizations can either be:  Small or Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs)  ORAcademic institutions OR;Non-government research centers.Have Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business number;Have existing prototype;Own the intellectual property for their technology or product;Technology must be at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 4 or higher;Technology intended to be commercialized within 5 years;Have clear benefit to Canadian economy should proposed project be successful;Must have financial and HR capacity to carry out proposed activities and cover their share of costs;Must not receive more than 75% government assistance for the same activities;Returning applicants must have demonstrated a good track record of progress reporting and effective use of CanExport Innovation funding.Note: The applicant eligibility will be part of the assessment criteria. Please ensure all the criteria are met.Eligible Activities:Activities in pursuit of key strategic partnerships with foreign organizations and individuals, with the overarching aim of commercializing technology:Partnerships should have the following objectives:Securing investments from foreign partners for R&D work;Licensing or purchasing the Intellectual Property of foreign partner's technology;Negotiating R&D collaborations that will lead to development, adaptation or validation of applicant's technology.Technology development or enhancement work with foreign partner, including:Working with the foreign partner to conduct a pilot of the applicant's technology:Working with the foreign partner to conduct clinical trials using the applicant's technology;Leveraging the technical expertise and/or technology of the foreign partner to test the applicant's technology.Technology validation:Pilot application and clinical trials.Virtual meetings;Pre-identified in-person meetings;Seeking expert legal business advice from consultants;For the purposes of:New certification requirements (only for countries where there is a pre-identified partner);Navigating foreign market legal framework;Pursuing IP protection;Due diligence on foreign partner and its technology;Drafting/ reviewing legal agreements;Identifying potential foreign partners;Market research; andInternational expansion roadmap.Development of professional promotion plans or materials for meetings with potential partners;Applying for intellectual property (IP) protection in the country of the foreign partners;Shipping applicant's technology for assessmentIneligible Activities:All activities after partnership formalization;Any services requiring payments to/from foreign partners;R&D activities;Customizing the technology to client's needs;Activities for sales and distribution purposes;Manufacturing;Client acquisition; andLobbying.Eligible Expenses:Consultant and legal fees (previously capped at $4,000); Foreign regulation certification fees;Only eligible in countries where the applicant has a pre-identified partner.Intellectual property protection fees;Development and printing of promotional materials;Translation or interpretation services (maximum cost: $2,000); Shipping costs (maximum cost: $4,000); Eligible travel expenses;Approval will be assessed based on:Duration - maximum of 5 days per travel destination;Number of participants - maximum of 2 travelers per trip;Costs (high costs may impact approval).Per diem (ie. accommodation & meals);Capped at $400 per approved travelerSingle entry visas; andRegistration fees for virtual/in-person events; andCost of video conferencing platform (only covered during the months in which meetings with the project partners are scheduled to take place).  Note: The program only supports travel activities that comply with the Government of Canada's travel advisories.Ineligible Expenses:Expenses incurred prior to application submission;Any travel expenses that are inconsistent with Canada's official travel advisories;Airfare costs paid with bonus points from programs such as Air Miles/Aeroplan/World Points or any other barter systems;Capital costs and office supplies;Cell phone charges;Passport costs;Costs of hospitality, entertainment, and gifts;Core activities and overhead expenses;Salaries and commissions;Goods and Services Tax; Event registration that includes booth fees; Events where meetings and pre-identified foreign partners have not been confirmed; andRental and/or installation of a booth for a conference or exhibition.Note: Please see guidelines for a full list of eligible and ineligible expenses. The list above is a selection of most common expenses.Program Details:If a project is approved, the start date of the funding agreement (the date that expenses are eligible) will be the application submission date;The program does not reimburse expenses incurred prior to a project’s start date.A project must focus on only 1 technology per project application;A project can target multiple partners to achieve multiple R&D objectives;Assessment criteria:Applicant eligibility;Technology readiness (TRL 4 and above - beyond ideation stage and into initial prototype creation) and ownership;The methodology used for pursuing partnership;Selection of foreign partners.Must demonstrate:Appropriate skillsExpertiseTechnology compatibility;Ability to make technical contributions.Successful applicants will receive a funding agreement by email, and must sign the agreement within 20 business days. Failure to do so may result in the forfeiture of the funds; Funding recipients must submit a final report no later than 7 days after the completion of the project; andThough all decisions made by CanExport are final and non-negotiable, however, revised applications may be resubmitted.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Applicants must clearly indicate all sources of government funding (federal, provincial/territorial, and municipal) they have received in the form of grants and non-repayable contributions, Canadian government assistance must not exceed 75%;This program is not to cover R&D expenses, those will be incurred after the agreement is signed, so don’t include those expenses in your application;Your product should be IP protected and ownership of the IP should be the applicant of this program; This program is not meant to fund sales, distribution, or manufacturing agreements. Any of these types of activities will be rejected.Process Best Practices:CanEx Innovate is a competitive program with limited funding, so the quality of the application is extremely important. Applications should tell the full story of the organization's plans for pursuing foreign R&D partnerships/investments. Forms and Links:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here
