        February 4, 2026The CanExport SME program is now open (Feb 4 – May 29, 2026),  early application is recommended.Projects must begin on or after April 1, 2026.Decisions usually take 60 business days (90 days for most U.S. projects).Agriculture, food, alcohol, and seafood companies are no longer eligible.Ag tech and food tech companies remain eligible.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      The CanExport SME program provides a subsidy to businesses of 50% up to $50,000 per project in matching contributions to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Canada seeking to develop new export opportunities and markets. This program requires a minimum annual revenue of $300,000 as shown on a business's corporate tax return. The intent of the program is to help Canadian companies prepare for and establish a presence in the international markets.Grant Value: 50% of eligible costs for $10,000 to $50,000 in funding per project. Turnaround Time: Committed to providing a decision within 60 business days.Timelines: Projects must fall within the fiscal year (April 1 to March 31).Eligible Applicants:Must be for-profit, legally incorporated in Canada (company, LLP, or cooperative);3 to 500 full-time equivalent (FTE) employees; Have an active Canada Revenue Agency business number (not dissolved or amalgamated); Annual Revenue in Canafa of $300,000 to $100 million CAD in the last complete tax reporting year; andMust show meaningful economic ties to Canada (product/service origin or value-added activities in Canada); andOnly one active CanExport SMEs project per company at any time. Companies may have active projects with other CanExport programs. Notes: Sole proprietorships, limited partnerships, franchisees (except franchisor), third-party representatives, trading houses, distributors, wholesalers, and export brokers (except agriculture/agri-food) are ineligible to apply. Eligible Target Markets:Up to 5 markets can be targeted within the same project; andMust be a non-sanctioned country and account for the following during the company's last complete GST tax reporting year (or last 12 months for quarterly or monthly filers):Less than $100,000 in sales;  ORLess than 10% of total sales; ANDIf your project includes multiple markets, total sales across all target markets/regions are less than 10% of your company’s total sales (aggregate).Projects targeting the U.S. only cannot include other markets (and vice-versa);2026-27 Priority is to emphasize non-U.S. market expansion and support Canada's trade diversification goals.Eligible Activities:Category A: International travelTravel to meet key contacts or attend trade events in target markets (up to 90 days total per project, max 30 consecutive days per trip);Maximum 2 travellers per trip; Canada-based employees only (age 18+).Category B: Participation in Trade events;In-person event attendance, booth/exhibitor fees, booth design/setup, shipping booth materials;Maximum 2 participants per event; demo products must be returned to Canada;Participation to trade events or conferences in Canada is NOT eligible.Category C: Marketing and translation;Creation or translation of promotional materials (brochures, banners, posters, content writing), website adaptation, trade show graphics and videos for target marketsCannot be in-house activities.Category D: Interpretation services;Engaging an independent contractor to provide interpretation services.Category E: Contractual agreements, product registration, and diversity certification;Adaptation and translation of contractual agreements;Certification application fees;Fees related to product testing, inspection, and/or development are NOT eligible.Supplier diversity certification (backgrounds including women, Indigenous Peoples, visible minorities, members of the 2SLGBTQI+ community and youth).Category F: Consulting - business, tax, and legal adviceExpert advice on legal, tax, business matters, regulatory issues, and digital and e-commerce marketing.Category G: Consulting - market research, feasibility studies, identification of key contacts, B2BExport market research and feasibility studies for target market;Identification of key contact and facilitation of B2B meetings;Facilitation of B2B meeting programs and matchmaking;Feasibility studies for the target market.See eligibility requirements for consultants & contractors.Category H: Intellectual property (IP) protectionFiling patents or industrial design applications;Registration of trademark or copyright;IP professional services from consultants and/or legal firms.Including the development of an international IP strategy, database search, drafting of formal IP documentation, and filing of IP documentation.Ineligible Activities:      The list below is a selection of the most common ineligible expenses, for further details of ineligible expenses by category, refer to the application guidelines.                                                                                                           On-going core/operational activities including corporate overheads and capital costs  (i.e. rent);Salaries including those working outside of Canada;Product/service development expenses;Travel within Canada;Preparation of a business plan, marketing plan, public relations plan, or documentation needed to present a CanExport application; Entertainment & hospitality, event sponsorship, and membership fees;SEOs;Digital Marketing;Participation in a trade event or conference in Canada;Product/service development expenses;Any equipment that cannot be sold internationally in that target market must come back to Canada. It can be sold in target markets in Canada; and In-kind expenses.Eligible Expenses :Airfare (economy/premium economy, roundtrip from Canada);Per diem allowance ($600/day, max 90 days total per project);Ground transportation (taxis, public transit, car rental, parking, fuel);Trade event registration and booth costs;Interpretation services;Professional consulting and legal fees (business development, tax, legal, market research, IP);Visa/travel authority fees;Website adaptation for target market;Promotional material translation and creation; andShipping of trade show materials and demo products. Ineligible Expenses:Domestic travel or activities within Canada;Salaries, wages, commissions, or employee labor costs;Capital assets (computers, office equipment, real estate);GST/HST and refundable taxes;Overhead (warehousing, utilities, office rent);Travel costs for consultants, interpreters, or non-employees;Product development, manufacturing, or distribution costs;Advertising and online marketing (social media, SEO, sponsored content);Ongoing operational or "core" business activities;Preparation of application or claims;Activities outside approved project timeline;Note: full list of ineligible expenses is provided in the applicant's guide.Program Details:Applicants must submit budgets with a minimum of $20,000 to a maximum of $100,000;Funding amounts range from $10,000 to $50,000;In-kind contributions are not allowed. The program provides two types of funding:Contributions: Applicants pay all costs upfront and receive reimbursement only after submitting detailed invoices, proof of payment, and reports; andGrants: Applicants receive the full payment upfront after signing the agreement, requiring only a final results report instead of individual claims.A detailed cost breakdown is necessary for the budget section;An applicant can only have one active CanExport SMEs project at any given time but may apply multiple times contingent on the total funding received not exceeding $99,999 per fiscal year (April 1 to March 31 of the following calendar year);A company may have an active project with another CanExport program;Projects must align with the April 1 to March 31 fiscal year; all costs must be paid within that year, as funds cannot be carried over:Two-year projects are allowed only in rare timing-related cases (like paying for an event in Year 1 and attending in Year 2), provided the project period covers both years and costs are billed to the year they are paid; andMedical cannabis projects must prove they are for medical purposes and follow all federal regulations.

andInvestments to maintain operations (designated commercial territories only).Ineligible Activities:Projects with costs below the minimum threshold ($5,000 in designated areas or $15,000 in other zones);Day-to-day operational expenses not tied to the project; andProject-related salaries or fees (excluding operational payroll).Ineligible Expenses:Operational wages and ongoing overhead;Expenses incurred before application approval; and Non-strategic or routine business costs.Program Details:Minimum project cost: $5,000 (designated territories) or $15,000 (other eligible zones);Non-repayable contribution, one grant per establishment every 5 years;Total City of Québec funding capped at $500,000 over two years across all programs;Applications must be submitted before incurring expenses; remotely;Marketing activities include: photography, digital media, websites, bio writing, publicity,

      Grant Criteria 
      The program provides 60% of the youth’s salary to a maximum of $20,000 in wage subsidies. This will help the employer adopt a diverse and inclusive work culture while satisfying their need for skilled labor, and will also help the employee get into the labor market and increase their knowledge of the sector’s needs. The intent of the program is to facilitate the transition of youth facing barriers into the labour market.Grant Value: 60% of wages up to $20,000;Program may provide wrap around support of up to $2,500 for the following:Relocation costs;Transportation supports;Housing Assistance;  Accessibility accommodations; Additional training for job success; Counselling and mental health supports; Personal protective equipment;  Childcare; Legal supports;  Cultural competency training; Networking events; Mentoring; Virtual networking sessions for participants; and Onboarding tools for employers, including a diversity and inclusion HR policy template and ongoing monitoring to ensure program success. Turnaround Time: 10 business daysEligible Employers: Be in one of the following industries:Bio-health;Bio-energy;Bio-industrial; andAgri-biotech.Have the ability to train and provide meaningful career;Maintain an internal process for supervising and mentoring for the participant; Have the participants on payroll which includes Federal/Provincial tax deductions (CPP, EI, etc.); andEmployers must identify a candidate before applying but they must not have started working.Eligible Candidates:Be Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or persons who have been granted refugee status in Canada;Legally entitled to work in Canada according to the relevant provincial and Canadian legislation and regulation;Be aged 15-30;Be a new hire;Identifying as a youth facing barriers including the following but not limited to: Involuntary not in education, employment, training for at least 6 months;With disability;Indigenous;A recent immigrant and/or refugee;A visible minority;LGBTQ2+;Homeless or at risk of becoming homeless;Living in a low-income household;Residing in a rural or remote location;Living with family care responsibilities;Affected by substance use;Currently in, coming out of, or who have been involved in the justice system;In or aging out of care; andLiving with low levels of literacy and numeracy.Ineligible Candidates:Candidates that have started employment at the organization prior to application submission; andCandidates must not have an existing relationship with the employer (must be arm's length).Program Details: Minimum hours/week: 30 (full-time only);Minimum of 3 months placement duration;Have an internal supervisor for a project;The work environment  must be safe, respectful, inclusive, free of harassment, abuse, and discrimination, and is in compliance with all applicable laws;The job placement must meet one of the following requirements:The work experience offers skills development and training opportunities;The work experience is related to the interests and pursuits of youth;The work experience offers a salary that is above the minimum wage; and/orThe work experience offers opportunities for advancement.The program now also provides additional support such as:Internal job coaching;Relocation support, if required;Online training courses for essential skills and technical skills;Access to BioSkills Recognition Program upon completion of the Career Starter program.The Job Coach and the participant will develop a Formal Coaching Plan before the start of the placement; The Job Coach will provide quarterly reports tracking the progress of the participant; andReimbursement claims are made monthly along with progress reports.

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers a maximum of 70% wage subsidy of up to $7,000 to hire current post-secondary students in part-time or full-time studies. It is intended to provide post-secondary students with work experience and valuable skills to secure meaningful employment as well as increase productivity and competitiveness in the aviation and aerospace industry. Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5,000;70% of wages up to $7,000 for students in the following underrepresented groups:Women in STEM;Indigenous persons;Newcomers to Canada;Visible minorities; Persons with disabilities; andFirst-year students.Turnaround Time: 2 business daysEligible Employers:Be directly or indirectly involved in the aviation/aerospace industry;Ie. aviation/aerospace organization, supplier of goods and services for the aviation/aerospace industry.Have registered business number;Have WorkSafeBC or Workers’ Compensation Board registration;Have General Liability Insurance;Employer Liability Insurance of $2,000,000 minimum; andGeneral Liability Insurance of $2,000,000 minimum.Must have participants on payroll; Cannot be receiving other federal funding for the placement; andEmployers must apply with a candidate.Eligible Participants:Must be a current student enrolled (full-time or part-time) in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Proof of enrollment required.Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents or persons with refugee protection legally entitled to work in their placement province; andMust have a co-op, internship, or practicum as a part of their study plan during the placement term or recognized work-integrated learning in the next semester.Ineligible Participants:Immediate family members of CCAA or employer;Must not be a recipient of Employment Insurance; andApprentices.Placement Details:The position must support the aviation and aerospace industry;Full-time or part-time positions;12 hours/week minimum is encouraged;An 8-week placement minimum is encouraged;1 placement is considered to take place over 4 months;An 8-month contract can result in 2 placements for a student, and a 12-month contract may result in 3 placements.Employers can fund up to 5 participants per term;Work-integrated learning must be in the participant's study plan and span over the duration of the placement;Employers to have identified participants and confirmed placements for the application;All aviation and aerospace businesses and post-secondary institutions can be pre-approved if desired, even before the selection of one or more students, presuming student eligibility.Employers must provide a company description, including the business number, company website, and job description;Employers must develop a learning plan for the participant;Wage subsidies in this program are reimbursements following an agreed payment schedule;Advance payments are possible for small and medium-sized businesses and nonprofits if there are operational cash flow needs. Eligibility will be determined on a case-by-case basis; andSubsidies can be transferred via cheque or electronic funds transfer.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Circular Food Innovators Fund provides $5,000–$35,000 to help Toronto businesses launch or scale reuse systems that reduce single-use food packaging. Its goal is to advance practical, low-waste solutions in the city’s circular food economy.Grant Value:  75% of project costs up to $35,000 for Reuse Systems;100% of project costs up to $5,000 for Green Workforce. Turnaround Time:  Expected May 2026. Eligible Applicants: For-profit businesses (including B2B and B2C) with less than 99 full-time employees;Registered not-for-profit and charitable organizations (including BIAs and academic institutions working with a business);Applicants must:Provide relevant services:Food and beverage products for takeaway consumption (including food distributed by vendors at public markets and events);Food and beverage products for delivery (including catering services);Reuse system infrastructure for food businesses.Be located in Toronto (or commit that the funded project operates in Toronto);Past CFIF recipients can reapply if the new project is different from what they previously received funding for. Note: The full list of ineligible applicants is available on page 11 of the program guidelines.Eligible Projects: Projects that introduce or expand reuse systems (e.g., reusable food containers, dishware, collection systems);Projects must be market-ready (not just ideas or prototypes);Can include technology or infrastructure that supports reuse;Workforce projects must focus on training and skills development related to circular food systems; Early-stage ideas, prototypes, or research studies; andGreen Workforce Project activities should:Build skills or job pathways for Toronto’s circular food and reuse systems;Go beyond internal procedures or project-specific materials;Provide sector-wide training, learning opportunities, or shared resources; andDo not need to link directly to the CFIF Project but must strengthen the wider workforce.Ineligible Projects:Early-stage ideas, prototypes, or research studies;Projects promoting compostable/biodegradable single-use items;Consumer education campaigns or general outreach;Retail product reuse (e.g., refillable packaged goods);Political advocacy or partisan activities; andProjects already being funded through other City of Toronto programs.Note: The full list of ineligible projects is available on page 9 of the program guidelines.Eligible Activities:Eligible activities under the green workforce development  component:Training people in practical, environmentally friendly skills, tools, or systems;Hands-on learning or job training connected to reusable food and beverage systems; andActivities that help participants find jobs or build careers in the circular economy.Eligible Expenses:Direct project costs such as reusable containers, materials, and supplies;Software or subscription services used for the project;Staff time (up to 50% of the budget);Capital cost (Equipment or infrastructure) up to 50% of the budget;Marketing, overhead, volunteer transportation (each capped at 15%); andTraining costs for workforce projects (materials, trainers, curriculum, evaluation).Ineligible Expenses:Costs incurred before signing the funding agreement;Normal business operating expenses (utilities, rent, general overhead);Staff or consultants unrelated to the project;Waste disposal services (compost, recycling);Fundraising, sponsorships, debt payments, gifts, property purchases; andConferences or courses not tied directly to the project.Program Details: This program is part of Toronto's circular economy transformation and efforts to build a more circular food system;It supports the implementation or scaling of reuse systems and, optionally, workforce training for circular food skills: For-profit: Up to 75% of project costs covered; applicant must contribute at least 25% (cash or eligible in-kind);Not-for-profit: Up to 100% coverage (max $35,000);Green Workforce: Up to 100% coverage (max $5,000). Applications must be submitted through the online portal to be considered eligible;Applicants may submit only one application per funding round; if multiple are submitted, only the first one will be reviewed;Deadline: March 1, 2026 at 11:59 pm (EST).Applicants must complete and upload the Project Budget Template and Project Plan Template;Workforce project components must focus on training and skills development related to circular food systems;The City encourages applications from equity-deserving groups (women, visible minorities, Indigenous peoples, people with disabilities);Priority is given to projects proposed by organizations that have not previously received CFIF funding;City staff may contact applicants for clarifications during the evaluation stage;Applicants may revise a submitted application only with written email permission from the City, and the revised version must be submitted before the deadline; otherwise, the original application will be evaluated;Evaluation criteria for core projects : Program Alignment (20%);Project Impact (30%);Financial Feasibility (25%); Organizational Capacity (25%). Successful applicants are notified in May 2026;Recipients must sign a Fund Agreement before receiving funds (separate agreements for CFIF-only vs. combined CFIF + Green Workforce Project);Funding is disbursed in two installments:50% at project start (after signing the agreement);50% at project completion, following submission and approval of the final report and receipts.Application and project timeline :Applications open January 5 – March 1, 2026;The City notifies successful applicants in May 2026;Projects run from June 2026 to June 2027;Interim report due December 1, 2026; Final report due at project end (2027).

      Best Practices & Forms

      Grant Criteria

The funding is open to technology developers industry,  industrial associations, small and medium-sized enterprises, research and development (R&D) organizations, post-secondary institutions, municipalities, not-for-profit organizations,   government research labs, and individuals who are seeking funding to advance innovation-commercialization or knowledge generation.Grant Value: 25-50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $2 millionTurnaround Time: 3-6 months (depends on the project dollar size)Eligible Applicants:Be 1 of the following applicant types:Technology developers;Industry;Industrial associations;Small and medium-sized enterprises;Research and development (R&D) organizations;Post-secondary institutions;Municipalities;Not-for-profit organizations;Government research labs; andIndividuals.Not required to be based in Alberta;Must demonstrate a clear value proposition for the province; andBe in 1 of the 5 technology portfolios:Advanced hydrocarbons:Cleaner hydrocarbon production; andInnovative hydrocarbon products.Clean Technology:Renewable and alternative energy;Bioenergy; andCarbon capture, and utilization.Environmental innovation:Land and biodiversity; andWater innovation.Smart agriculture and food; andBioindustrial materials.Eligible Expenses:Labour;Materials;Capital assets and software;Travel;Sub-contractors; andOther.Note: full breakdown of eligible expenses can be found here.Program Details:The program prioritizes technology or knowledge development projects;Technology  solutions  can  originate  from  anywhere  globally  but  must  address  challenges  and  opportunities of importance to Alberta;Projects that will be researched, piloted, demonstrated, and/or implemented in Alberta with long term Alberta-based infrastructure/resources will be prioritized;Technology projects should demonstrate a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 3-7;All applicants are expected to provide a portion of the funding towards a project, which can include cash and in-kind contributions from project partners or other sources of funds;Funding made available through this Process is  provided to support the execution  of  projects  with  well-defined objectives, milestones, deliverables, and timelines;Regular project update meetings will be held with the applicant and the assigned Project Advisor to assess progress towards milestones.There are no restrictions on the number of applications that can be submitted by any applicant; andOnce projects are completed, Alberta Innovates continues to collect information from clients for up to 5-years to assess the economic, environmental, and social benefits realized for Albertans.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides support for the diversification and expansion of the northern BC economy. It subsidizes the costs of hiring a business consultant with the aim of boosting productivity, profitability, job creation and yielding incremental revenues. Grant Value: max. 50% of project costs up to $30,000Turnaround time: 1 weekEligible Applicants:For-profit or not-for-profit organizations;Non-profits are eligible only if the sole purpose of the organization is to create jobs and economic prosperity in their respective industry;Incorporated;Can be Community contribution companies,  First Nations development corporations, or First Nations businesses in eligible industries;Must be in one of the following sectors:Manufacturing;Transportation;Distribution;Resource processing;Innovation/technology;Industrial supply chain (services and suppliers);High tech; andTransportation.Must have less than 500 employees;Must be in operation with revenue (cannot be start-up);Must have less than $100M in annual revenue; andHave project minimum budget of $2,000.Ineligible Applicants:Start-ups without revenue; andMunicipalities, regional districts and First Nations bands.Eligible Expenses:Consulting fees in the following areas:Business planning, strategic planning and management;Business development feasibility studies (limited to 25% contribution up to $20,000);Export development, E-commerce platforms andInventory processes;HR management;Operations or efficiency consulting;Quality and safety management;Innovation consulting; andFinancial system improvement.Consultant travel costs (within Canada) directly associated with the project;Other costs directly associated with the project (approved on a case-by-case basis);Software development or web design;Staff training courses (delivered by a third-party); andPST.NOTE: All consultants must:Be located in Canada (unless able to demonstrate that the service is not available in Canada)Provide a detailed quote with the application (including a fixed fee, fixed timeline of <12 months, fixed deliverables).Ineligible Expenses:Printing costs directly associated with producing a final report and cost of obtaining research material directly related to the project;Costs incurred prior to approval from program advisor;Operational costs and staff wages;Management or staff travel costs;Consultant administration fees or management fees;Legal and accounting services;Engineering costs;Meeting costs (equipment rental, refreshments etc.);Purchases of equipment or tools;Project cost over-runs;In-kind labour or donated services/materials;GST; andFees for consultants outside of Canada unless it is demonstrated that the service is not available in Canada.Program Details:Projects must be no more than 12 months in duration (timelines must be indicated on quotes provided by consultant)Applicants will be required to submit annual reports for up to three years following project completionReports may include: Number of jobs createdAnnual revenuesAnnual operation costs

      Grant Criteria

The program aims to advance the careers of Indigenous artists in Canada.Grant value: up to $30,000Turnaround time: 12 weeksEligible Applicants:First Nations, Métis, and Inuit arts professionals;Aspiring First Nations, Métis, and Inuit artists working under the guidance of a professional artist;First Nations, Métis, and Inuit groups and/or cultural carriers;First Nations, Métis, and Inuit art and culture non-profits; andFirst Nations, Métis, and Intuit for-profit businesses in the arts and culture sector.Note: To apply for this grant, you must create a profile in the Canada Council for the Arts online portal. Your profile must be verified before you can apply for grants. Be sure to create your profile at least 30 days before submitting your grant application. Eligible Activities:Travel activities led by First Nations, Métis, or Inuit individuals, cultural carriers, or arts/culture professionals;Must be by invitation;The destination must be at least 100 km from the place of departure; andMust have one of the following purposes:Sharing artistic works or cultural knowledge;Participating in significant artistic or cultural events;Undertaking research activities;Building professional and artistic networks;Engaging in professional development opportunities;Developing regional, national, or international markets.Note: Touring is not an eligible activity for this program. Arts professionals who wish to tour should apply to the Arts Across Canada or Arts Abroad programs instead.Ineligible Activities:Artistic activities that are led by non-professionals (this does not apply to new and early career artists);Activities that are carried out to satisfy the course requirements of an educational institution;Activities that directly support the delivery of an educational program or course;Fundraising activities;Capital expenditures, unless explicitly eligible;Contests and competitions (including prizes and awards), except practices in:powwow;hip-hop and urban arts -       This federally funded program offers wage subsidies to employers in the cultural sector who wish to hire students for a work-integrated learning experience. The student may be in any field of study, and the work does not need to be artistic or cultural in nature, as long as the employer is in the arts and culture sector (for example, a cultural sector employer can hire a computer science student to build a website). The goals of the program are to support partnerships between post-secondary institutions and the arts and culture sector, and to help students develop work-ready skills that will aid their transition into the workforce.Grant Value:Regular participants: 50% of wages to a maximum of $5,000Underrepresented participants: 70% of wages up to a maximum of $7,000Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Employers:Canadian for-profit and not-for-profit employers in the cultural sector, including but not limited to the following sub-sectors:Digital media;Film and television;Performing arts;Music and sound recording;Visual arts and crafts;Writing and publishing; andHeritage.Employer can identify candidate before or after application. Note: Government institutions (federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal) are not eligible employers. Eligible Participants:Must be enrolled in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution (part-time or full-time, graduate or undergraduate); Must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or refugee;International students are NOT eligible;Must be legally entitled to work in Canada; andMust be added to the employer's payroll (not a contractor). Note: Employers are encouraged to prioritize students from under-represented groups, including Indigenous, Black, Persons of Colour, Persons with Disabilities, Official Language Minorities, Newcomers to Canada, and first-year students.Placement Details:There are no minimum or maximum placement lengths;Placements may be full-time or part-time;The placement must allow the student to apply their academic studies in a workplace setting;Remote work is permitted; andBoth the student and the employer must submit reports to the CHRC.

      Grant Criteria 
      The DÉPART program aims to help SMEs in driving economic recovery by providing access to funding and supporting initiatives such as feasibility studies, investment projects, and innovation activities. For feasibility studies, the program offers a non-repayable contribution covering up to 60% of eligible expenses. For other projects, the program offers a non-repayable contribution covering up to 50% of eligible expenses.Turnaround Time: Approximately 50 business days.Grant Value:Feasibility Study:60% between $15,000 and $150,000;Up to $25,000 annually for hiring a professional with a professional, technical, or undergraduate degree; and Up to $35,000 annually for hiring a professional with a graduate or postgraduate degree in the required field for project deployment.Other Projects:50% between $15,000 and $150,000Up to $25,000 annually for hiring a professional with a professional, technical, or undergraduate degree; and Up to $35,000 annually for hiring a professional with a graduate or postgraduate degree in the required field for project deployment.Eligible Applicants:For-profit small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) with 250 employees or fewer, legally constituted under the laws of Quebec or Canada, operating an active establishment in Quebec;Collective enterprises (cooperatives and non-profit organizations) as defined under the Social Economy Act with a primarily commercial activity;For‑profit businesses legally established under Quebec or Canadian law, with 250 employees or fewer;Operating within designated target areas for economic revitalization (specific territories identified by the program);Businesses in the following sectors:Manufacturing;Information and cultural industries (e.g., ICT, media);Accommodation;Tourism;Including accommodation enterprises that provide entertainment and leisure services and projects related to the development of cultural, scientific, recreational, outdoor, or other attractions for a regular tourist clientele with growth potentialWith the exception of tourist residences, bed and breakfasts, and campgroundsIneligible Applicants:Companies in the arts, entertainment, and recreation sector;Businesses in construction (except those tied to the Action Plan for the Construction Sector or productivity improvements);Retail and wholesale trade companies;Professional and financial services (including finance and insurance);Restaurants and food service businesses;Real estate, rental, and leasing companies; andPublic services, including health care, social assistance, education, and public administration;For the full list of eligible and ineligible applicants, click this link (french only).Eligible Projects:Feasibility studies;Investment projects including:Business creation, expansion, or modernization;Technological transition;Post‑acquisition investments;Development or demonstration of innovative products or processes.Technological adoption;Construction and renovation;Business buyouts;Innovation initiatives.Eligible Expenses:Professional fees for external consultants;Travel and accommodation for project implementation, per Quebec government guidelines;Salaries for hiring a new qualified professional in a relevant field, with required credentials; replacements not eligible;Acquisition, construction, development, or expansion of buildings;Purchase and installation of equipment or software for the project;Acquisition of new technology;R&D expenses for products or processes;Costs for approvals, compliance, or certifications;Expenses for real-world demonstrations to potential clients;Purchase of studies, data, or documentation needed for the project.Program Details:The project must be located in one of the targeted territories, such as specific MRCs (french only);The project must correspond to eligible sectors, including secondary/tertiary transformation of primary sector, manufacturing, value-added services (ICT, environmental services, industrial design), and tourism with cultural, scientific, or recreational components;Each business can receive a maximum of $300,000 in total funding.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Development and Commercialization Program supports the development and commercialization of Ontario made products and services that integrate/adopt Critical technologies by providing funding 50% up to $200,000. The program enables SMEs to access technology facilities an capabilities across the province to develop, test, validate and showcase their products and services.Grant Value: 50% of eligible costs to a minimum of $50,000 and a maximum of $200,000Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Applicants:SME with fewer than 500 global full-time employees;Must have registered operations in Ontario and a valid CRA business number;Has the intent and potential to apply, exploit and/or commercialize the results of the project for the economic benefit of Ontario;Has the necessary expertise and resources to put the project into effect within an appropriate time frame;Adoption of critical technologies is part of their long-term product roadmap;All applicants and partners must be in good financial and reporting standing with OCI; andApplicants who have received over $500,000 of funding from OCI-administered programs in their lifetime (excluding TalentEdge) are required to obtain OCI approval before a new application for funding is initiated.Eligible Partners:SME applicant companies may choose to apply in collaboration with a strategic partner
company. (Not mandatory, but preference will be given to SME applicants with strategic
partners involved in their project outcomes);A strategic partner could be a private industry partner and/or public sector organizations such
as but not limited to a municipality, a healthcare facility, or a public utility;The strategic partner company should represent a significant potential commercial
partner/strategic client for the proposed innovative product/service;The SME and strategic partner must have an arm’s-length business relationship; andStrategic Partner must agree to complete the required OCI report.Eligible Project:Projects must support Critical Technology integration, adoption, demonstration, prototyping,
testing by the SME;The solution should involve the acceleration, development, or integration of at least one of the six
Critical Technologies (5G and Advanced networks, AI, blockchain, robotics, cybersecurity and
quantum);Projects should result in the development of a new solution, product, or service with strong
commercial opportunities in one or more of the four Key Sectors.Eligible Expenses:Sub-contractor and consultant fees if approved by OCI management prior to
the start of the project and if procured in accordance with the Broader Public
Sector (BPS) Procurement Directive;Research and Development costs directly related to the project;Project-related computer hardware and software, including specialized
hardware and software;Cost of usage of equipment;Cost of direct materials, necessary for specifically identified activities and
measured as having been used for, the completion of the project;Materials used for prototypes, configuring, testing production processes,
systems, and training employees;Cost of upgrade of project-related equipment;Capital lease of equipment (interest costs are not eligible);Project-related leasehold improvement costs (prior OCI approval required);Sales and marketing costs attributed to the project;Training costs directly attributable to the project; andCost of regulatory compliance (up to a maximum specified by OCI).Program Details:Project activities are to be carried out in Ontario;Minimum 1:1 contribution match from the Applicant;Project length maximum 6 months;Projects must involve the utilization of at least of the Technology development sites for a minimum of 2 hours per test bed; Projects must be the basis for a highly competitive business and must offer a good
return on investment and benefits to Ontario (e.g., new revenues, job creation/retention,
new customers, follow-on investment, and productivity improvement); andProjects must already have all necessary certifications, if required for a project to be executed.

      Grant Criteria 
      These programs are offered by the Downtown Vancouver Business Improvement Association to support local street-level businesses in improving safety, appearance, outdoor spaces, and customer experiences. They provide small matching grants, with funding amounts varying between $2,000 and $3,000, to help businesses invest in upgrades and activations that strengthen downtown vibrancy and increase foot traffic.Grant Value: The funding amount varies by grant type:Beautification Fund: Up to $2,000Security Camera Fund: Up to $2,000Downtown Patio Fund: Up to $3,000Activation Fund: Up to $2,500Turanround Time: March 20, 2026.Eligible Applicants:Common requirement (all four programs):Must be a member of the Downtown Vancouver Business Improvement Association; andMust operate a street-level business in a commercial building located within the Downtown Van boundaries.Additionally:Patio Fund: Open to restaurants, cafés, bars, retailers, and cultural spaces with patios; andSecurity Camera Fund: Requires participation in a security best-practices workshop (Vancouver Police Department).Eligible Projects:Beautification FundExterior façade upgrades; andStorefront refresh (paint, finishes, signage, landscaping, window improvements).Security Camera FundPurchase and installation of new security cameras; andExpansion or upgrades to existing camera systems.Patio FundPatio construction or expansion;Weatherproofing, accessibility upgrades, sustainability improvements; andPatio repairs or design upgrades. Activation FundStorefront activations tied to major events; andThemed installations, workshops, performances, collaborations.Eligible Expenses:Beautification Fund:Window/door upgrades;Signage replacement;Exterior painting; andLandscaping and display improvements.Security Camera Fund:Purchase of cameras; andUpgrading or expanding existing camera systems, including installation and reinstallation costs. Patio Fund:Patio application and permit fees;Architectural design and drawing costs;Construction of a new patio or expansion of an existing patio;Patio furniture and design features;Weather protection elements, such as umbrellas, awnings, or heaters;Accessibility upgrades, including ramps and non-slip surfaces;Sustainable improvements, such as planters, solar lighting, and energy-efficient fixtures;Seasonal storage solutions; andRepairs and refurbishment of existing patio infrastructure. Business Activation Fund: Themed décor;Interactive installations;Workshops/tastings;Live performances; andMarketing tied to activations.Note: The above list is not exhaustive. Other improvements may be eligible if they align with the purpose of the programs. Ineligible Expenses:Payroll;Rent;Unrelated capital purchases;Regular operating expenses; andCosts incurred before approval. Program Details:The Downtown Van Association offers four funding programs:Business Beautification Fund: supports exterior storefront improvements to enhance curb appeal.Business Security Camera Fund: supports the installation or upgrades of business security camera systems.Downtown Patio Fund: offers funding between $1,000 and $3,000 to support construction, expansion, and enhancement of outdoor patios. Business Activation Fund: Supports creative activations tied to major seasonal or cultural events to attract visitors.Each business may receive a maximum of two funds per year; however, it may apply to more than two programs;Applications must be submitted before deadline March 2, 2026 ; except the Patio fund which runs on a rolling until funds exhausted.Applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis;Applicants must wait for approval before starting work; otherwise, costs incurred before approval will not be reimbursed;Applicants to the Security Camera Fund must attend a security best-practices workshop provided by the police department;General Evaluation Criteria for all programs: Feasibility / Financial need/ Creativity & visibility/ Economic impact / Timing / Environmental benefitEvaluation criteria for the Downtown Patio Fund :Patio size and seating capacity;Visual impact and contribution to a vibrant streetscape;Project readiness, including secured or planned City and/or liquor permits; andInclusion of safety, accessibility, or sustainability features. Eligible costs will be reimbursed after the project is completed; andReimbursement is issued via EFT (or by cheque for Patio Fund applications).

ECE Registry;Employed or self-employed on a full- or part-time basis by an eligible licensed child care facility;Enrolled part-time in an ECE program at a recognized post-secondary institute with the intention to complete the ECE certification or upgrades within a mutually agreed-upon timeline with their Employer (up to a maximum of three years);Must submit evidence of successful course completion to their Employer at the end of each course/semester;Students must take at least 1 course per semester with an intention to complete the training on a part-time basis within 3 years; andEmployed at the childcare facility for a minimum of 15 hours per week.Post-secondary Institute Requirements:Approved by the Province of BC as a recognized program and institute;Meets provincial standards and ECE certification requirements.Program Details:Maximum funded employees:Facilities license for under 32 spaces - 2 eligible staff;Facilities license for 32 or more space - 4 eligible staff.The subsidy can go towards in-class/online instructional hours to complete and/or upgrade their ECE credentials at a recognized post-secondary institute of their choice;The training wage cannot be applied to practicum hours or courses already started or completed prior to grant approval.

      Grant Criteria 
      The B.C. Employer Training Grant provides funding of 80% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000 per employee to employers who support skills training for their new or current employees. Training can be taken at a public post-secondary institution or through a private training provider (additional course syllabus requirements apply), so long as training is in compliance with PTIB (see pages 15/16 of the PTIB Policy Manual here).  The intent of the program is to help British Columbians access the skills training required to adapt to the labour market’s changing job requirements, while also addressing the skills gap in the province.Grant Value: 80% of eligible training costs up to $10,000 per traineeTurnaround Time: Up to 40 business daysEligible Applicants:Be operating in B.C. for at least 1 year;Have a Business BCeID; andBe in good standing with the Province of B.C.Eligible TraineesCanadian citizens, permanent residents, or protected persons;Be either unemployed or employed by the applicant employer;Be at least 16 years at the time of application;Have no real or perceived conflict of interest with the employer.To ensure an application is not denied due to conflict of interest, employers wishing to train family members must email etg@gov.bc.ca with a clear justification for their choice of the participant following the submission of their application.Trainees could be from outside BC, so long as the employer is BC-based, is paying for the training and will continue to employ people who live in BCIneligible TraineesIndividuals employed by a company other than the employer at the time of application;Temporary foreign workers, international students, working holiday visas, or other temporary residents; andParticipants who are receiving Employment Insurance (EI) or Income Assistance (IA) without prior approval from the Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction.EI or IA recipients are advised to seek approval from the Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction prior to training.Eligible TrainingMust be relevant to the immediate needs of the business and the trainee's job;Must lead to a "better job", leading to one of the following results:Increased pay;Promotion or advancement to another position;Move from part-time to full-time employment; ORMove from temporary/casual/seasonal employment to permanent employment.Training with a start date on or after the date of application submission;Training duration must be 52 weeks in duration or less.Ineligible TrainingTraining toward diploma or degree programs;Training needed to maintain current skills/certification;Training that has already been funded for the same participant;Training that is simultaneously funded for the participant by another federal or provincial program;Ineligible training methods:Consulting;Coaching;Coaching may be permitted as part of training toward coaching certification or when coaching is needed to complement a broader skills training program.Mentorships;Trade shows;Annual meetings;Networking;Seminars;Conferences; andPaid practicums.Eligible Training Providers:Be a B.C.-based training provider;Exceptions may be considered in exceptional circumstances.Be arm's length from the employer with no real or perceived conflict of interest;Training providers must deliver training as the main business activity;Includes but not limited to the following types of training providers:B.C. public post-secondary institutions;Trade or technical schools designated by the Industry Training Authority (ITA);Private training institutions certified and designated by the Private Training Institutions Branch (PTIB);Exceptions may apply if the Ministry deems the provider is a qualified instructor and training is competitively priced.Training organizations run by a B.C. school district;Industry associations.Indigenous Elders.Only when the trainee is Indigenous; andThe request for Elder support will be assessed on a case-by-case basis. The application should identify the Elder(s) providing the supports, the associated costs, and a description of the Elder supports.Training providers must be in compliance with Private Training Institutions Branch (PTIB) (see pages 15/16 of the PTIB Policy Manual here);Examples of programs that DO NOT require approval include:A career-related program at a registered institution for which tuition is less than $4,000;  A career-related program at a designated institution for which tuition is less than $1,000; A language program at a designated institution that is no more than six months and lessthan $4,000;Any language program at a registered institution; andA commercial driving instruction program. Programs that DO require approval fall into three categories and include: Class A: Career-related programs with 40 or more hours of instruction, for which tuition is at least $4,000. A career-related program is defined as a program that has the purpose of enhancing students’ employability or ability to carry out a career occupation;Class B: Career-related programs at designated/interim designated institutions, other than Class A programs, for which tuition is at least $1,000; andClass C: Language programs at designated/interim designated institutions that are longer than six months or for which tuition is at least $4,000. A language program is defined as a program that has as its learning objective that students gain or improve proficiency in a language.Eligible ExpensesTuition feesMandatory student feesExamination feesTextbooks, software and other required materialsTravel costs, only under certain circumstances (please see Appendix C for more information)Mandatory unpaid practicums for occupational certificationsIneligible ExpensesMembership fees, subscription fees, annual fees, professional association duesSoftware purchase/license for the businessLaptops, tablets, and other hardwareEquipment (e.g. boots and tools)Participant wages while in trainingProgram Details:Maximum funding per fiscal year (April 1 - March 31): $300,000 per employer;Applications that are not assessed after 60 calendar days will be returned unassessed;Applicants must submit and appeal within 15 days of having an application denied;Applicants can have paid for training prior to applying however cannot have started training prior to applying;Each course must be applied for in a separate application;If separate payments are required for individual courses, the applicant will need to submit separate applications for each course.Employers must pay all costs in full before reimbursement claims can be made;Training should be of no cost to the trainees.       Grant Criteria 
      The PRIIME (Programme d’aide à l’intégration en emploi des immigrants et des minorités visibles) provides a wage subsidy of up to 60% of the employee’s gross salary, capped at minimum wage, for a maximum duration of 40 weeks, with an increased subsidy of up to 70% available for individuals with disabilities. The program supports the employment integration of immigrants and visible minorities by funding onboarding, HR adaptations, and job-relevant training. Grant Value:Wage subsidy up to 60% (or 70% for people with disabilities), capped at minimum wage;Up to $2,000 for onboarding;Up to $5,000 for HR adaptations;Up to $5,000 or 80 hours for training;Up to $10,000 for general disability-related expenses.Turnaround Time: pendingEligible Employers:Must be an employer based in Québec;Can be private-sector companies, non-profits, or cooperatives;Must provide:Supervision and onboarding support;Mentorship or accompaniment during the integration period;A workplace environment conducive to skill development.Must commit to long-term employment potential for the candidate beyond the subsidy;Must not be a public organization, government entity, or political body;Must demonstrate:Inclusion and diversity efforts in HR practicesWillingness to adapt HR tools if required (e.g., evaluation processes, onboarding guides)Must agree to submit progress updates and reimbursement documentationEligible Candidates:Must be an immigrant or visible minority, legally authorized to work in Canada;Must reside in Québec;Must be seeking a first significant North American work experience in their trained field;Can be overqualified or under-employed in current job market;Must be hired for a position related to their academic or professional background;Must be employed on payroll (not contractors);Persons with disabilities are eligible and receive additional support;Candidates cannot have previously held significant, long-term work experience in their field in North America; andMust not have previously participated in a similar Emploi-Québec integration subsidy.Eligible Expenses:Onboarding & Mentorship Support:Up to $2,000 to help cover costs of coaching, supervision, or mentoring the new hireAdaptation of HR Tools & Practices:Up to $5,000 to modify internal HR practices or tools to accommodate the new hire (e.g., training materials, evaluation systems)Job-Relevant Training:Up to $5,000, or a maximum of 80 hours, for technical or professional training aligned with the job roleMay include French language training, software skills, or sector-specific upskillingDisability-Related General Costs:Up to $10,000 to support accommodations such as accessible equipment, specialized software, or other services necessary for integrationProgram Details:Maximum funding duration is 40 weeks;Positions must be full-time position (30–40 hrs/week) in the candidate's field of study or expertise;Candidates must be added to official payroll, not freelance or contractor arrangements;Placement maximum duration of 40 weeks;The employer must apply before the candidate starts employment;Job placements must have:A clearly defined training and integration plan;Performance evaluations and tracking.The program promotes:Diversity hiring;Access to meaningful, skilled employment for immigrants and minorities.Applications are assessed based on:Quality of integration plan;Suitability of the job position;Candidate's fit and support mechanisms provided.Reimbursements are conditional on:Completion of surveys and progress reports;Submission of wage records, invoices, and mentorship activity logs.Funding is not stackable with other government wage subsidies (e.g., wage subsidies from Emploi-Québec or federal Youth Employment programs).

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program may not be combined with other provincial or federal wage subsidies for the same position;This program is not retroactive — employers must receive approval before the candidate begins employment;Preference may be given to employers who:Demonstrate inclusive hiring practices for immigrants and visible minorities;Offer full-time roles aligned with the candidate’s field of study or expertise;Provide mentorship and structured onboarding aligned with PRIIME expectations;Commit to retaining the employee after the subsidy period ends;Adapt HR tools or training practices to support the candidate’s integration;Include accessibility measures for participants with disabilities where applicable.Process Best Practices:Employers should consult with a program officer early to confirm candidate and project eligibility;Applications must be submitted before the employment start date and include a job description, integration plan, and HR adaptation outline (if relevant);Supporting documents may include the participant’s resume, immigration or minority status confirmation, and proof of residency in Québec;Reimbursement is conditional upon submission of payroll records, onboarding documentation, and mentorship/training activity logs;If applying for disability-related costs, employers should estimate required accommodations and provide justification as part of the application.Links :Program website: click hereProgram guidelines (French only): click here

andFirst year students.Turnaround Time: 5 business daysEligible Employer:Canadian-owned companies or subsidiaries;Companies primarily involved in the generation, transmission and distribution of electricity;Firms manufacturing equipment and providing services necessary to the generation of green energy;Firms that provide sector support in R & D, business development, or energy efficiency; Must have a nepotism policy in place; andNot receiving Employment Insurance (EI) benefits.Ineligible Candidates:Students registered in trade or apprenticeship programs;Students in Canada on work visas or student visas; andReturning students who have been funded by the program previously.The same student will not be eligible for multiple rounds of funding for the same type of employment with the same employer.Program Details: Placements can be part-time or full-time;Maximum 30 hours per week;Maximum duration: 1 year;The program operates on a rolling intake basis;It does not offer funding based on the semester system like the other SWPPs.Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. andConstruction, renovation, or retrofit activities for personal use.Note: Ergonomic office furniture is typically not eligible - office equipment needs to be adapted for accessibility and not just ergonomics.Project Details:Maximum 1 application per organization per intake;Funding is provided through a contribution agreement;Non-Indigenous workplace applicants must have current employees with disabilities and describe future hiring plans to support persons with disabilities;Indigenous workplace applicants must have hiring plans (but not necessarily current employees); Indigenous community projects do not require current employment of persons with disabilities;Projects may have a duration of up to 24 months (2 years);Projects must be ready to begin incurring eligible expenses no later than December 1, 2026; This funding supports the development of digital diagnostics, digital roadmaps, implementation strategies, and system selection, with the goal of accelerating digital transformation and investment projects among Québec-based businesses.Grant Value:Non-repayable financial assistance covering up to 50% of eligible project costs;Maximum funding of $20,000 per project.Turnaround Time: Approximately 50 business daysEligible Applicants:Must be a for-profit business or social economy enterprise established in Québec;Foreign businesses must register in Québec and begin regular operations within 12 months of project approval;Must be undertaking a project that supports the company’s digital transformation and long-term performance;Businesses must generate at least 40% of their revenue from autonomous activities; andApplicants that do not meet public integrity standards may be denied.Eligible Projects:Must involve digital diagnostics, roadmaps, implementation strategies, or technology/system selection activities;Projects must be tied to investment efforts that improve digital performance, operational productivity, or market competitiveness; and Must align with Québec’s economic modernization goals.Eligible Expenses:Professional Services fees;Consulting fees to conduct diagnostics or develop plans;Relocation Fees; andExpenses must be directly linked to the approved project and incurred after the funding agreement is signed.Note : for full list of eligible and ineligible applicants, projects and expenses click here (french only).Program Details:Maximum project length 12 months; Program focus area includes:Integration of AI systems;Numerical systems;Numerical diagnostics. Applications are assessed on their alignment with digital transformation goals, financial soundness, and overall project feasibility;A strategic planning document is required, including SWOT analysis, mission, vision, and main challenges for the next three years;All required documents must be provided at application, and incomplete submissions will be rejected without review;       Grant Criteria 
      Eurostars is an international R&D funding program that helps innovative Canadian SMEs work with European and other international partners to develop new or significantly improved technologies. Through NRC IRAP, Canada supports eligible Canadian SMEs with up to $500,000 CAD per project to carry out collaborative research and development that leads to products, processes, or services with strong commercial potential in global markets.Grant Value: Up to 50% of eligible costs ( to a maximum of up to $500,000). Turnaround Time: Eligibility check within 1 week, but funding decisions are typically made within 7–8 months after the Eurostars application deadline.Eligible Applicants:Incorporated, for-profit Canadian SMEs (≤ 500 employees);Must be eligible for and registered with NRC IRAP before applying;Canadian SME does not have to be the overall project lead, but an innovative SME must lead the consortium;Must participate as part of an international consortium meeting all 7 Eurostars eligibility criteria:The project must involve at least two independent entities from at least two Eurostars countries;The project must be led by an innovative SME from a Eurostars country (the lead does not have to be Canadian);Innovative SMEs must collectively account for at least 50% of the total project budget;No one organization (or country) may carry more than 70% of the total project costs;The project must be for civilian applications only (no defence or military use;The project must involve research and experimental development leading to a new or significantly improved product, process, or service, with a clear plan for commercialization.Ineligible Applicants:Large enterprises.Universities, colleges, and research institutes (not funded by Canada under Eurostars).Not-for-profit organizations.Canadian firms not eligible for NRC IRAP or not registered with IRAP.Self-financed applicants.Eligible Projects:International collaborative R&D projects involving:At least two independent entities; andFrom at least two Eurostars countries. Project must be civilian (non-military);Clear technical innovation and commercialization pathway; andProject duration: up to 36 months. Ineligible Projects:Projects without genuine R&D or technical uncertainty;Projects focused only on commercialization, deployment, or scale-up;Projects lacking an eligible international consortium;Defence or military applications; andProjects where SMEs do not play a central R&D role.Eligible Activities:Industrial research and experimental development of new products, processes, or services;Technology development and prototype creation;Commercialization pathway development with market validation;IP protection and patent development; andInnovation with international collaborative dimension.Eligible Expenses:Personnel costs for R&D activities:Salaries and wages of employees directly performing experimental R&D;Time must be clearly tied to approved technical work and documented.Materials and supplies:Consumable materials used directly in R&D activities;Must be essential to conducting the approved technical work.Subcontracting / third-party R&D services:Specialized R&D services required to carry out the project;Must directly support experimental development activities;Subcontracting should be limited, justified, and not replace core in-house R&D.Technical consulting and expertise:External technical expertise for testing, validation, or specialized R&D tasks;Must be directly related to resolving technical uncertainty.Ineligible Costs:Marketing, sales, and commercialization costs ; Travel and subsistence Equipment and capital expenditures ; Intellectual property and legal costs;Dissemination and communication costs;General business and operating costs;Indirect costs and flat-rate overheads;Project management and coordination (non-R&D);Manufacturing, scale-up, and production costs;Costs incurred outside the eligible project period; andAny expense not aligned with IRAP eligible cost categories or not pre-approved.Program Details:Call opening: January 2026;Deadline: March 2026 (CET deadline applies internationally);Single centralized application via Eurostars platform;National funding decisions are made after Eurostars ranking;Projects are evaluated on:Excellence (innovation & technical challenge/ 40%);Impact (market potential & commercialization/ 30%);Quality & efficiency (consortium & work plan/ 30%).Each Eurostars country's funding body has country-specific eligibility criteria, documentation requirements, and funding rates, applicants must contact national funding body (IRAP) before applying;Best 200 projects from remote expert evaluation advance to Independent Evaluation Panel for final selection; only projects with positive legal/financial viability and "excellent" or "good" quality rating receive funding; andAppeal possible for procedural errors only.

      Best Practices & Forms

      Grant Criteria 
      The Expanded Energy Management Program is a three-stream program supporting organizational energy management capacity building. Ontario businesses can receive up to $100,000 annually to hire an Energy Manager, plus up to $250,000 for Energy Management Information Systems, alongside free strategic energy management coaching and training.Grant Value: Up to $100,000 per year for 3 years to hire an Energy Manager; Up to $250,000 for industrial facilities implementing Energy Management Information Systems; andFree Strategic Energy Management Coaching and Training.Turnaround Time: Pending.Eligible Applicants:Must be an active Save on Energy business customer account in Ontario and connected to the IESO-Controlled Grid or Distribution System;Must commit to annual performance reporting.;Industrial facilitiesmust meet minimum energy-use thresholds:SEM participation: at least 20,000 GJ total energy consumption (all fuels) over any 12-month period in the past 24 months;Energy Manager funding: at least 50,000 GJ total energy consumption (all fuels) over any 12-month period in the past 24 months;Must be in eligible NAICS codes: 11, 21, 22, 23, 31-33, 48, 56 (Agriculture, Mining, Utilities, Construction, Manufacturing, Transportation, Waste Management);Commercial facilitiesmust meet minimum energy-use thresholds:SEM participation: at least 3,000,000 kWh total electricity consumption over any 12-month period in the past 24 months;Energy Manager funding: at least 6,500,000 kWh total electricity consumption over any 12-month period in the past 24 months;Energy Manager candidates must have relevant qualifications (engineering degree OR professional certification such as CEM or CMVP); andEnergy Manager must dedicate a minimum 50% of work time to energy management activities.Eligible Activities:Activities related to the Energy Manager Hiring:Recruiting and employing dedicated energy management personnel;Energy audits, consumption analysis, conservation project development;Staff training and awareness programs.Activities related to Strategic Energy Management:Developing energy management action plans;Integrating energy considerations into business operations;Performance tracking and continuous improvement initiatives. Activities related to Energy Management Information Systems:Implementing energy tracking and monitoring systems;Installing data collection hardware and analytics software;System integration and automation for energy optimization. Eligible Expenses:Energy Manager salary and benefits (up to funding cap);EMIS software licensing and implementation costs;Energy monitoring hardware and sensors;System integration and installation services;Data analytics platforms; andTraining costs for energy management staffProgram Details:The program has three streams : Stream 1 - Energy Manager: Annual salary subsidy distributed over 3 years to hire dedicated energy management staff;Stream 2 - Strategic Energy Management: Free coaching program helping businesses develop energy management action plans and integrate energy considerations into operations;Stream 3 - Energy Management Information Systems: Funding for software/hardware systems that track, analyze, and optimize energy consumption in industrial facilities.Funding is distributed annually over a 3-year period with performance milestones;All participants receive access to free energy management training workshops and resources;EMIS funding is specifically targeted at industrial facilities with significant energy consumption;Facilities using 400,000 GJ or less per year can receive up to $50,000 for an EMIS;Facilities using more than 400,000 GJ per year can receive up to $250,000 for an EMIS;Funding covers up to 50% of eligible project costs.Applicants may combine up to 5 facilities;Applicants must : Provide business profile and facility information;Commit to 3-year program participation;Agree to annual performance reporting.The Strategic Energy Management (SEM) Program is cohort-based (7-15 participants): Helps organizations implement continuous energy management practices and reduce energy consumption ;Applicants must create an internal Energy Team to complete SEM milestones and implement energy-saving actions;The initial participation period is 2 years, with possible extension;Participants receive performance incentives: Paid at $0.02/kWh of confirmed electricity savings from non-incented projects;Maximum $100,000 per 12-month period;Savings must pass Technical Review and be based on the electricity baseline model.Participants receive enabling incentives: Up to $5,000 total for energy management tools (e.g., monitoring tools, software).Payments for the Energy Manager stream are issued in two parts each year: 25% upfront (max $50,000) and the remaining amount after the Annual Report is approved, up to the $100,000 annual cap.All industrial activities funded by NRCan must be finished by March 31, 2027. Note: Full details on the Energy Manager, SEM, and EMIS program requirements are available on the program website.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Energy Manager candidates must meet the required qualifications (engineering degree or certifications like CEM or CMVP);Matching the Energy Manager role with at least 50% of work hours focused on energy management;Industrial facilities should check EMIS funding eligibility separately (up to $250,000 available);To access energy training and coaching support, applicants should join a Strategic Energy Management (SEM) cohort; To qualify for performance incentives, the project cannot receive funding from any other IESO or Ontario government program; andThe program is not retroactive—any measures installed before your program start date do not qualify for funding.Process Best Practices:Plan for a 3-year commitment with yearly performance reporting; funding is paid annually, not upfront;Combine hiring an Energy Manager with free Strategic Energy Management coaching to maximize benefits;Use the program’s free training opportunities to build internal energy management skills.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides up to $30 million in funding over three years (2024/25–2026/27) to help cover the additional costs of transporting uneconomic or residual fibre from BC Crown land to non-sawlog processing facilities. The goal is to increase the use of low-value fibre that would otherwise be left unused or burned.Grant Value: The program does not specify an average funding amount per project, as funding is calculated based on each project’s incremental costs.Turnaround Time: To be confirmed.Eligible Applicants: First Nations (bands, Treaty and Indigenous governments) in BC;Companies owned by Indigenous governments or entrepreneurs;Small area-based tenure holders (e.g., community forests, woodlot licensees);Forest tenure holders, fibre suppliers or purchasers not owning a dimensional softwood lumber mill;BC provincial agencies and local governments (municipalities, regional districts); andThird parties with written authorization from an eligible applicant.Ineligible Applicants:Companies or tenure holders that manufacture dimensional softwood lumber.Eligible Projects:Be located on BC provincial Crown land;Deliver uneconomic residual fibre to non-sawlog facilities;Identify current market value of the fibre acceptable to FESBC;Not displace fibre within the economic radius of the receiving facility;Be completed and scaled by March 31 of the fiscal year; andAlign with Ministry of Forests and regional priorities.Notes: Previously funded projects are referenced here.Eligible Activities:Delivery of uneconomic residual fibre from cutting authorities harvested for sawlog; andOverstorey removal and delivery of uneconomic fibre from fire or insect-damaged stands or other acceptable stands.Ineligible Activities:Delivery of fibre within restricted zones (Coast Fibre Recovery Zone);Delivery from recent BCTS timber sales (post-Dec 31 2022); andFibre delivery inside the economic reach of the receiving facility.Eligible Expenses:Incremental delivery costs from end location through to receiving facility gate (e.g., skidding/forwarding, processing, loading, hauling, road maintenance)Overstorey removal costs acceptable to FESBC;Project administration (planning, reporting); andGST, if applicable.Note: More detailed information on cost calculations is available in the application portal.Ineligible Expenses:Costs where destination is a dimensional lumber facility;Costs that are tenure obligations or part of standard appraisal;Expenses funded by other sources;Activities outside the intent of the funding;Costs incurred beyond the receiving facility gate; andSilviculture costs.Program Details:This program has Two-Track Model:Track 1: Incremental delivery costs for fibre from standard commercial harvesting operations outside the economic radius of receiving facility; and Track 2: Stand rehabilitation/overstorey removal from wildfire or insect-damaged stands, delivering fibre to non-sawlog facilitiesFunding Calculation (Track 1): Incremental Net Cost = End Product Market Value − Incremental Delivery Cost. FESBC approves funding only for the differential (not the full cost). Market value must be validated by recent log/fibre purchase agreements acceptable to FESBC;No maximum funding request, but large budgets may be scaled or phased depending on available annual funds;Approved projects subject to semi-annual review and adjustment of net cost calculations to align with current market conditions;Projects must not displace or prevent the movement of fibre within the economic radius of the receiving facility. Applicants must map overlapping areas of interest and provide verification that all available fibre will be utilized;Land Manager Coordination (Track 2): Applicants proposing stand rehabilitation must engage with local Ministry of Forests District staff prior to application to ensure alignment with Land Manager priorities;Applications are submitted via the FESBC online portal (FESIMS);Applicants can submit multiple applications (e.g., projects in different geographic areas);The Guide for Submitting a Proposal is available for download from the Additional Information menu on the FESIMS main landing page;Applicants must provide detailed cost and delivery information, maps, timelines, and volume projections;FESBC evaluates applications based on cost effectiveness, Indigenous involvement, innovation, and alignment with program goals; If project is scalable, indicate this—FESBC may fund part of the proposal if full funding isn’t possible, with the option to add later if funds free up; andAll projects must be completed and scaled by March 31 of the applicable fiscal year; quarterly status updates on cutting authorities required during project lifecycle.

those living within must apply through Kativik services;Cree individuals residing in a Cree community may be required to show that local employment services were accessed first;Naskapi individuals are eligible regardless of residence, as long as initial community procedures have been completed.Program Details : Maximum subsidy duration of 52 weeks, extendable to 60 weeks for participants with disabilities depending on needs and job requirements;Maximum 40 hours per week;Employers may receive up to $2,000 to provide onboarding support and mentorship for the hired participant, as outlined in the PRIIME guide(only available in French);Reimburses up to 100% of eligible human resource management expenses, up to a maximum of $5,000;Provides up to 100% of direct training costs, capped at $5,000 or 80 hours of supplementary training;Additional support of up to $10,000 is available to cover eligible general costs for participants with disabilities, as per Emploi-Québec accessibility guidelines;Supports the integration of First Nations and Inuit individuals into small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through employment, onboarding, diversity initiatives, and skill development;Employers must offer roles with long-term retention potential beyond the subsidy period and actively engage in diversity management practices;Encourages partnerships between Indigenous organizations and employers to support recruitment and inclusion efforts;Only employers operating as SMEs in Québec are eligible, and must commit to hiring individuals from eligible Indigenous communities.
