andHave the financial capacity to pay the student for the duration of the placement in full (the wage subsidy will be administered after receiving the final pay stub at the end of the placement).Note: Restaurants are out of scope and are ineligible for this program.Eligible Candidates:Full- or part-time students in recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Graduate students (including Masters and Ph.D.) are eligible.Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or persons to whom refugee protection has been conferred under the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act;Legally entitled to work in Canada in accordance with relevant provincial or territorial legislation and regulations;Undertaking a placement recognized as a Work-Integrated Learningcomponent in their studies.The placement can be required or optional, for credit or not for credit.Underrepresented students:Women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics);Indigenous students;Students with disabilities;Newcomers to Canada (immigrated within the last 5 years);First-year students; An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.The employer must provide on-the-job supervision;Applications that are 2 months out from the start of term are added to a waitlist;If the employer has applied and is on a waitlist, they will receive communication approximately 45 days before intake opens to review the status of the application.Remote work options for students are available; andThe final subsidy amount will be determined at the end of the placement term upon receipt of all supporting documents.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Gearing Up program provides up to 70% a maximum of $7,000 to mining or mineral exploration employers to subsidize the hiring of post-secondary students. The intent of the program is to attract talent to in-demand mining careers and to build skills needed for a meaningful career in this sector.Grant Value: 50% of wages to a maximum of $5000;70% of wages to a maximum of $7000 for students from the following underrepresented groups:Women in STEM;Indigenous peoples;Persons with disabilities;Recent immigrants;First year students; andVisible minorities.Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Employers:Be Canadian-owned or a Canadian subsidiary;For-profit companies in the mining or mineral exploration sector; andNon-profit organizations.Eligible Candidates: Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person with refugee protection given under the law;Be registered in a post-secondary program (full- or part-time);Studying fields related to science, technology, engineering, mathematics, and/or business; andStudents in both required and optional courses with Work Integrated Learning components are eligible.Note: International student, students in apprenticeships or vocational studies are ineligible for the programProgram Details:Placements must be completed within Canada;Can be full-time or part-time;Employers are responsible for the recruiting and the selection of participants;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.While employers can submit multiple applications for different students, each student is eligible to receive 1 subsidy;Placements in consecutive semesters is not allowed.The wage subsidy is paid out at the end of the placement or when the employer contribution threshold has been met;Mandatory training for both the participants and their immediate supervisors:Gender equity in mining works;Introduction to intercultural awareness training; andIndigenous awareness training.Required documents at the end of the placement:Student payroll information;Employer exit survey; andParticipant exit survey.

Funding supports activities such as product development, market validation, strategic hiring, and securing strategic partnerships. The program is intended to accelerate commercialization, attract private investment, and position Quebec companies for long-term growth.Grant Value:Equity or quasi-equity investments ranging from $250,000 to $1,000,000 for most sectors;Up to $2,000,000 for companies in the biopharmaceutical sector (limited to $750,000 for those based in Greater Montreal);Requires a 1:1 matching investment from a recognized private investor;Structured as convertible debentures or SAFE-type instruments.Turnaround Time: PendingEligible Applicants:Must be for-profit, legally incorporated in Quebec, and in the pre-commercial stage;Must offer innovative, scalable solutions with strong commercialization potential;Must be supported by a recognized incubator, accelerator, or innovation partner; andSole proprietors, NPOs, or entities without a scalable growth plan.Eligible Projects:Final development and validation of innovative products or services;Hiring key talent for business development, operations, or commercialization;Forming strategic alliances or preparing for export-readiness; andActivities that enhance investor readiness and long-term growth positioning.Ineligible Projects:Routine operating expenses or maintenance activities;Projects without clear commercialization timelines; andActivities unrelated to innovation, scaling, or market entry.Eligible Expenses:Salaries for new hires in strategic roles (e.g., commercial lead, business dev);Consulting fees related to go-to-market, IP, legal, or investment readiness;Expenses tied to investor engagement, strategic partnerships, or pilot testing; andDevelopment tools, certifications, or infrastructure necessary for commercialization.Program Details:Projects may span multiple fiscal periods depending on growth milestones;Funding is non-repayable only upon conversion terms or exit/liquidity events;Applicants must collaborate with Investissement Québec and private investors; andBusinesses must show measurable outcomes tied to commercialization and job creation in Quebec.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices :This program does not provide retroactive funding. Only expenses incurred after the project start date, as identified in the investment agreement with Investissement Québec, will be deemed eligible;This program may be stackable with federal or municipal funding sources but cannot be combined with other Investissement Québec funding for the same project expenses unless explicitly approved as part of a coordinated financing structure;All applicants must secure a matching private investment from a recognized investor equal to the amount requested from the program.Process Best Practices :Applicants must be referred by a recognized incubator, accelerator, or innovation support partner and consult with Investissement Québec prior to submitting an application;Proposed projects will be assessed according to the following criteria:Degree of innovation and scalability of the proposed solution;Readiness for commercialization, including product development stage, market validation, and investor appeal;Alignment with Quebec’s strategic sectors and potential for economic impact in the province;Capacity to attract private investment, meet funding milestones, and contribute to job creation or ecosystem growth.Forms and Links :Program Website (French only) : click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Incoming Buyer Program (IPB) helps Manitoba SMEs bring international buyers to the province for face-to-face business meetings to facilitate export sales. Reimburses up to $5,000 or 50% of airfaire and accommodation costs, rolling intake until funds exhausted.Grant Value:   50% of costs up to $5,000.Turnaround Time: to be confirmed. Eligible Applicants:Manitoba-based small to medium-sized enterprises (SMEs);Companies with under 500 employees;Annual revenues between $30,000 and $50 million;Must be actively pursuing export sales opportunities;Must have the capacity to host international buyers and conduct business meetings;To qualify as a buyer:Must be an international for-profit buyer;This must be the buyer’s first visit related to the applicant company;Buyer must be actively seeking to purchase new products/services and participate in business meetings with the company;In commercial contexts, buyers can be distributors, agents, dealers, importers, or wholesalers;For project procurement, eligible buyers can be prime contractors seeking subcontractors/products; andBuyers must have senior decision-maker responsibility (e.g., owner, CEO, VP, manager).Applicants cannot have outstanding Manitoba tax arrears and cannot be in receivership; andMust be fully compliant with all relevant government laws and regulations.Eligible Target Markets:International buyers from any country outside Canada;Qualified buyers with genuine interest in purchasing Manitoba products or services;Buyers who have not previously visited Manitoba for business purposes with this company (preference for first-time visits). Eligible Activities:Economy airfare costs for international buyers traveling to Manitoba;Local accommodation costs in Manitoba for visiting buyers;Business meetings and negotiations conducted in Manitoba;Facility tours and product demonstrations for visiting buyers; andActivities directly related to facilitating export sales discussions.Ineligible Activities:Entertainment, meals, or hospitality expenses;Ground transportation or local travel costs;Costs for accompanying family members or non-business participants;Premium or business class airfare upgrades;Accommodation costs outside of Manitoba; andExpenses incurred before application approval or after the visit has concluded. Program Detail:Applications are accepted year-round until funds are fully committed;Events must be within the current fiscal year; applications for future fiscal events open on January 1 of that year; Applications must be submitted and approved before the international buyer's visit occurs;Companies may apply for multiple incoming buyer visits throughout the year (subject to budget availability);All expense costs must be paid by the applicant first and then reimbursed;Applicants must submit supporting documents (business overview, tax return, financials);Reimbursement is made after proof of payment is submitted (receipts, invoices);Applications do not guarantee funding approval;The total government support from all sources for an activity cannot exceed 50 % of the costs;Priority given to first-time applicants and companies with strong export potential;Approved applicants will be contacted within 12 months after the visit to complete an evaluation.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Ensure the international buyer qualifies as a legitimate business prospect with genuine purchasing interest;Document how the visit will directly support export development;Ensure previous government funding for the same activity is disclosed so total support does not exceed program limits.First-time applicants and companies demonstrating strong export potential receive priority consideration;Companies can apply multiple times per year for different buyer visits, but each application is subject to available funds.Process Best Practices:Apply well in advance of the planned buyer visit to ensure approval before travel arrangements are finalized;Submit expense claims within 30 days after the visit. Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

Funding is provided for a one year term, with a possible extension to a second year. The program aims to help Alberta companies scale new technologies, create high skill jobs, and de-risk the commercialization process. Grant Value: 75% of the candidates salary to a maximum of $120,000. Turnaround Time: 6-8 weeks.Eligible Employers: For-profit SME incorporated in Alberta with less than 500 full-time employees;Must have annual revenues less than $50,000,000;Must be developing innovative technologies or knowledge-based solutions;Not have more than 2 active Alberta Innovates-funded associates simultaneously;Applicants are required to have a significant portion of their physical and operational presence in Alberta;Discernible intent for operational benefits to flow primarily within Alberta; andHave up-to-date corporate filings (Alberta Innovates may perform a corporate search including bankruptcy and litigations). Eligible Associates:Cannot be a shareholder of the applicant company with over 15% of total shares;Has no more than 12 months of previous employment with the applicant company; andMust be legally entitled to work in Canada and prepared to live in Alberta for the duration of the internship.Note: Preference will be given to Associates who have formal business education (e.g. BBA, BCom, MBA, etc.).Program Details:Applicant companies should be developing mid-to-late stage technologies*; Early developmental stages will be considered on a case-by-case basis;The application must identify a phase of product development that can be completed and evaluated in 1 year;Successful applicants can reapply for an extension at the end of the first year;The funded position must focus on the commercialization of technology and include activities relating to: business development, product validation, manufacturing analysis, production planning, exploration of new markets, sales, and marketing, financial strategy, etc.;Position must be full-time (min. 30 hours per week);The applicant company must be able to pay 25% of the candidate's salary;       Grant Criteria 
      This program offers up to $7,000 for employers willing to hire students from Arts/Arts adjacent program in any accredited Canadian post Secondary institute for tech meaningful roles. Through the subsidized placements, the program seeks to build the talent bench of Canadian businesses and contribute to developing the skills of the next generation in Canada's workforce.Grant Value: 50% of wages up to $5000;70% of wages up to $7,000 for participants in the following underrepresented groups:Women in STEM or business;Indigenous students;Visible minorities;Recent immigrants (immigrated to Canada within the last 5 years);Persons with disabilities;First-year students;Students on their first work-term. Turnaround Time: Approximately 2 weeks.Eligible Employer: Be a registered Canadian business or organization;Be either a private, non-profit, or municipal institution;Both tech and non-tech organizations are eligible; Have the financial capacity to hire a student for a part or full-time work term, pay them consistently, and provide meaningful work experience; andEmployers cannot apply without a candidate. Ineligible employers:Post-secondary institutions;Banks or large financial sector employers; andFederal or provincial government.Eligible Participants:Canadian Citizen, permanent resident, or a protected person defined by the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act;Must be a registered student in an Arts/Arts adjacent course in a post-secondary institution program;Private colleges may be eligible on a case-by-case basis;Arts and Arts adjacent courses may include:Commerce; Data Science;Economics;Creative Writing;Linguistics;Sociology etc. (A full list of examples can be found here)Pursuing a tech-immersive career;The student must not be an international student with a work permit; andThe student must not be an immediate family member of the employer with the same employer previously.Placement Details:IntakesWinter 2025 - January 1, 2025, to March 31, 2025: CLOSEDSummer 2025 - May 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025: OPENPositions must be IT-related (e.g. software, programming, web/app development) OR Business-related (e.g. sales, business development, or marketing roles that promote tech skills development);Must be no more than 16 weeks in duration;The position can be full- or part-time;Minimum 15 hours per week;Maximum applications per employer: 5;Note: this is an additional 5 on the Career Ready SWPP placements for a total of 10 for student placements from Technation;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.The employer must have a nepotism policy with respect to the intern;The employer must provide on-the-job mentorship and support;Remote work is permitted.Preference will be given to tech immersive roles that are within high-growth sectors:Digital technology (IT, digital marketing, software engineering, etc.);AI / IoT / Machine Learning / Advanced Manufacturing;Cybersecurity;Agri-Tech;Clean Tech; andHealth Tech.

      Grant Criteria 
      The program provides up to $250,000 in funding to SMEs to commercialize their products, achieve optimal market position, increase revenue and potentially expand into global markets. The program is designed to de-risk the commercialization process by providing funds and coaching to SMEs. Grant Value: Up to $250,000.Turnaround Time: 3-4 weeksEligible Applicants: For-profit organizations that are either:Incorporated;General partnerships registered in Alberta;Limited partnerships registered in Alberta; orLimited liability partnerships registered in Alberta.Be Alberta-based;Have a significant physical and corporate operational presence in Alberta;Have appropriate Alberta ownership; andDiscernible intent that operational benefits will flow primarily within the Province of Alberta;Exist as a corporate person, with up-to-date corporate filings;Be authorized to undertake the proposed project, and execute a grant with Alberta Innovates on the standard terms; Have fewer than 500 full-time employees;Have less than $50,000,000 in annual gross revenue; andMust be in good standing with Alberta Innovates or its subsidiaries (InnoTech Alberta, C-FER Technologies).Eligible Partners: Exist as a corporate person, with up-to-date corporate filings; Be authorized to undertake the proposed project; Demonstrate that the relationship between the Applicant and Partner/ Strategic Partner/ Service Provider/ Collaborator does not create a conflict of interest; Be at arm's length from the Applicant;Must not have a conflict of interest with the applicant.Provide a letter indicating the Partner's/ Service Provider's/ Collaborator's intention to participate in the Project at the time of application; Have the financial capability to purchase or enter into a distribution agreement of the product upon Project completion of a demonstration;Show tangible resources committed to the Project; andMust be in good standing with Alberta Innovates or its subsidiaries (InnoTech Alberta, C-FER Technologies).Eligible Projects: Show that the product is a viable technology at Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 to 8; Be stepped with critical "go/no go" milestones with measurable target outcomes; Be completed within an 18-month term; Have the participation of at least 1 International Project Partner(s); Outline the financial contribution required by Applicant; and/or Comply with other criteria that Alberta Innovates may develop from time to time. Eligible Expenses:Labour costs, directly related to the project;Costs of materials;Acquisitions of property;Acquisitions of software or information databases;Direct operating costs;Technology transfer to the Applicant from an Alberta public sector research organization;Travel expenses if they are a necessary part of accomplishing the project and also have to be pre-approved by Alberta Innovates; andAny other expense pre-approved by Alberta Innovates in writing.Ineligible Expenses: Any cost incurred prior to the project start date;Any costs which have been or will be funded by other government funding;Transactions between related persons; Provisions for contingencies;Allowance for interest of debt;Losses on investments, bad debts and expenses for collection charges;Losses on other projects or activities outside the Alberta Portion of the Project;Fines and penalties;Unreasonable compensation for Project labour; Costs for professional training and development;costs related to land and buildings;depreciation and amortization charges;Advertising costs;Costs associated with applying for government grants and programs;Costs of internships or support for students of knowledge institutions;Basic professional services, fees and disbursements, such as ongoing routine accounting, tac and legal business requirements; Routine testing and maintenance; Costs relating to meals, entertainment, hospitality, alcohol and gifts;Federal and provincial income taxes, goods and services taxes; and Any other costs deemed ineligible by Alberta Innovates.Program Details: Funding is provided to support SMEs to find and enter a partnership with an "International Project Partner" for further product development or to pilot the technical and business merits of their product with the goal to prove the product value, and advance commercialization;Objectives of the program include: Have applicants build a relationship with an International Project Partner for collaborative development and testing, leveraging industry knowledge or access to new distribution channels;Establish an early to late-stage pilot;Form long-term business partnerships that extend market access;Provide access to new capital sources;Increased global competitiveness.The support of a technology development advisor is required for the ITP. They provide guidance and coaching and assess the Applicant's ITP readiness;Project Activities may include:Developing and testing technology;Piloting in an operational or test environment to move towards commercialization.Alberta Innovates will match the applicant's contributions for eligible project costs to a maximum investment of $250,000; andThe applicant's matching funds must be in the form of 50% cash and 50% in-kind contributions;E.g. Alberta Innovates investment of $250,000, Alberta SME $250,000 (50% cash and 50% In-Kind) and International project partner $250,000 (50% cash and 50% In-Kind).

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This program is not retroactive;This program can be stacked with other government funding however it won't cover any expense funded by another program;SME and International project partners must contribute equal funding to the project. Process Best Practices:Funding will be disbursed based on milestones being met.Forms: Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereApplication Portal: click here

Businesses may receive a conditional contribution, or both a repayable term loan and conditional contribution up to this amount. The goal of this program is to invest in projects that will result in full-time jobs creation or retention, and benefit the overall economic development of the region.Grant Value: Up to $5,000,000Turnaround Time: 4 weeksEligible Applicants:Canadian businesses from outside Ontario aiming to locate business operations in Northern Ontario; andHave a minimum 1 year of incorporation.Ineligible Applicants:Retail and consumer service businesses that primarily earn revenue by providing products and services directly to individuals;Accommodation & food service businesses and related business activities; andBusinesses that are primarily involved in wholesale activities.Eligible Expenses:Capital construction;Leasehold improvements;New or used equipment including capital leases;Land servicing costs;Information & communications technology (ICT) investments;Marketing for new products and business initiatives (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs, or $75,000, whichever is less); andTraining costs incurred with third parties (limited to a maximum of 20% of all other eligible project costs).Ineligible Expenses:They include but are not limited to the following projects, costs, and activities (some exceptions may be made where projects address a priority economic need in Northern Ontario):Ongoing operating costs including maintenance;In-kind contributions;Restructuring or refinancing of existing business operations;Business plans, strategic plans, feasibility studies, etc.;Assets acquired through operating leases;Research and development;Land purchase/lease;Rolling stock (e.g. cars, trucks & boats and motors);Project management, consulting, and administration costs;Mineral exploration, mine development, and milling operations;Working capital;Cost of inventory;Cellular and internet service projects;Capital projects or leasehold improvements to residential or personal properties;Acquisitions and buy-outs of existing businesses; andElectricity generation projects.Program Details:The applicant is expected to secure the balance of funding or financing necessary to implement the project;The applicant may be required to reimburse NOHFC if assets financed by NOHFC are sold after project completion; andCombined federal and provincial government funding (including any contribution from NOHFC) may not exceed 50% of eligible project costs for private sector projects;Agencies that are arms-length from government, with an independent Board of Directors, are not considered “government funding.”Evaluation Criteria:Factors that will be considered during the evaluation of applications will include but are not limited to:Job creation;Level of investment from other sources to be secured by the applicant;Strength of the applicant’s detailed business plan;Does not unreasonably impact existing Northern Ontario businesses;Net economic benefits for Northern Ontario; andOther business activities that will result in an economic development advantage for Northern Ontario.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Tourism businesses that provide accommodation services and operate as a tourist destination for local, regional and international visitors for extended stays (e.g., remote outfitter, family vacation resort) are potentially eligible;Businesses that only serve the overnight travelling public are considered ineligible (e.g. hotels and motels).Process Best Practices:Review the extensive ineligible expenses list to confirm all proposed activities will be approved;Recommended to have bridge funding between start of project and reimbursement payments, which are negotiated during project approval.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program offers employers a maximum of $13,440 wage subsidy to create new positions. Positions with 52 weeks of continuous employment will receive a bonus of $2,000 to the employer and $1,000 to the employee. This program is intended to promote sustainable long-term employment or seasonable employment by offsetting the costs associated with training and managing new employees.Grant Value: a maximum of 80% up to $13,440 wage subsidy + $2,000 completion bonusTurnaround Time: 20 daysEligible Employers:Be in Newfoundland and Labrador;For-profit and non-profit employers that are incorporated or sole proprietorships;Maintains a Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) business number; andBe in good standing with the Registry of Companies and Deeds.Note: Federal and provincial government departments, crown agencies and corporations, boards and commissions, municipalities, and political parties are ineligible for this program.Eligible Candidates:Be residents of Newfoundland and Labrador;Be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or person granted refugee status in Canada; ORBe an international graduate of Memorial University of College of the North Atlantic with a Post-Graduate Work Permit and a resident of the province;Be a recent post-secondary graduate;Be unemployed or underemployed (averages less than 20 hours per week or in a field unrelated to their training);Is not receiving any federal or provincial government pension, Workplace NL benefits or other benefits prescribed by the Minister.Note: Individuals on a temporary work permit are ineligible.Ineligible Candidates:Individuals on temporary work permits;Members of the immediate family of the employer; The aim is to accelerate the health science industry's use of critical technologies such as 5G and advanced networks, ethical artificial intelligence, blockchain, cybersecurity, quantum and robotics.Grant Value: Funding between $25,000 and $100,000 for strengthening technology commercialization; andFunding up to $250,000 for technology adoption.Turnaround Time: 2-4 weeks after EOI submission.Eligible Applicants: Be either a private health science company based in Ontario, or emerging venture with IP developed in Ontario;Focused on developing human health science products/services, including but not limited to medical devices, diagnostics, digital health, health IT and therapeutics;Working to develop, integrate or have integrated at least one critical technology (5G/advanced networks, ethical artificial intelligence, blockchain, cybersecurity, quantum, and/or robotics) into your products, services and/or opertaions; Committed to the creation and commercialization of made-in-Ontario IP.Eligible Expenses: Costs related to the project deliverables and milestones.Ineligible Expenses:Cost of goods;Publication;Conferences; and Overhead.Program Details:Project length up to 12 months;Program will require projects to have milestones;Funding will be required to be a 2:1 contribution; andApplications must be submitted by a member of the senior management team.Stream Eligibility:Stream 1: De-risking of emerging technologies and venture creation:Be either an emerging venture with intellectual property (IP) developed in Ontario, or an early stage, private health science SME based in Ontario;For emerging ventures, high potential for company creation with operation in Ontario;       Grant Criteria 
      This federal program offers wage subsidies to hire current post-secondary students part-time or full-time. Undergraduate students and graduate students are eligible to apply. Employers must be willing to provide a quality learning experience to a student and have the financial capacity to pay the student for the duration of the placement in full. Students from under-represented groups are eligible for a 70% subsidy up to a maximum of $7000, while others will be eligible for 50% subsidy up to a maximum of $5000. Grant Value:50% of wages up to a maximum of $5000; or 70% of wages up to a maximum of $7000 for students from any of the following under-represented groups:Women in STEM;Indigenous persons;Newcomers to Canada;Persons with disabilities;Visible minorities; andFirst-year students.Turnaround time: 20-25 business daysEligible Employer:Registered for-profit businesses;Not-for-profit organizations;Must have the capacity (financially and otherwise) to hire and supervise a student.Ineligible Employer:Post-secondary institutions, hospitals, and long-term care facilities;Non-secular institutions; Federal, provincial, territorial and municipal governments; andFinancial institutions: click here to see the list of ineligible financial sector employers.Eligible Candidates:Must be a current student enrolled (full-time or part-time) in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Graduate students (ie. Master's and  Doctoral students) are also eligible.Undertaking the work opportunity as a work-integrated learning experience in connection with a course, degree, certificate, or diploma;Mentorships, co-ops, internships, practicums, and applied research projects are all considered eligible work-integrated learning experiences;The WIL component may be optional or required by the student's program. It may be for credit or not for credit;Magnet will send a letter template to pre-approved applicants. The student can use the template to request the required letter from a representative of their post-secondary institution, such as the Office of the Registrar, Career and Co-op Office, or Dean's office;For non co-op placements the letter must be signed by the Associate Dean of the relevant faculty or Program Director if applicable.Must be Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, or persons with refugee protection legally entitled to work in their placement province; andInternational students are not eligible for the subsidy. Note: Only when the placement is considered "articling" would this be deemed ineligible (ie. student working towards their CPA, OBA, realtor license, etc)Program Details: Full-time or part-time positions;No maximum or minimum duration;Any industry and focus are accepted;Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between;Winter Semester 2025 (January 1 - March 31, 2024) - CLOSED.Summer Semester 2025 (May 1 to August 31, 2025) - CLOSEDFall Semester 2025 (September 1 - December 31, 2025) - Opening August 1, 2025.Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Back-to-back placements are eligible only if the participant has 2 separate co-op requirements from their post-secondary institution;The employer must provide on-the-job supervision; The employer must ensure student hires are placed on payroll and are not contractors;Work-integrated learning must be in the participant's study plan and span over the duration of the placement;Employers will have the flexibility to postpone placement start dates to avoid rescinding placements; Employers will be able to apply for funding before they finalize their selection of students to hire; andThe program provides 1 reimbursement payment at the end of the placement.Note: Placements can begin earlier and end later than the funded semester, however only the placement between the semester start dates and end dates are eligible for funding.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices: This grant cannot be combined with other federal wage subsidies. However, it can be combined with provincial tax credits, and with provincial, municipal, and/or territorial sources of funding, so long as total funding received does not exceed 100% of the gross wages paid to the student;If the student was funded by another federally funded program for a part of a semester, then the entire semester will be ineligible for the Magnet wage subsidy;The program will fund wages retroactively as far as as the start of the semester to which the subsidy applies;Process Best Practices:Applications are assessed on a first-come, first-served basis;Must provide students email address associated with their post-secondary institution as the program will send the student consent form directly to them, students must return the Student Consent Form from their student email;Proof of WIL eligibility letter must now be sent directly from the post secondary institution to the program to magnet@mail.outcomecampusconnect.ca with the application ID on the subject line; andIf you have trouble finding candidates relating to tech, you can check out our partners at Hatchways who have a pool of candidates and can assist with the hiring process here.Forms: Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The BC Manufacturing Job Fund provides funding of up to $10 million to manufacturers to conduct business/project planning as well as invest in new manufacturing infrastructure, technology, and processes. The program has 2 funding streams: the Project Readiness stream and the Capital Investment stream.  The intent of the program is to boost productivity, increase competitiveness and support clean and inclusive growth.Grant Value:Project Readiness stream: Up to 50% of eligible costs to a maximum of $50,000Capital Investment stream: Average of 20% of eligible costs to a maximum of $10,000,000Turnaround Time: 4 weeks after the initial proposalEligible Applicants:Registered for-profit manufacturing businesses in BC;Have established operations (at a proposed project location or elsewhere);Have an established employee base;Be in a viable financial position.Have a business plan and/or financial records demonstrating the ability to pay off short-term debts;Not in foreclosure or for sale;Paid taxes in the last fiscal year.Eligible Projects:Be located in B.C.;Contribute to long-term regional economic growth, sustainability, and/or diversity;Be financially viable and leverage market demand;Create, maintain, or diversify job opportunities for local workers;Have a high degree of readiness and bring direct benefits to communities; andDemonstrate alignment with program goals (see Best Practices section below).Eligible Expenses:Stream 1 - must be related to business and project planning to prepare for investment:Business plans;Market assessments;Operational plans;Financial plans and costing;Risk analyses; andOperational technical assessments.Stream 2 - must be essential to project delivery:Capital expenditures including equipment, machinery, technology, and construction materials;Wage or contract costs for net new and project-specific labour;Material transportation costs;Installation and implementation costs; andOther time-limited costs directly related to project implementation.Ineligible Expenses:Costs unrelated to the project;Operating costs (core staff salaries, bonuses, repayment loans, fines/penalties, etc.);Acquisition of land and existing buildings;With the exception of First Nations/Indigenous-owned enterprises acquiring or buying into existing manufacturing operations).Early research, concept development, scoping, prototyping, and feasibility studies (Technology Readiness Level 1-7); andCosts eligible for tax rebates and other rebates.Program Details:Stream 1 - Project Readiness StreamFocus on final-stage business, project planning, and operational & technical assessments;Early-stage R&D, concept development, and scoping are not eligible; andShould ideally begin the project within 3 months of funding approval.Stream 2 - Capital Investment StreamFocus on investing in new or renovated manufacturing equipment, infrastructure, technology, and processes;Projects must be initiated within 1 year of project approval; andApplicants in this stream will be asked to submit project documentation that outlines the project budget, and other potential and secured funding sources, and demonstrates project viability.Successful recipients of Stream 1 may apply for Stream 2 when ready;Receipt of Stream 1 funding does not guarantee approval through Stream 2.Process and timelines:Submit high-level proposal - 4-week turnaroundSubmit a detailed application - turnaround time will vary depending on the funding stream and complexity of the projectFunding Decision - within 12 weeks of the submission of the full application, depending on project complexity and applicant readinessFunding Agreement and project implementationSuccessful applicants will be required to report on progress and provide documentation throughout the term of the Agreement using templates provided by the program:Progress updates tied to funding release, including activities completed and progress made toward deliverables and program outcomes;Financial reports provide information to ensure funding is being applied to eligible costs;The final Report will describe the process, performance, outcomes, impacts, and key learning from the project.The program will prioritize projects that meet the following criteria:Projects within the forestry sector;Projects located in rural, remote, or forestry-dependent communities;Projects that have a high degree of readiness, need, and direct impact; andProjects that are Indigenous-led or benefit Indigenous peoples.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Market Readiness Program funds up to $250,000 to early-stage technology companies that are incorporated and are at the commercialization stage. Applicant companies will be evaluated based on the potential long-term competitiveness, value proposition, capacity to scale as well as strong Intellectual Property rights. The intent of the program is to attract additional private investment, support scalable business growth, and support innovation in Ontario.Grant Value:MR125 Stream: $125,000MR250 Stream: $250,000Turnaround Time: 3 monthsEligible Applicants:Be based in Ontario;Headquartered in the province and have at least 50% of the current company headcount in the province.Have been incorporated within the last 5 years;Have raised less than $1 million in third-party capital, excluding friends and family;Currently or previously affiliated with a university, college or research hospital campus linked accelerator or incubator, in Ontario;Be an early-stage technology company in sectors including, but not limited to:IT;Robotics;AI;Health technology;Cleantech; andAdvanced manufacturing.Has a minimum addressable market size of $100M;Has a product built;Have early market traction;Close to commercialization;Meet the stream specific eligibility criteria below:MR125 for $125,000 Investments:Be prepared to discuss the proposed terms of the current round which is being led by third party investors (Not OCE);Be past the internal beta design and development stages and work with prospective market customers to improve the offering;Be developing proprietary technology;Be defining its primary product/ market fit and establishing reasonable pricing models with a sales strategy/pipeline;Have a defined business model and financial forecasts (1-2 years); andBe raising sufficient investment to reach the next defined significant milestone(s).MR250 for $250,000 Investments:Have already raised a pre-seed or seed round and are looking for additional growth capital;Be advanced in their growth and sales strategy, showing early but consistent traction and a sales strategy that is repeatable and scalable;Have potential to redefine or disrupt a targeted industry (ie. strong IP and a differentiated offering);Be pivoting to target growth with higher momentum;Have a business model and financial forecasts (2-4 years); andHave milestones that drive a Seed extension or Series A round in the near-term future (1-2 years).Eligible Activities:Customer creation and development of scalable sales processes;Business model development activities; andInvestments for the round to be used for significant milestones for a runway up to 12 months.Program Details:Companies are reviewed through a rigorous internal pre-vetting process before being selected to proceed to an investment advisory committee for consideration;Due diligence documents will be evaluated by the IAC against assessment criteria, including:Product Offering: core value proposition, ability to address customer challenges, appropriateness of stage of development, and commercializationTarget Customers: identification and plan to access customers, willingness to pay, marketing strategyMarket and Competition: appropriateness and feasibility of the business model and pricing structure, plan to address competition and barriers to entry (e.g. regulatory), potential exit strategyTeam: ability and resources to achieve the milestones and deliver a repeatable sales processMilestones: suitability to grow customer base and/or attract follow-on investment, risk mitigation plan, clarity and feasibility of next stepsSuccessful companies must complete the following activation requirements within 30 days of investment approval:Execution of OCE’s standard funding agreement.Do not fill out this template. A copy of the agreement will be generated through AccessOCE and sent to the Company upon approval of the investment);Proof of Matching Funds: Please note that the proof of matching contribution in the form of a current bank statement (dated within 30 days approval notification) is required before the OCE investment can be released;Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT)/ Direct Deposit form and void cheque;Execution of OCE's standard Convertible Debenture or other financial instrument approved by OCE prior to submission; andCompany's profile.The program will not release any funds until the investment is activated;If for any reason the requirements for activation are not met within 30 days from the date of release of the approval notification, the investment offer may be retracted.Successful applicants will be required to provide:An annual investor update:With annual metrics survey each April for 5 years following investment date;A final report:Including progress, performance metrics, proof of expenditures, and a financial attestation;Be submitted within 30 days of completion of the milestones.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program helps to connect academic researchers with companies for collaborative research projects. The purpose of this program is to match companies with students studying at a Canadian college or university in order to create meaningful placements where the candidate can gain valuable work experience while providing research work that is relevant to the prosperity of the company. Grant Value:For 1 intern: 50% of wages up to $7,500 (employer must contribute $7,500)For 3 or more interns: ~45% of wages up to $13,333 (employers must contribute $6,000)Note: The minimum stipend for the intern must be at least $10,000.Turnaround Time: 6-8 weeksEligible Employer:For-profit or non-for-profit organization of any size within Canada;Municipalities;Hospitals;For-profit businesses operating in select Mitacs Partner countries.Eligible Candidates:Must be:Full-time students at a Canadian college or university;For Postdoctoral fellows, PhDs must have been granted no more than 5 years before the project’s start date, with exceptions available for extenuating circumstances such as parental leave or military service. Fellows must not have been employed full-time at the partner organization before applying.Full-time graduate students from select Mitacs partner countries;Recent graduates from a Canadian college or university, within two years of graduation.Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or international student over the age of 18; andMust not have more than 6 months of post-graduation work experience.Note: Current employees of the applicant employers are ineligible.Program Details:The internship must be at least 4-months in duration, possible to renew for graduate-level students;The internship must include at least one intern traveling to or from Canada, university, or partner organization that is based in Canada;Recent graduates:Must have status at the academic institution;Must start the internship within 2 years of graduation; andAre normally eligible for one 4-6-month internship but internships could be 3 months in duration depending on the needs of the project and the discretion of the academic institution.All research projects must demonstrate a viable economic or productivity orientation. Examples of research projects include (but not exclusive to):Creation of video games and apps for the purposes of being used in a festival;Development of a program to help stroke victims return to work;Research to better understand the impacts of blindness towards employment and working environments;The employer must provide on-the-job mentorship and support;Interns are required to spend at least 50% of their internship on site with the partner organization. In exceptional circumstances, interns may spend less than half of the internship with their partner;Any potential conflict of interest must be declared and mitigated.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best PracticesNon-for profit should contact a Mitacs representative to confirm eligibility;Process Best Practices:Proposal writing guide here;Get feedback from a Mitacs business development representative before submitting your final proposal;Proposals must be submitted at least 8 weeks prior to the intended start date of the internship for projects within Canada and at least 16 weeks prior for international projects.Forms: Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here

        February 11, 2026Fall Cohort applications are now open. Internship dates are September 14, 2026 – March 12, 2027.Application deadline (for employers and students): June 3, 2026 at 9:00 AM (PST).
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers up to a $7,500 wage subsidy to employers looking to hire interns for a 4-6-month part-time or full-time internship. Employers are able to recruit Masters of Business Administration or undergraduate students from Kwantlen University's School of Business in positions that address business strategy needs in relation to addressing organizational critical issues.Turnaround time: Up to 2 weeksGrant Value:$7,500 (with employers contributing $2,500) if the participant is aged 29 or younger at the start of the internship (part of RBC's youth contribution)$5,000 (with employers contributing $5,000) if the participant is aged 30 at the start of the internshipEligible Employers:Be one of the following organization types:For-profit businesses;Nonprofit organizations;Municipalities;Industrial associations;Charities;Foundations; andResearch centers.Employers must have the appropriate administrative support and capacity to train and mentor the participants to enhance and maximize the participants' experience;Contribute $2,500 (discounted stream) or $5,000 (regular stream) towards student stipend; andMust support the participants in the development and implementation of work activities to provide participants with a meaningful internship.Eligible Participants:Be a student at Kwantlen University's School of Business;Must be a current student and ready to graduate in the next 3 terms with a Bachelor's Degree, Post-Baccalaureate Diploma or Graduate Diploma;Now must be enrolled at KPU for at least 2 terms at the internship start date;Have a minimum GPA of 3.0;Valid work and study visa holders are eligible;Must reside in Canada at the time of application and during the internship placement;A local address and phone number are required.Be available to reside in Canada for the entire duration of the internship ;Not be actively enrolled or participating in a Co-op Program; andNot be a current, active participant in another Mitacs program.Internship Details:The position must be designed to address one or more business strategy components (i.e., marketing strategy, operations strategy, finance strategy, etc.);Should support the business community, provide real-world education, collaboration, and insights to the student;Placement duration: 4-6 months part-time or full-time with the possibility of extension for certain types of projects;Maximum placements per employer: 6;Kwantlen University to assist in and coordinate interviews;Employers cannot start candidates prior to application approval;There are no limits on the maximum number of placements per company;Participants will not be on payroll with the employer as Kwantlen University will pay the participants directly;Employers will only need to contribute $2,500 or $5,000 to start the placement.Participants will be paid by Kwantlen University on a bi-weekly or monthly basis;Have supervision from the Intern Host Organization as well as an academic supervisor from Kwantlen University; andEmployers will need to submit an exit survey and provide feedback on the placement experience.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:The program technically allows for funding to be used in conjunction with other wage subsidy programs. However, because the program pays participants directly, participants won't be on the employers payroll, making this program not easily stackable;This program cannot be applied retroactively, candidates must be approved before they can start their placement;Employers can make additional fund applications for multiple student hires;The initial invoice due from the employee to Mitacs must be paid by the employer directly (not a third party or other funder); andThe application online does not allow for saving. It is recommended to have the internship placement details and all responses prepared and saved separately before applying.Program Website: click hereApplication Form: click hereMitacs Registration & Application Portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Music Company program is to help support the growth of B.C.'s music industry by providing funding up to $60,000. This program supports the sustainability, growth, and capacity of B.C.'s music companies, through investing in business development activities. Grant Value: $2,000 to $60,000 or up to 50% of expenses.Turnaround Time: Approximately 14 weeks after the program deadline date.Eligible Applicants:Companies with primary business activities in the music industry, such as record labels, music publishers, artist managers, record producers, recording studios, etc.;Companies from a related sector, proposing a multimedia, cross-sector, or technology project that has direct implications for B.C.’s music industry.The applicant company must be:B.C. corporation, B.C. registered business, or sole proprietorship with a valid GST number, that files B.C. tax returns;Canadian corporation with operations in B.C. that files B.C. tax returns; orB.C. or Canadian not-for-profit organization with headquarters in B.C.Ineligible Applicants:Companies that primarily exist to benefit one artist or client. Artist-entrepreneurs are not eligible for this program and must apply for funding through the Career Development program; andCompanies that primarily exist to present live music are ineligible for this program and must apply for funding through the Live Music program.Eligible Activities:New jobs and staff growth;Improvements to business processes, policies, and procedures;Expanded company marketing initiatives;Development of knowledge and skills;Capital infrastructure improvements;Researching, developing, and testing new technology, products, or revenues streams;Sustainability initiatives and environmentally friendly business practices; andEstablishment of new business operations or satellite offices in B.C. Eligibile Expenses:Salaries and benefits for new or expanded company staff positions, including paid internships and apprenticeships, with a plan for how the positions will be sustained after the funding has been used; Training, courses, and consultants to grow knowledge, build processes, and develop skills for employees in a specific area; Training, planning, and policy development related to communicable disease plans, emergency preparedness, risk assessment, respectful workplace, accessibility, equity and inclusion, etc.; Marketing and advertising campaigns; Green initiatives such as eco-friendly power sources, energy-efficient renovations and products, reduction of physical waste or emissions, and other expenses related to creating a more sustainable business; Equipment purchases and upgrades for software, hardware, gear, technology, accessibility, etc.; Construction, building materials, and any other costs related to renovations or infrastructure improvements; GST for applicants who do not have GST accounts; and Existing resources directly related to the project to support a portion of the projectIneligible Expenses:Costs and initiatives associated with a particular artist;Costs related to the presentation of live music;Receptions, mixers, networking events, luncheons, award shows, fundraisers, galas, and parties;Capital purchases not specific to the project;Operating costs not specific to the project, including rent, utilities, regular maintenance, corporate overhead, or salaries;Subscriptions, membership fees, or recurring expenses prior to this project;Expenses paid in cash;In-kind expenses or donated services;Grant writing fees, legal fees, management fees, business registration fees, or fees for financial statements; Major expenses not included in the approved budget and incurred prior to Creative BC approval; andConference and business travel fees.Program Details:Grant varies from $2,000 to $60,000 for up to 50% of budgeted cash expenditures;Program activities and related expenses incurred must be between January 1, 2024 and June 30, 2025;Successful applicants will receive a 75% advance payment with the remaining 25% being funded upon completion of the final report;Applications will be evaluated by Creative BC staff and a panel of industry professionals representing a variety of music companies, industry backgrounds, regions, and demographics; andProjects are required to be completed as well as a final report detailing the impact of funding by June 30, 2025.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Best Practices:This program is stackable with other provincial funding however it cannot equal to more than 75% of the project budget; andCreative BC encourages applications from underrepresented groups, including Indigenous Peoples (First Nations [Status/Non-Status], Métis, and Inuit), Black, People of Colour, People living with one or more Disability, 2SLGBTQIA+ communities, and other groups who experience systemic barriers to participation.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereProgram Guidelines: click here

grants.grant_criteria: The New Entrant Farm Business Accelerator Program supports beginning farmers and ranchers in British Columbia by providing up to $15,000 in cost-shared funding (covering up to 75% of eligible project costs) to help develop business plans, implement farm infrastructure, and accelerate the growth and financial viability of new agricultural enterprises. The aim of this program is to enable new entrants to strengthen business management capacity, improve productivity, and transition their operations toward long-term commercial success within B.C.’s agri-food sector.
grants.best_practices: Eligible Best Practices :Applicants can combine this program funding with other government cost-share programs up to a maximum of 75% of total eligible project costs;The program does not provide retroactive funding for expenses incurred before the contribution agreement is signed;Applicants should:Be new entrants who have reported farm income for five years or fewer;Demonstrate a clear business concept with potential for long-term commercial viability;Possess or plan to develop a comprehensive business plan and marketing strategy;Show readiness to invest in on-farm infrastructure, equipment, or technology that improves productivity and profitability;Contribute a minimum of 25% of total project costs through cash or in-kind resources;Maintain a valid Business Registration Number and Premises ID;\Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee funding approval;Funding may only be used for projects that align with program objectives and are completed within the approved timeframe.Process Best Practices :Applications are reviewed on a merit basis, considering project feasibility, financial capacity, and potential for business growth and economic impact within B.C.’s agriculture sector;Applicants are encouraged to apply well in advance of their planned project start date, as costs incurred prior to approval will not be eligible;Approved applicants must complete projects within the designated Phase 1 or Phase 2 timelines;Funding is reimbursed upon project completion and submission of required documentation;Projects are monitored for compliance, and applicants may be asked to provide proof of expenditures, progress updates, and results achieved.

      Grant Criteria 
      The New Entrant Farm Business Accelerator Program supports beginning farmers and ranchers in British Columbia by providing up to $15,000 in cost-shared funding (covering up to 75% of eligible project costs) to help develop business plans, implement farm infrastructure, and accelerate the growth and financial viability of new agricultural enterprises. The aim of this program is to enable new entrants to strengthen business management capacity, improve productivity, and transition their operations toward long-term commercial success within B.C.’s agri-food sector.Grant Value:Phase 1 – Business Planning: Up to $3,000 (consultant-assisted) or $1,250 (self-developed);Phase 2 – Implementation: Up to $15,000 (75% reimbursement).Turnaround Time: Approximately 25–30 business days.Eligible Applicants:Individuals or farm businesses located and operating in British Columbia;Have reported farm income to the Canada Revenue Agency for five years or fewer (or none to date);Intend to operate a commercial, for-profit agricultural enterprise;Possess or plan to acquire a valid Business Registration Number and Premises ID;Have not received funding from the program in a previous intake;Be in good standing with the B.C. Ministry of Agriculture and Food.Eligible Activities:Development of a business plan or market strategy;Investment in on-farm infrastructure, equipment, or technology that supports productivity and efficiency;Adoption of financial, production, or marketing systems that enhance growth and profitability;Projects that demonstrate readiness to scale operations and generate sustainable farm income.Eligible Expenses:Consultant or advisory fees for business planning;Costs of infrastructure materials and equipment purchases;Labour and professional services directly tied to approved projects;Marketing and branding activities associated with farm expansion;Other direct project expenses pre-approved by the Ministry.Program Details:Applicants must contribute a minimum of 25% of total eligible project costs;All projects must be completed within program timelines;Funding is reimbursed after project completion and submission of required documentation;Projects must align with program objectives of business growth, economic sustainability, and local food system development;Administered by the B.C. Ministry of Agriculture and Food under the Sustainable Agriculture Strategy.

      Eligible Best Practices :Applicants can combine this program funding with other government cost-share programs up to a maximum of 75% of total eligible project costs;The program does not provide retroactive funding for expenses incurred before the contribution agreement is signed;Applicants should:Be new entrants who have reported farm income for five years or fewer;Demonstrate a clear business concept with potential for long-term commercial viability;Possess or plan to develop a comprehensive business plan and marketing strategy;Show readiness to invest in on-farm infrastructure, equipment, or technology that improves productivity and profitability;Contribute a minimum of 25% of total project costs through cash or in-kind resources;Maintain a valid Business Registration Number and Premises ID;\Meeting the eligibility criteria does not guarantee funding approval;Funding may only be used for projects that align with program objectives and are completed within the approved timeframe.Process Best Practices :Applications are reviewed on a merit basis, considering project feasibility, financial capacity, and potential for business growth and economic impact within B.C.’s agriculture sector;Applicants are encouraged to apply well in advance of their planned project start date, as costs incurred prior to approval will not be eligible;Approved applicants must complete projects within the designated Phase 1 or Phase 2 timelines;Funding is reimbursed upon project completion and submission of required documentation;Projects are monitored for compliance, and applicants may be asked to provide proof of expenditures, progress updates, and results achieved.Links :Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The On-Farm Value-Added grant program offers funding of up to $250,000 to support primary producers in adding value to their agricultural products to grow sales, expand production capacity, explore market opportunities and create jobs in Alberta.Grant Value:Stream A: Up to $50,000;Stream B: Up to $250,000.Turnaround Time: 2-3 monthsEligible Applicants: Be a primary producer;Be an individual or corporation registered in Alberta and operating in Alberta;Be responsible for input costs for crops, bees or livestock;Produce at least $25,000 worth of commercial agriculture production annually;Not be a landlord whose only interest in crop, bee, cattle operation is ownership of the land; andBe adding value past harvest or slaughter of the agricultural product. An applicant that has an active application to the On-Farm Value-Added Program or Emerging OpportunitiesIneligible Applicants: Processors;Industry organizations;Applied research organizations;Post-secondary institutions;Federal, provincial, and municipal governments agencies and institutions;Retail businesses, restaurants and food establishments; andAny other person deemed by the Minister to be ineligible.Eligible Activities: Applicants may apply for funding under one of the following:Processing Capacity Expansion;Food Safety Improvement;New Product and Process Development; andMarket Development and Access.Ineligible Activities: Activities related to cleaning, bagging, handling and/or storing of primary products;Construction of walls, floors, ceilings, or ancillary buildings;Labels and packaging design that is not in relation to new products or for new markets;Advertising;Promotions;Activities associated with aquaculture, aquaponics, or seafood processing, with the exception of actitivies related to the international marketing of fish and seafood products which are eligible and may be included in the application; andActivities that provide support for province-specific branding, promotion or marketing activities that are detrimental to another province or territory.Eligible Expenses: 25% of eligible capital expenses are covered by the program and the remainder by the applicant;50% of eligible non-capital expenses are covered by the program and the remainder by the applicant;Eligible expenses vary depending on which area the applicant is applying underProcessing Capacity Expansion:Eligible Capital Expenses:Processing Equipment;Food Safety Equipment;Software systems to assist in processing;Third party engineering related to purchase, and configuration of eligible equipment.NOTE: Leased equipment is ineligible.Eligible Non-Capital Expenses: Training costs associated with adopting new technologies, new equipment and/or new automation processes as related to processing.Food Safety Improvement:Eligible Non-Capital Expenses:Development and implementation of a food safety system;Training costs associated with adopting new technologies, new equipment and/or new food safety food processes related to food safety improvement.New Product and Process Development:Eligible Non-Capital Expenses:Sensory and shelf-life testing;Validation of nutritional or health claims;Attribute identification;Environmental product declaration;Non-food product regulation studies;Scale-up trials;Formulation development, including ingredient costs for trials;Process improvement;First run of labels and/or package printing used for new product launch to a max of 2500 units per new product; andFirst-time brand design and development. Market Development and Access:Eligible Non-Capital Expenses:Feasibility studies;Market readiness assessments;Marketing and export plans for local, domestic, or international market opportunities;Design of market support materials for new product and new market launch;Capital investment strategy development;First-time certification audit;Development of initial online presence for the purpose of e-commerce, including translation for new markets;Enhancement and expansion of an online marketing/sales platform;In-store or in-market product demonstrations, excluding the cost of product samples and shipping, and Trade shows and conference registration fees for events directly related to accessing new markets and/or launch of new products (max of two people per event) virtual events are included.Ineligible Expenses: Travel expenses not in compliance with the Travel Expense Policy;Expenses not incurred by the Eligible Applicant in carrying out the Eligible Activity;Installation and labour costs;Shipping and commissioning costs for equipment;Costs of lease of office furniture, space and equipment;Fixture that are not an eligible capital expense;Costs of equipment for storage purposes, not directly related to the eligible activity;Costs associated with the building such as plumbing, framing, flooring, electrical and insulation;On-going business operational activities and overhead expenses;Staff or consulting expenses for product sale activities, or in market representation for existing products;Advertising expenses;Sponsorship;Donation of product;Listing dess, distribution fees or shelf stocking fees;Website hosting, domain registration or ongoing website maintenance;Vehicles of any kind; andGoods and Services Tax.Program Details: Project activities can take place between January 1, 2025 and March 15, 2026;Funding is granted on a case-by-case basis and not on a first come, first served basis;The eligible applicant will also be required to submit a final report to the Minister;Additional reports may be requested throughout the project duration;Stream A application must include: A completed application form, signed by an authorized representative, and all documents required to be submitted pursuant to that form;Quotations or invoices for capital expenses over $10,000; andAny additional supplementary documentation requested by the Minister.Stream B application must include:A completed application form, signed by an authorized representative, and all documents required to be submitted pursuant to that form;Documents to demonstrate the applicant has the necessary capacity to complete the activities included in the applications; andAny additional supplementary documentation requested by the Minister.

andMust have a manufacturing location in Ontario by the time the project starts.Eligible Projects:Must focus on 1 or both elements:Advancing production cycle management and capabilities;Improving competitiveness and/or supporting the design, engineering or manufacture of new products through the adoption of advanced technologies (hardware, software) and/or training.Operational efficiency and competitiveness improvements through the adoption of Lean Manufacturing practices.Adoption of advanced technology may be part of the overall project scope.Align with O-AMP’s goals:Including economic gains, business improvements, and operational improvements (e.g., cost savings, increase in revenue, and contributions to regional and/or automotive sector development).Be no more than 2 years in duration.Eligible Expenses:Capital costs;Including equipment, testing tools, software, and instruments.Training costs;Including staff hours charged by non-management employees and sub-contractor/consultant fees (must be associated with LEAN Mentorship/specialized expertise related to LEAN).Salaries and benefits; andIncremental salary and benefits for employees of the company working on the project activities, to a maximum specified in the funding agreement with the Ministry (position and employment status must be specified);Hourly wages for training for employees who are not part of the company management team;External third-party training provider costs; andSalaries and benefits must only be claimed in proportion to the amount of time spent working directly on project activities.Travel and living costs.Transportation and accommodation costs that are exclusively project-related and use the most economical option (economy fare and standard hotel rooms).Ineligible Expenses:Management salaries, including any activity related to managing the project;Tax expenses;Ongoing operations including maintenance;Acquisitions and buyouts of another business;Insurance;Cost for research and development;Costs not directly associated with meeting the deliverables and milestones as specified in the funding agreement with the Ministry;Cost of basic utility services;Tangible capital costs such as, but not limited to, land, buildings, vehicles, equipment such as storage cabinets, tool cribs, forklifts, shelving, tooling, telephones, carts, and any other equipment that is not related to technology adoption;Meals and entertainment costs, gifts, and alcoholic beverages;Any travel costs that are not the most economical option.Program Details:The company shall be required to maintain signed timesheets or appropriate records for all employees working directly on the project;Hourly wages used for the staff hours being expensed must be stated in the supporting documentation.Interim reports, including the progress of the project, proof of expenditures, and a request for disbursement must be submitted halfway through the project;A successful applicant must submit its final report within 30 days of project completion in order to be reimbursed for expenses incurred for eligible project costs.
