grants.grant_criteria: This program provides funding of up to $5,000,000 to for-profit Ontario businesses undertaking projects that respond to U.S. trade disruptions. Funding supports initiatives that strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity, reshore production, or diversify export markets. The program is intended to help businesses mitigate risks caused by tariffs, supply chain instability, and protectionist trade measures.Grant Value:Business Projects:Interest-Free Loans for up to 75% of eligible project costs, to a maximum of $5,000,000 per project; andLoan Forgiveness: Up to 30% of the loan (max $1,500,000) may be forgiven if the project meets defined investment and job creation targets.Grants are available for qualifying applicants but are assessed on a case-by-case basis based on project impact and regional needs.Turnaround Time: Approximately 45 business days.Eligible Applicants:Business Projects:Must be for-profit and incorporated in Ontario;Must have a minimum of 3 years in operation with financial statements;Must employ at least 5 full-time employees in Ontario;Must be able to demonstrate economic harm caused by U.S. trade disruptions, such as tariffs or export barriers; andProjects must have a minimum eligible cost of $200,000.Ineligible applicants :Not-for-profit organizations/associations/charities;Sole proprietors;Retail;Construction companies providing primary construction services (production of construction products is eligible);Providers of personal services; andConsulting firms.Eligible Projects:Projects must demonstrate how they will enhance domestic resilience and competitiveness by:Expanding domestic manufacturing or processing capacity;Reshoring or onshoring key operations previously outsourced abroad;Diversifying into new export markets or supply chain routes; andIntroducing equipment, technology, or facility upgrades to support these objectives.Ineligible projects :Ongoing operations including maintenance and capital replacement (exact replacements are not eligible, upgraded technology/equipment would be considered eligible);Refinancing of existing business operations;Acquisitions and buyout;Restructuring, or relocating to other jurisdictions within Ontario;Electricity projects;Waste management/primary recycling; andHospitality projects (hotels and restaurants).Eligible Expenses:Capital equipment and advanced manufacturing technology;Facility upgrades and retrofits;Labour and training costs directly related to project implementation;Consulting or third-party expertise required to complete the project; andDomestic market entry or export diversification costs.Please see program guidelines for details on eligible and ineligible costs.Program Details:Projects may be up to 4 years in length, with funding disbursed over multiple fiscal years;Applicants must complete an eligibility self-assessment and connect with a program advisor before submitting a full application;Applications must be submitted through Transfer Payment Ontario (TPON);A complete application includes:Eligibility checklist;Project plan and detailed budget;Financial statements (minimum 3 years);Articles of Incorporation and corporate structure; andSupporting documents outlining trade impact and job creation potential.
grants.best_practices: Eligible Best Practices:This program does not provide retroactive funding. Only costs incurred after the project start date identified in the Funding Agreement will be considered eligible;This program may be stackable with other non-provincial funding sources, including federal programs, but cannot be combined with other Ontario provincial funding streams for the same project expenses.Process Best Practices:Applicants must complete the online eligibility self-assessment and consult with an Ontario Advisor before being invited to apply;Proposed projects will be assessed according to the following criteria:Potential to strengthen domestic supply chains and reduce reliance on trade-impacted inputs;Jobs created, retained, or enhanced (including quality and long-term impact);Demonstrated impact of U.S. trade disruption on the business and the proposed solution’s effectiveness;Overall project feasibility, including financial capacity, operational readiness, and alignment with program goals.

The program is intended to help businesses mitigate risks caused by tariffs, supply chain instability, and protectionist trade measures.Grant Value:Business Projects:Interest-Free Loans for up to 75% of eligible project costs, to a maximum of $5,000,000 per project; andLoan Forgiveness: Up to 30% of the loan (max $1,500,000) may be forgiven if the project meets defined investment and job creation targets.Grants are available for qualifying applicants but are assessed on a case-by-case basis based on project impact and regional needs.Turnaround Time: Approximately 45 business days.Eligible Applicants:Business Projects:Must be for-profit and incorporated in Ontario;Must have a minimum of 3 years in operation with financial statements;Must employ at least 5 full-time employees in Ontario;Must be able to demonstrate economic harm caused by U.S. trade disruptions, such as tariffs or export barriers; andProjects must have a minimum eligible cost of $200,000.Ineligible applicants :Not-for-profit organizations/associations/charities;Sole proprietors;Retail;Construction companies providing primary construction services (production of construction products is eligible);Providers of personal services; andConsulting firms.Eligible Projects:Projects must demonstrate how they will enhance domestic resilience and competitiveness by:Expanding domestic manufacturing or processing capacity;Reshoring or onshoring key operations previously outsourced abroad;Diversifying into new export markets or supply chain routes; andIntroducing equipment, technology, or facility upgrades to support these objectives.Ineligible projects :Ongoing operations including maintenance and capital replacement (exact replacements are not eligible, upgraded technology/equipment would be considered eligible);Refinancing of existing business operations;Acquisitions and buyout;Restructuring, or relocating to other jurisdictions within Ontario;Electricity projects;Waste management/primary recycling; andHospitality projects (hotels and restaurants).Eligible Expenses:Capital equipment and advanced manufacturing technology;Facility upgrades and retrofits;Labour and training costs directly related to project implementation;Consulting or third-party expertise required to complete the project; andDomestic market entry or export diversification costs.Please see program guidelines for details on eligible and ineligible costs.Program Details:Projects may be up to 4 years in length, with funding disbursed over multiple fiscal years;Applicants must complete an eligibility self-assessment and connect with a program advisor before submitting a full application;Applications must be submitted through Transfer Payment Ontario (TPON);A complete application includes:Eligibility checklist;Project plan and detailed budget;Financial statements (minimum 3 years);Articles of Incorporation and corporate structure; andSupporting documents outlining trade impact and job creation potential.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program does not provide retroactive funding. Only costs incurred after the project start date identified in the Funding Agreement will be considered eligible;This program may be stackable with other non-provincial funding sources, including federal programs, but cannot be combined with other Ontario provincial funding streams for the same project expenses.Process Best Practices:Applicants must complete the online eligibility self-assessment and consult with an Ontario Advisor before being invited to apply;Proposed projects will be assessed according to the following criteria:Potential to strengthen domestic supply chains and reduce reliance on trade-impacted inputs;Jobs created, retained, or enhanced (including quality and long-term impact);Demonstrated impact of U.S. trade disruption on the business and the proposed solution’s effectiveness;Overall project feasibility, including financial capacity, operational readiness, and alignment with program goals.Forms :Program Website: click hereProgram Guidelines: click here

The intent of the program is to improve on-farm efficiency, food safety and environmental sustainability.Grant Value:Up to 85% of eligible costs for Youth ProducersUp to 70% of eligible costs for regular applicantsTurnaround Time: 100 business daysEligible Applicants:Be one of the following:Chicken producers;Turkey producers;Turkey breeders;Egg producers; andBroiler hatching egg producers.Be an individual and/or legal entity capable of entering into legally binding agreements or contracts;Have held quota/shares of provincial production on January 1, 2021;Be one of the following types:Poultry and/or egg producers holding quota;Poultry and/or egg producers licensed, or equivalent, by a provincial marketing agency;Atlantic Canada Hatching Egg Producers; andPoultry and/or egg producers under new entrants programs with loaned quota and/or whole-farm leases with loaned quota at the time of the calculation.Eligibility for Young Producer:Is 35 years old or younger on January 1, 2021;Is actively engaged in farming in Canada;Is either:A majority owner:Is a sole proprietor;Has majority ownership or more than 50% of the business;Led by a young producer who has:Managed the business for more than 2 years;Is working towards acquisition/successionHas an active role in strategic decision-making;Be a child's spouse or grandchild of the majority; andBe currently developing or has developed a succession plan to acquire the farm.Eligible Activities:Meet 1 or more of the following objectives:Increasing efficiency or productivity;Improving on-farm food safety and biosecurity;Improving environmental sustainability;Responding to consumer preferences (improving animal welfare, adopting alternative housing systems, transitioning to organic production, etc.)Examples include but are not limited to:The hiring of external expertise;Construction of new infrastructure or expansion of infrastructure;Building retrofits;Purchasing equipment;Shipping and installation of eligible assets, equipment, and materials; andTraining related to other eligible project activities.Eligible Expenses:Capital assets;Contracted services;Salaries and benefits quota/production on January 1, 2021, as identified by the respective provincial marketing board;Applicants must register with the program prior to the application submission here;Applicants with       Grant Criteria 
      This provincial program provides up to $10,000 for for-profit food and beverage businesses in Saskatchewan developing new or improved products that use Canadian-grown agricultural inputs.Grant Value:50% of eligible costs between $1,000 to $10,000 per project.Turnaround Time: Approximately 5 business days.Eligible Applicants:Agriculture value-added processors who meet the following criteria:A value-added product is defined as the upgrading of a raw primary agricultural product(s), or further upgrading of a processed product or derivative (includes co-product, by-product) into a new product;Processors must use an identifiable portion of inputs originating from primary agricultural commodities grown or raised in Canada;Operations and tax payments must be within the Province of Saskatchewan; andApplicants must be for-profit organizations.Eligible Activities:Technical service costs;Product development and demo costs;Test processing costs;Assessment and development of process & manufacturing technology costs; andSpecification development costs.NOTE:  Activities must be conducted at a third party facility and/or by a contracted service provider:Ineligible Activities:Activities already receiving funding from other Government of Saskatchewan sources or the Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada Agri-Marketing program;Training and wages/salaries for employees;Expenses for ongoing activities or other typical operating expenses;Per diems and meals domestically and internationally;Equipment purchases or other capital expenditures not explicitly identified as eligible;Administration costs and other activities not directly related specifically to the project;Cost of production for saleable products;Taxes, legal fees, and/or financing fees; andMembership in trade organizations.Program Details:Applications are accepted on a rolling basis and reviewed first-come, first-served;Only one PDP project can be active per business at a time;The proposal/product must demonstrate substantial use of Canadian-grown agricultural products; The program is part of a $5 million investment under the Sustainable Canadian Agricultural Partnership running until 2028;Projects must demonstrate commercial potential, include Canadian-grown inputs, and align with the goals of value-added food or beverage product development;The main objectives of the program include:Increase Value-Added Revenues;Enhance Value-Added Processing of Canadian Agriculture Products;Foster the Development of New Value-Added Products, Prototypes, and Processes;Reduce By-Product Waste; andExpand and Nurture Value-Added Businesses.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program allows stacking with other provincial or federal funding sources, provided the combined total of government assistance does not exceed 75% of eligible project costs; All sources of funding must be disclosed at the time of application and during final reporting; The program does not fund projects retroactively—costs incurred before formal approval are ineligible.Process Best Practices:Applicants must complete the Prospective Client Form and receive confirmation from the Saskatchewan Food Centre before starting any project work;Any changes to the project scope, timeline, or budget must be communicated to the Food Centre promptly for potential amendment and continued eligibility.Forms : Program Website : click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Project Development Fund will provide funding for the development of independent film and television productions, on a project-by-project basis, in the form of a non-recoupable development advance. Applications will be evaluated on a first-come, first-served basis until the budget has been fully designated for the fiscal year. Funding is based on a commitment from an eligible triggering agent. Grant Value: Up to $50000Note: The program does not take equity in any of the projects.Turnaround Time: 8 weeks.Eligible Applicants:Must be a company incorporated in British Columbia or Canada with its head office in British Columbia. A majority of the issued common voting shares must be held by BC residents;The applicant company may own 10% or less of the shares of a broadcaster;The applicant company may have 10% of its shares owned by a broadcaster or by a distributor;100% of the copyright of the project being developed must be owned, optioned, or controlled by the applicant; and,The market trigger must be at arm's length from the applicant company.Eligible Triggering Agents:Eligible applicants may apply to Creative BC for a total non-recoupable development advance of up to 50% of the committed cash amount from one of more of the following Triggering Agents for the development of an eligible project An arm’s length bona fide distribution entity (Canadian and international distributors);National Film Board of Canada (NFB co-productions only; 100% owned and controlled NFB productions are not eligible); A licensed public or private broadcaster (Canadian and international broadcasters);Over the top (OTT) subscription-based services (Netflix, Crave, Amazon, Hulu, YouTube Premium originals, Vimeo On-Demand originals);Telus Originals (Small Program Production Agreement);Bell Fund Slate Development; and Telefilm Canada Feature Film Fund (CFFF) Development Program.Eligible Projects:Feature films, destined for theatrical release (live action or animated);Televisions movies, pilots, televisions series and mini-series (live action, animated, variety, human interest, lifestyle and performing arts and entertainment);Short films and web series (live action or animated) (Limit of 10 short films and web series during fiscal year); andDocumentaries and docudramas for television broadcast or theatrical release.Eligible Expenses:Acquisitions of rights including option payments and license fees for platforms or formats;Research including the creation of a report, bible, outline and/or treatment; Writing of script stage including editing and various breakdowns (i.e. outline, treatment, first draft, second draft, final draft and polish and applicable fringes);Production of a demo-tape including, but not limited to, creation of a sizzle reel, presentation pilot, webisode or storyboards;Creation of a character model pack (for animated projects);Polishing, packaging, and a casting phase including creation of a casting reel;Travel costs necessary for creative work (e.g. interviewing, demo-taping and travel by/to/from the director); andAudience Development and Community Outreach Plan. Program Details:The program has an application submission fee of $105:Total development funding available to each eligible applicant(including affiliated related companies) may not exceed $50,000 in the fiscal year 2023/24;The total development funding available to an eligible project for the fiscal year 2023/24 is capped at $10,000;Except for television series, which include dramatic, animated, lifestyle, or documentary, which are capped at $20,000; and,The maximum 3 cumulative funding an eligible project can receive throughout its development history is $30,000, except for television series which are capped at $50,000;Eligible applicants must have a written agreement with one or more of the Triggering Agents confirming their commitment
to provide a development advance for the eligible project;Applications must be submitted to Creative BC no later than 30 days after the date that the BC applicant receives the letter of commitment or agreement with the Triggering Agent.Exceptions to the 30 days may be given. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:If a producer should receive funding from Telefilm’s CFFF Development Program above the $30,000 threshold for one project, they are not eligible to apply for the Telefilm Development Top-Up for that project; The program is not retroactive.Process Best Practices:Applications must be submitted to Creative BC no later than 30 days after the date that the applicant receives the letter or commitment or agreement with the Triggering Agent.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication form: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      Proof-of-concept plans for trials and demonstrations that are intended to exhibit the commercial feasibility of biologically-derived natural products or technologies may be granted up to 40% funding to a maximum of $350,000. The aim of this program is to prove the commercial feasibility of these products and technologies in order to minimize risk and advance future investment in the natural products sector. Grant Value: 40% of eligible project costs to a maximum of $350,000Turnaround Time: 2 monthsEligible Applicants:Canadian start-ups or SMEs:Must have the potential to achieve 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period; andSole proprietors are ineligible.Research institutes:Products or technologies must address an industry or sector challenge with significant market potential; andNo limit on number of employees.Be a member of Canada’s Natural Product Innovation Cluster;Have a novel pre-commercial (Technology Readiness Levels(TRL) 4-9) 'natural product or technology';Defined as a biologically-based innovation that benefit people, animals and the planet, and can be applied to a range of industries, including: Food production and value-added agriculture; Bioproducts and sustainability; Human nutrition, health and wellness; Animal health and nutrition; and Water and waste management.Have potential for: Achieving 10MM- 15MM in annual revenue within a market-reasonable period;Significant economic, social, health and/or environmental benefits;Commercialization in Canada;Spillover benefits to more than one sector;Improving the representation of women, visible minorities, and Indigenous peoples in the natural products ecosystem.Eligible Activities:Animal, field, demonstration, or human trials;Late-stage trials for naturals products, services, or technologies that derive from a biological source; andCommercial demonstration trials.Ineligible Activities:Basic research or preliminary product/technology development;Pharmaceutical trials; andTrials that are not biological in nature.Eligible Expenses:Direct materials;Direct Labour;Subcontractors/consultants;Equipment (up to 10% of budget);Other direct costs (e.g. trial participant costs and some specialized software);Indirect costs up to ~15% of costs.Program Details:The project period cannot exceed 18 months; Applicants required to contribute 60% of project costs unless leveraging other government grant funding;Contract with NPC will include project scope, reporting requirements, and key milestones to be achieved;Applications will be reviewed by NPC staff, board members, and an external industry expert on a monthly basis;Disbursement of funds takes place through reimbursement of eligible project costs upon approval of quarterly reports;Includes a written and financial claim containing invoices and proof of payment.Annual reporting required for 5 years following program period; andFor research institutes, projects must be aimed at moving a product or technology from intellectual property disclosure to near-term spin-out and/or licensing opportunities.Evaluation Criteria: The novelty of the natural product or technology; Market opportunity; Business model/commercialization strategy;Competitors; Strength of the management team/research leadership team;Need and impact of the trial; Trial design and key activities; Qualifications of the individuals and/or centres conducting the trials; and Risk mitigation.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides a wage subsidy of up to 70% to a maximum of $7,000 to employers in the tourism and hospitality sector that hire post-secondary students for full-time or part-time placements. The goal of the program is to create employment and skills development opportunities that  benefit both students and employers.Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5,000;70% of wages up to $7000 for students from the following underrepresented groups:Women in STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics);Indigenous students;Visible minorities; Newcomers to Canada (immigrated to Canada within the last 5 years);Persons with disabilities; andFirst year students. Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Employers:Registered Canadian businesses, startups, and not-for-profits related to the tourism and hospitality sector; andI.e. accommodations, food and beverage services, culinary, recreation, entertainment, culture, events, transportation, travel services, etc.Must provide a work-integrated learning opportunity for the student.Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial, territorial, and municipal governments;Crown corporations, hospitals, public long-term care facilities, and post-secondary institutions; andMembers the House of Commons and/or Senate.Eligible Candidate:Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or has refugee status;Registered at a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution in a program that includes a work-integrated learning component;Undergraduate or graduate student;Full- or part-time student; andLegally entitled to work in Canada.Ineligible Candidate:International students; andImmediate family members, unless a clear, transparent, and fair nepotism policy is in place.Peogram Details:Applications are being accepted for placements in the following semesters:Winter 2025 (January 1, 2025 to April 30, 2025): CLOSEDSummer 2025 (May 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025): CLOSEDFall 2025 (September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025): OPENThe work experience must coincide with a course, degree, certificate, diploma, or other recognized program offered by the student's institution;The student will need to provide proof of enrolment (e.g. a letter from a registrar) in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Ideally, the document will also demonstrate that the student’s program includes a work-integrated-learning component.Eligible placement types include:Co-op placements;Internships;Practicums;Mentorships;Field placements; and Applied projects.Placement can be full-time or part-time;Minimum 20 hours per week;4-15 weeks per semester;On-site, remote, or hybrid allowed; Participants must be placed on payroll; Students hired as independent contractors are not eligible for the subsidy;Placements must not displace an existing worker or fill a role left vacant due to a labour dispute;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Apprenticeships that are part of the designated trades governed by regulations under the Provincial and Territorial Apprenticeship Acts (Red Seal Trades) are not eligible for the wage subsidy.

Eligible activities include hiring a market development specialist, obtaining necessary certifications, developing a commercialization strategy, and registering trademarks in Quebec.Grant Value: Up to 50% of eligible costs, with a maximum contribution of $250,000 per company per year;Mandatory private contribution: at least 25% of the total project cost.Turnaround Time: Approximately  4–6 weeks from submission to decision.Eligible Applicants:Québec‑based for‑profit businesses or cooperatives with annual sales under $100 million;Applicants must intend to integrate into Québec supply chains or public purchasing networks.Eligible Activities:Hiring market development specialists or commercial reps;Developing marketing or commercialization strategies;Conducting market analysis or securing certifications;Trademark registration in Québec;Implementing inventory or order management systems.Eligible Expenses :Professional fees; Including, where applicable, travel and accommodation expenses for specialized services (such as subcontracted services that comply with current government standards).Salaries for new hires; Funding is available for up to 52 weeks (excluding bonuses and social benefits) to support the hiring of a new resource dedicated to market development in Quebec (maximum of one hire during the program, up to $45,000).Commercial representative salaries;Support for the hiring of a new commercial representative in Quebec (excluding bonuses and social benefits), for up to $45,000 and limited to one hire during the program.Trademark registration fees;  Costs associated with registering trademarks in Quebec.Testing, analysis, and certification costs; Including the purchase of normative documents required for approvals, compliance, or certifications that facilitate commercialization.Storage rental fees; For materials or inventory in Quebec, when required by a client or to support integration into a supply chain.Transportation costs;For moving materials or inventory when requested by a client or necessary for supply chain integration.Program Details:Supports initial market consolidation in Québec as a stepping stone to export;Focuses on de‑risking market entry and facilitating buyer integration through strategic tools and hires;Accepts rolling applications while funding remains available.

      Grant Criteria 
      The OVIN R&D Partnership Fund – Electric Vehicle (EV) Stream 2 provides co-investment funding of up to $1,000,000 to support the development, testing, validation, demonstration, and deployment of electric-vehicle and battery-focused technologies, covering light-duty vehicles, heavy trucks/buses, charging infrastructure, and intelligent-transport systems.Grant Value:Up to $1,000,000 per project over a maximum of 24 months. Requires a minimum 2:1 private-sector match (i.e., the applicant and/or private partners must cover at least two-thirds of total project costs). Note: This funding is a co-investment (non-repayable) grant. Eligible Applicants:Ontario-based SMEs (fewer than 500 full-time employees globally). Projects must be carried out in Ontario. Eligible partners can include other SMEs, large enterprises, academic institutions (as collaborators), municipalities, Indigenous communities, and not-for-profits/crown-corporations/transit authorities where relevant. Eligible Activities:Applied development, demonstration, testing, validation, and piloting of EV and battery technologies (e.g., electric powertrains, battery systems, charging infrastructure, hydrogen/alternative-fuel EVs, light-weighting, etc.) Deployment of early-stage EV or smart-mobility solutions (e.g., fleet electrification, charging systems, smart-mobility infrastructure, ITS, etc.) Activities must result in demonstrable, market-ready solutions that can be showcased in-Ontario (e.g., operational EVs, prototypes, pilot deployments) Program Details :Projects must occur within a 24-month timeframe. Private-sector match funds must be cash or eligible private investment; in-kind contributions are not sufficient to meet the match requirement. Applicants must sign a Contribution Agreement before incurring eligible expenses.Reporting requirements include financial, technical, and performance reports as outlined in the program guidelines.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices :The program requires applicants to provide at least two-thirds of total eligible project costs from private-sector sources, as OVIN will contribute up to one-third of eligible expenses, to a maximum of $1,000,000 per project;All matching funds must be cash contributions; in-kind contributions are not eligible toward the required match;Public funding from federal, provincial, municipal, or crown programs cannot be used to satisfy the mandatory private-sector matching requirement, although additional public funding may be used outside the match as long as total public support stays within allowable limits; andProjects must be completed within a maximum 24-month delivery window, and a Contribution Agreement must be executed prior to incurring eligible expenses.Eligible Best Practices :Only costs incurred after the submission of a fully completed application are eligible; retroactive expenses are not permitted under this stream;Applications must clearly disclose all confirmed and anticipated sources of project funding, including the applicant’s contribution and support from:Private-sector partners (required match);Industry associations, networks, or ecosystem partners;Academic or research collaborators;Municipal, regional, or Indigenous partners (permitted, but not toward the private-sector match).Applicants must ensure that no provincial, federal, or municipal public funding is counted toward the required two-thirds private-sector match, and that all combined public contributions remain within OVIN’s allowable funding thresholds;All project activities must take place in Ontario and demonstrate clear pathways toward the development, validation, demonstration, or deployment of EV and battery-related technologies.Links :Program Website : click hereProgram Guidelines : click here

      Grant Criteria 
      The Regional Tariff Response Initiative (RTRI) in British Columbia is part of the Government of Canada's $1 billion strategy to defend Canadian jobs, industries, and supply chains from trade and tariff disruptions. The initiative helps B.C. businesses pivot to new paths to growth by boosting productivity and reducing costs, building more resilient supply chains, reaching new markets and enhancing domestic trade.Grant Value:Repayable Funding - Up to 75% from $200,000 to $10,000,000 per project; Non-Repayable Funding - Up to 50% from $200,000 to $1,000,000 per project;Indigenous-led Businesses - Up to 100% from $200,000 to $10,000,000 repayable and/or $200,000 to $1,000,000 non-repayable.Turnaround Time: Approximately 90 business days from receiving complete application.Eligible Applicants:Incorporated businesses in British Columbia;10-499 full-time employees (SMEs); In continuous operation for at least 3 years leading up to March 21, 2025;Minimum 2 complete years of externally reviewed financial statements;Must have been viable prior to tariffs and either:Have minimum 25% sales in markets targeted by tariffs; orDemonstrate significant likelihood of negative tariff impacts.Eligible Target Markets:International markets;Domestic Canadian markets; andInterprovincial trade markets.Eligible ActivitiesDigitization, automation or technology integration investments; Market diagnostics, development and expansion activities;Strategic alliances and supply chain optimization;Strengthening domestic supply chains and internal trade; Business support and market development services; andReshoring or onshoring of production and R&D. Ineligible Activities:Basic and applied research and development (TRL 1-6);Land and building purchases;Entertainment expenses;Salary bonuses and dividend payments;Refinancing existing debts;Federal and provincial income taxes;Lobbying activities;Donations and membership fees.Program Details:Applications submitted by October 15, 2025 will be priortized;Funding disbursed based on claims for reimbursement of eligible costs;Quarterly claims submission allowed;No collateral required for repayable funding;No penalty for early repayment;Additional repayment flexibilities possible by exception;SR&ED tax credits and other government assistance must be declared;Required reporting includes:Revenue growth;Export sales growth;Jobs created (HQP and non-HQP);Technologies to market;Private sector investment attracted;New technologies/processes implemented. Priority sectors for non-repayable funding:Steel;Forestry value-added products;Metal fabrication and products;Machinery and equipment;Agriculture and seafood value-added products.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Regional Tariff Relief Initiative helps businesses and sectors negatively impacted by new tariffs from the U.S., China and/or Canadian counter-tariffs. The program aims to boost productivity, catalyze growth, and diversify markets by raising productivity, enhancing competitiveness, reducing costs to mitigate tariff impacts, and improving resiliency among Canadian businesses.Grant Value: Up to 50% of eligible project costs from $500,000 to $5 million per project for repayable funding; andUp to 50% up to  $1 million in non-repayable contribution funding for eligible.Turnaround Time: 90 days after submitting complete application.Eligible Applicants: Be an incorporated businesses conducting business in the Prairies;Have been viable prior to newly imposed tariffs by the U.S., China, and/or Canadian counter-tariffs and prior to March 21, 2025;Have at least 1 employee;Have been in operation for at least 2 years;Have staffed operating facilities in the Prairie provinces;Have at least 25% of your sales in the markets targeted by tariffs or are able to demonstrate having been directly negatively affected by the tariffs or the uncertainty they create. This could be demonstrated by:Higher cost of materials;Higher cost from suppliers;Higher retail cost of finished product;Fewer purchase orders or sales;Addition of an import or export tax;Loss of access to markets;Other proof of negative impact.If you are applying for non-repayable funding, you must also:Generate economic benefits for the local economy or region;Play an important role in supporting the local supply chain.Eligible Activities: Productivity improvement Including:Investing in digitization, automation, or technology to enhance business productivity and competitiveness; and Reshoring production, research & development operations, recruiting highly qualified personnel and expertise;Market expansion and diversification including:Developing and diversifying markets to help businesses find new customers; and Business support, market development and diversification, and guidance services.Strengthening supply chains and trade resilience including:Optimizing supply chain logistics and ensuring compliance with standards to gain market access and/or enhance sales;Strengthening domestic supply chains and facilitating internal trade to increase business resilience and reliability of domestic markets.Eligible Costs:Labour (wages and benefits) and material costs;Capital costs (machinery or equipment purchase);Consultancy fees (professional, advisory and technical services);Advisory expenses (planning, business information, counselling advisory services, coaching, mentoring or networking events, workshops or conference fees, fees for business training through business service organizations); Costs related to expanding or maintaining markets; andAll eligible costs must be incremental, reasonable and essential to carrying out eligible project activitiesIneligible Costs: RTRI funding does not support projects that move company operations outside of Canada;Basic and applied R&D (technology readiness levels 1-6);Land acquisition and goodwill;Salary bonuses and dividend payments;Entertainment and hospitality expenses;Refinancing of existing debts;Amortization or depreciation of assets;Purchase of assets for more than fair market value;Lobbying activities;Donations;Dues; andMembership fees.Program Details: Project activities can last up to 3 years and must be completed by March 31, 2028;Repayable contribution funding for businesses is normally repaid with no interest over 5 years in monthly instalments beginning 1 year after project end date;RTRI funding does not support projects that move company operations outside of Canada;Program requires an initial EOI to be submitted before being invited to submit a full application; andPriority will be given to activities that:Have higher proportions of Canadian inputs;Demonstrate greater economic benefits for the Prairies;Support local, regional or national supply chains.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Program allows for funding to be stacked up to 90% with other non Federal funding and prioritizes those that do so; Program may allow for retroactive funding for up to 12 months prior to receipt of signed funding request, but no earlier than March 21, 2025.Process Best Practices:Confirmed, at the time of application submission, other project funding sources including government and non-government;Applicants should consult with accountants and/or Canada Revenue Agency to understand how RTRI funding could affect taxes or other current or future funding agreements.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click hereEOI application: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      Regional Tariff Response Initiative (RTRI) - Southern provides $125K-$10M in repayable funding or $125K-$1M non-repayable to southern Ontario incorporated businesses with 5-500 employees affected by trade disruptions and tariffs. Grant Value: Repayable contributions - up to 75% ($125K-$10M)Non-repayable contributions - up to 50% ($125K-$1M)Up to 100% for Indigenous applicants.Turnaround Time : Pending.Eligible Applicants:Business located and operating in southern Ontario;Be an incorporated, for-profit business (including Indigenous-owned businesses) registered in Canada or Ontario for at least 3 years;Must employ at least 5 full-time equivalent (FTE) employees in southern Ontario, and fewer than 500 FTE employees overall;Must have been viable before the US/CHINA tariffs took effect (before March 21, 2025);Businesses must meet at least one of the following criteria: At least 25% of sales are in markets targeted by the tariffs; ORDemonstrate direct negative impacts such as:Increased production material costs;Increased cost of finished products;Import/export tariffs;Decline in revenue or market access;Employment impacts (layoffs, hiring freezes, etc.);Other documented evidence of negative impact.Eligible Target Markets:Must specify whether markets are regional, national, or international;Must explain how the business serves its customers;Applicants must articulate how their project will:Diversify the markets they serve;Expand into new Canadian or international markets;Reduce exposure to tariff-affected markets; andStrengthen competitive position and increase market share.Eligible ActivitiesDigitizing, automating, adopting/adapting technologies to boost productivity;Market development, diagnostics, expansion (including trade missions);Strengthening supply chains, building strategic partnerships, and compliance upgrades;Activities supporting domestic supply chain resilience and internal trade;Business support, advisory, or market development activities; andReshoring/onshoring production, R&D, or personnel to southern Ontario. Ineligible Activities:Land or real estate purchases, including buildings;Entertainment and hospitality expenses;Motor vehicle purchases, leases, or operational costs;Refinancing existing debt or covering ongoing operational/production costs unrelated to the project;Non-incremental or unreasonable costs, or costs not directly related to eligible project activities;Costs incurred before March 21, 2025 (not eligible).Program Details:Businesses may request either:Repayable contribution;Non-repayable contribution (available only once per business for this initiative).For Non-repayable ($125,000 – $1,000,000), applicants must demonstrate strong economic benefits for the region;Indigenous businesses have tailored provisions (e.g., up to 100% funding coverage);If the applicant has an existing FedDev project, the RTRI project must be distinct;Priority for Non-repayable Funding Based on :Business operates in the region where funding is requested;Business is Canadian-owned;Being able to finish the project on time;Can secure some funding from non-government sources;Work in a sector strongly affected by tariffs;Provides economic benefits to the local community;Prefers to buy Canadian-made goods or use domestic suppliers.Mandatory Attachments:Financial statements (last 2 fiscal years, externally prepared);Most recent interim financial statements;Articles of incorporation/amendments / constituting documents;Supplementary Form;Work plan or project schedule, showing activities, milestones, and detailed budget.Additional documents (required depending on project type):Intellectual Property (IP) strategy (mandatory for IP-intensive firms);Financial projections for 3–5 years;Company structure diagram;Any documents demonstrating:Tariff impacts (e.g., cost increases, lost contracts, revenue decline);Market impacts or opportunities;Sales in affected markets. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Total government assistance cannot exceed 90% of eligible costs;In-kind contributions are NOT eligible as matched funding;Retroactive costs allowed up to 12 months prior to application receipt, but not earlier than March 21, 2025;Process Best Practices:Applicants should first complete the self-screening step before applying;Only one application allowed at a time across all FedDev programs;Project must end by March 31, 2028;Funding is reimbursed based on approved costs incurred during the project;Projects are assessed againt the following criteria :Extent of tariff impacts on the company or sector and the project’s contribution to new or expanded initiatives;Potential to improve productivity, drive growth, or diversify markets;Strength of expected results, project plan, budget, readiness, and organizational capacity, including ability to repay;Quality of risk mitigation measures and, where applicable, the IP strategy.Forms and Links:Program Webpage: click here

Applicants may be from a range of industries, including retail, manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, and construction. To be eligible, applicants must be Scale AI members and must have a consortium of 2 or more applicants.Grant Value: 40% of eligible costs.NOTE: Projects across Canada are being funded however, projects in Quebec have access to more funding. Turnaround Time: 3-4 months.Eligible Applicants:Be members of SCALE.AI (membership applications can be submitted online)(membership fees can be paid once project is approved);Be companies across a range of industries that are deploying AI to enhance their supply chain, including but not limited to:Consumer goods and retail;Industrial goods and manufacturing;Transport and logistics;Healthcare;Infrastructure and construction.Have projects that contribute to SCALE.AI strategic objectives, such as AI adoption and the commercialization of AI-based products;Have applicant CEO or executive endorsement; andMust have a minimum of 2 applicants per consortium and must contain at least one small- and medium-sized business:SMEs, post-secondary or research institutions are all eligible.Eligible Expenses:Salaries, wages, or contracts for carrying out project activities;Costs of purchasing or renting equipment, supplies, or services critical to the project (The amount of funding allocated to equipment and supplies etc. varies, usually 20%-30% is funded) ;Dissemination costs that are vital for the performance of the project; andCapital expenditures that are linked to the objectives of the project agreement and are vital for the success of the project.Ineligible Expenses:In-kind contributions.Program Details:All project-oriented work must be executed in Canada;Projects must be net-new and incremental to regular business;Projects must last a minimum of 1 year and usually last a maximum of 2 years:Projects typically last from 12 to 18 months;All projects must be completed on the timeline set out in the project agreement;Projects more than 2 years are generally deemed to be research and development and this is not funded by this program. For those projects that are selected, a predefined portion of eligible project expenses are reimbursed on a quarterly basis; andThe project members have complete flexibility to decide who will own the Intellectual Property (IP) created in their projects.Neither the Government nor Scale AI will own any of the IP.Evaluation Criteria:Team and project management plan (25%)Business impact (20%)Strategic alignment to Scale AI’s strategic plan (30%)Ecosystem impact (25%)

      Best Practices & Forms
      Process Best Practices:As a Scale AI member, applicants will have the opportunity to connect with other potential project partners, both through the Scale AI platform and at networking events hosted by Scale AI;Non-Scale AI members can submit a project for evaluation, but if the project is selected, the applicant must become a member in order to receive funding;For a better understanding of projects funded by the program, please see the list of funded projects here; andInterested applicants can learn about funding and more by joining one of the twice-weekly information webinars. Sessions are held every Wednesday and Thursday at 3:00 p.m. EST in the link here.Forms:Program webpage: click hereApplication portal: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      Free digital twin technology training (valued at $15,000) for Ontario-based Agriculture, Food/Beverage Processing, Clean Tech, and Manufacturing businesses ready to implement advanced simulation and modelling technology in their operations.  Turnaround Time: Approximately 2-3 weeks.Grant Value:  Free training and Licence estimated at $15,000 CAD per participating company;$2,000 stipend to offset the cost of wages during the training (the funding for this stipend has been exhausted for 2026 intake).Eligible Applicants:Must be a Canadian or Ontario-registered business operating in the Agriculture or Food/Beverage Processing sector (related businesses may also qualify);Must operate in one of four eligible sectors: Agriculture;Food and Beverage Processing;Clean Technology; andManufacturing. The business must have operating facilities in Ontario (with some limited seats available for businesses outside Ontario);Leadership team must be willing and able to participate in all training sessions- Company must demonstrate readiness to implement digital twin technology;Business must have operational processes suitable for digital twin applications (simulation, modeling, optimization). Eligible Trainees:Leadership team members (owners, executives, senior management);Operations managers and production supervisors;IT/Technology leads responsible for implementation;Project managers overseeing digital transformation initiatives;Multiple team members from the same organization can participate;Trainees must commit to attending all scheduled training sessions;Participants must be authorized to make technology implementation decisions. Eligible Training: Digital twin technology fundamentals and applications;Advanced simulation and modelling techniques;Process optimization using digital twin platforms;Hands-on training with Plataine's digital twin software;Implementation planning and strategy development;Data integration and system connectivity;Real-world case studies and sector-specific applications;Practical workshops focused on applying digital twins to business operations; andOngoing technical support and implementation guidance throughout the cohort period. Eligible Training Provider:Plataine (primary digital twin technology provider and training delivery partner);Ontario Chamber of Commerce (program administrator and delivery partner); andExpert trainers and technical specialists are affiliated with the program. Program Details:Free training plus a one-year Unity software license and access to the Unity Hub learning library (including over 400 self-paced learning activities);Cohort-Based Learning (First-Come, First-Served);Training covers digital twin topics like :  Improving CAD files so they work smoothly in digital tools;Connecting live data so systems update in real time;Accessing 3D environments online and modelling real-world settings remotely;C# programming;Building practical tools like product configurators, interactive demos, and real-time building management systems.12-week online program with live weekly classes plus self-paced learning (Total 120 hour commitment based on 10 hrs/week x 12 weeks);The program value includes:access to Plataine's digital twin technology platform during the training period;Expert-led training sessions and workshops;Hands-on implementation support and technical guidance; and Ongoing access to program resources and community.Employers must support participants in achieving a positive employment outcome within six months after training (e.g., change in job duties, title, or compensation);Technical prerequisites include access to a computer with Windows 10, 11; macOS 11+, 8GB RAM,  at least 15 GB of free storage space ,  dedicated graphics card. Hardware upgrades may be needed for successful participation;Possibility to access The Talent Opportunities Program (TOP) with subsidies of up to 50% of the wages -to a maximum of $5,000- for each ‘net new’ placement.Employer Stipend Funding (for Wage Offset) is now exhausted for 2026 applications. - There was not context to this, had to look the guidelines to figure out what this was (see notes above on how to input)

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Possibility to apply for multiple team members (leadership, operations, IT, project managers) to better support outcomes;Apply with a clear business problem or improvement idea in mind so the training can be directly applied to real work and deliver meaningful results.There is a $2,000 non-completion penalty per employee if the participant does not complete the program. This requires strategic candidate selection and schedule commitment planning;Participants are expected to receive one positive career advancement opportunity from their employer within 6 months post-completion. This includes a change in job description/responsibilities (including new responsibilities associated to advancement track), change in title, or change in compensation.Process Best Practices:Early applications are highly advised. Cohorts have limited spaces and fill on a first-come, first-served basis; waitlists may apply;Confirm leadership availability before applying: all participants must attend every scheduled sessions;Show operational readiness: applications are favoured when clear, well-defined processes are in place;The program focuses on practical, real-world implementation;Planning for post-program costs (training is free, but software or implementation costs may follow).Forms: Program Website: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereRegistration Link: click here

      Grant Criteria 
      This is a wage incentive program that offers up to $25,000 of funding to Nova Scotian employers with a labour need that are looking for support to offset the cost of hiring, training, or equipping a new employee to succeed in a permanent position. The amount of financial support made available through START is assessed by Employment Nova Scotia (ENS) on a case-by-case basis. The intent is to help Nova Scotians find meaningful long-term employment while helping employers attract the talent they need.Grant Value: $25,000Turnaround Time: up to 3 weeksEligible Employers:Private-sector, government-funded, non-profit, or charitable organization, social enterprise or a municipality;Have workplace accident/injury insurance coverage for employees;Have business locations in Nova Scotia; andI.e.; Companies with headquarters outside of Nova Scotia are eligible if they also have a physical location in Nova Scotia.Have the capacity to supervise and develop the participants.Note: The program prioritizes assisting small and medium enterprises with fewer than 500 staff.Eligible Candidates:Unemployed and actively seeking full time or increasing employment;A resident of Nova Scotia;Canadian citizens or permanent residents who are legally entitled to work in Canada.Participants may self-identify as:Mi’kmaq or Indigenous; Recent graduates (within the last three years);Persons with disabilities;Recent immigrants (within the last three years);African Nova Scotians;Visible minority (including Persons of African Descent);Acadian and francophone Nova Scotians; orIncome assistance recipients.Unemployed international graduates who meet the following requirements are eligible:Must have graduated from a Nova Scotia (NS) public or private post-secondary institution;Note: not all programs of study authorized by private institutions are eligible for START;Graduates must have studied in NS to obtain a Canadian post-secondary credential that
requires at least 2 academic years of study.The participant must have a valid post-graduate work permit;The occupation must be a NOC (National Occupational Classification) code O, A or B (professional occupations);The position funded through START must be available for a minimum duration of one year.Family members are eligible if the participant is in an underrepresented group and the employer has conducted a fair hiring process.Eligible Expenses:Salary and mandatory payroll deduction costs of a new hire;Training costs of a new hire (1 price quote is required); orEquipment and/or miscellaneous costs of a new hire (2 price quotes are required).Program Details:1 employee per application;Employers can submit only 1 application for START;Exceptions may be granted on a case-by-case basis.The full wage must be paid to the participant including the payment of mandatory and voluntary payroll deductions;Minimum of 30 hours per week:Exception: 15 hours per week may be considered for:Recently established small businesses creating a part-time position which will develop into a full-time position;Cases where special accommodations need to be considered for Persons with
Disabilities; orCases where this level of employment is the norm for the industry.Employers will be required to provide feedback to Employment Nova Scotia on how participants are progressing and the impact of the program on your business;Employers can hire more than one individual through START on a case-by-case basis; andEmployers can reapply to the grant for additional funding 6 months after the end date of your current agreement.Ineligible Employment:Paid strictly on a commission basis, or by the kilometre;Already funded through the Labour Market Development Agreement
(LMDA), Workforce Development Agreement (WDA), or through Department of Community
Services (DCS);Displacing current employees, or those on layoff, vacation,
maternity/parental, or sick leave; andSummer employment.

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides bursaries to full-time secondary and post-secondary students who work in eligible farm, food, seafood, or fisheries jobs in British Columbia during the summer. Students receive up to $3,000 based on the number of hours they work, helping them gain experience while supporting seasonal labour needs in the agriculture sector.Grant value :  Up to $3,000Turnaround Time: To be confirmedEligible Applicants:Students who:Are 16 years or older by May 1 of the program year;Are enrolled as full-time secondary or post-secondary students;Are returning to full-time studies in the fall following the summer work term;Are enrolled in a recognized educational institution; andAre legally permitted to work in Canada.Ineligible Applicants:Students under 16;Part-time students;Graduate and post-doctoral students; andStudents who have completed their studies and are not returning to school.Eligible Activities:Paid employment during the summer work term (Between May 1 and September 1 of the program year);Completion of at least 250 eligible work hours;Work performed in British Columbia; andHands-on, operational, or production-related roles in eligible sectors:Primary Agriculture;Food, Beverage, and/or Seafood Processing;Fishing or Aquaculture;Nurseries for bedding plants (large-scale/wholesale production)Notes: Nurseries for bedding plants are eligible only when operating as large-scale or wholesale operations; garden centres, landscaping businesses, and farm supply or feed stores are not eligible.Ineligible Activities:Employment that is : Outside of British Columbia;With companies based or headquartered outside of BC;In landscaping, garden centres, feed or farm supply stores;At farmer’s markets, hobby farms, community gardens, or apiaries;With research farms, industry associations, non-profits, or food security organizations; andIn remote, office-based, retail, marketing, sales, social media, or event roles.Program Details:The program aims to increase youth and domestic seasonal worker employment in the BC agriculture sector for summer 2026;Bursary is a tiered funding based on documented hours worked during the work season (May 1–September 1, 2026), allowing for 1–4-month blocks of work:250 hours worked = $1,500 minimum500 hours worked = $3,000 maximumProrated payments available for 250–500 hours (e.g., 350 hours = $2,250)Eligible Sectors includes primary agriculture, food/beverage/seafood processing, fishing and aquaculture, large-scale/wholesale bedding plant nurseries; Applications are submitted through the online IAF Client Portal;Applicants may apply before securing employment, but job confirmation is required for final approval;Bursaries are paid after employment is completed and verified, and students must submit:Proof of employment and hours worked (e.g., paystubs or employer verification); andA final report and survey (by Sept 30, 2026).Recipients may be required to acknowledge government funding support in public communications. 

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:Confirm full-time student status and fall enrollment before applying;Ensure the employer and role clearly fall within eligible sectors;Verify the employer is BC-based;Track work hours carefully to meet the minimum threshold; andAvoid roles that are primarily administrative, retail, or remote.Process Best Practices:Apply early, as funding is limited and demand is high;Create and maintain an up-to-date IAF Client Portal account;Keep copies of paystubs and employment records throughout the summer;Submit final documentation promptly after completing work hours;Review acknowledgement requirements before posting publicly about the role or funding; and Contact IAF program staff early if eligibility questions arise.Forms: Program website: click hereProgram Guidelines: click hereApplication portal: click here

      This federally funded program provides non-repayable contributions to help Aboriginal people and/or communities in the Coast Salish territory start, expand, or acquire businesses. Contributions are capped at $99,999 for individual business owners and $250,000 for community-owned businesses. The applicant must have a viable business plan, proof of Aboriginal ancestry, and the ability to cover at least 15% of the total project cost. The goals of the program are to increase the number of viable businesses owned by Aboriginal Canadians in the Coast Salish area, to cultivate a culture of entrepreneurship in the Aboriginal community, and to increase access to capital for Aboriginal businesses. Grant Value:Up to $99,999 for individual businesses;Up to $250,000 for community-owned businesses.Turnaround Time: 6 weeksEligible Applicants:Canadian Aboriginal individuals (Status or Non-Status, Métis, Inuk) residing in the TACC service area, which includes:Lower Mainland (to Squamish);Fraser Valley; andVancouver Island.*Canadian corporations, partnerships, associations, or other legal entities majority owned and controlled by Aboriginal individuals residing in the TACC service area;Applicant must be involved full-time in a management capacity in the proposed business project, and must possess the relevant certifications, qualifications, and/or licenses; andApplicant must be able to contribute at least 15% of the total project cost.  *Note: Northern BC, Central BC, and some parts of Vancouver Island are not included in TACC's service area, but TACC will refer applicants to other Aboriginal Financial Institutions as necessary. If your business falls outside of TACC's service area, you can access similar programming through the AFI that serves your region. Eligible Projects: Projects may involve starting, purchasing, expanding, or modernizing a business, and must create measurable benefits, including but not limited to additional revenue, new markets, and/or new job opportunities;Eligible market expansion activities include advertising campaigns, trade shows, seminars, and conferences;Eligible innovation activities include research, process and product development, productivity improvement, and investment in new technology and/or systems;The minimum project budget for starting, purchasing, expanding, or modernizing a business is $25,000; andThe minimum project budget for marketing and innovation is $10,000. Ineligible Projects:Community infrastructure projects that are unrelated to commercial enterprise;Purchase of land, buildings, and/or investment property; andBusiness activity related to pawn shops, payday loan firms, gaming operations, and/or the production/distribution of alcohol, tobacco, and sexually exploitative materials.Program Details:BEP contribution levels vary depending on the type of project the applicant submits. Higher contribution levels (60-75%) are available for business planning and market expansion activities. Capital projects (including equipment purchase, start-ups, and acquisition) typically qualify for a 25% non-repayable contribution through BEP, but may receive additional fundsthrough the  First Citizen's Fund or the NRT Equity Match grant; The First Citizen's Fund offers loans with a 40% forgiveness portion. All Indigenous entrepreneurs (Status, non-status, Métis, Inuit) can borrow a lifetime maximum of $75,000 from this fund. Applicants who have not already exhausted their First Citizen's Fund allowance can combine it with a BEP contribution;The New Relationship Trust (NRT) Equity Match Grant is offered in conjunction with TACC's other programs and is available to Indigenous entrepreneurs who are members of a BC First Nation, and who live in the TACC service area. The Equity Match Grant is a non-repayable contribution of up to $5000 that reduces the amount of cash equity the applicant has to provide to receive a BEP contribution.TACC will determine whether BEP applicants are eligible for a First Citizen's Fund loan and/or an Equity Match Grant;Combining all three programs significantly increases the non-repayable portion of the funding, but applicants who do not qualify for the additional programs can still receive a non-repayable contribution through BEP.There is one application form for all types of projects (business planning, market expansion, and capital). The  form requires the applicant's business information, a description of their project, a summary of their  business experience, an approximate budget, and the following supporting documents:Evidence of Aboriginal ancestry;Evidence of identity;Resume;Evidence of sufficient cash equity to undertake the project;Letters of commitment from other funders;Financial statements from the last three years (for projects related to existing businesses);Projected financial statements for the next three years;Copies of partnership agreements or incorporation documents;Business plan, if available; andAny additional information supporting the proposal (ie: market studies).Applications are reviewed within 10 business days, and are deemed eligible, ineligible, or sent back to the applicant with a request for more information;Eligible projects can proceed to the next stage in the application process, in which the applicant submits a detailed business plan;TACC provides a template for business plans, but can also issue funding to cover up to 75% of legal, accounting, and/or consulting fees related to the development of the plan;The business plan will be assessed within 30 business days; if approved, TACC will issue a Letter of Offer, outlining the amount and terms of the funding; Each funding agreement is unique, but typical contribution levels for various project costs are outlined in the table below; andProject financials and performance may be monitored for up to three years after the agreement is signed.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This funding can be combined with other provincial and/or federal funding programs;BEP will not fund project costs retroactively; applicants are advised not to commit any project costs before finalizing the funding agreement with TACC; andCredit rating is an important factor in the eligibility assessment; applicants are encouraged to seek a credit report before applying. Forms:Program website: click hereProgram guidelines: click hereApplication form: click here

lifetime (excluding TalentEdge) are required to obtain OCI approval before a new application for
funding is initiated.Eligible Candidates:Recent Undergraduate or Masters graduates from an accredited College/University within three years of graduation;Must be eligible to work in Ontario(Ontario resident) and have employee status for the duration on the internship;Cannot be a conflict of interest with the company;Cannot be enrolled in a co-op program or other equivalent job placement/employment program; andCannot be previously employed by the employer.Program Details: Internships must be full time 4 months in length;Consecutive placements can be funded but only to a total of 2 placements;Internships must be working on an industry-driven project related to one of the six CIT critical technology ares:5G and advanced networks;Artificial Intelligence;Blockchain;Cybersecurity;Quantum; andRobotics.The internship must also be within one of the 4 key sectors:Advanced Manufacturing;Agri-Food; Construction; andMining.Projects must have an R&D component;Interns will receive on-the-job training in areas related to critical technologies;Commensurate with the intern's experience and expertise;Maximum funding per company is $20,000 (2 placements per employer); andProject activities must be carried out in Ontario.

        December 16, 2025Winter 2026 term (January – April 2026) is now open and accepting applications.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This program provides a wage subsidy of up to $7,000 for internships for employers operating in any industry sector. Up to 70% of the new employee’s salary is offered for post-secondary students where a work placement is part of their study plan. The program aims to help to bridge the gap between formal post-secondary learning and the skill requirements of Canadian employers.Grant Value:50% of wages up to $5000 per regular participant;70% of wages up to $7,000 per participant in any of the following under-represented groups:Women in STEM or business;Indigenous students;Visible minorities;Recent immigrants (immigrated to Canada within the last 5 years);Persons with disabilities;First-year students;Students on their first work term. Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Employers:Be a registered Canadian business or non-profit;Have Workplace Safety and Insurance Board (WSIB) or alternate workplace insurance coverage;Committed to paying the student for the role for the duration of the placement in full;In compliance with all federal and provincial human rights and labour legislation, regulations, and any other relevant standards including the Occupational Health and Safety Act and the Employment Standards Act;Employers in all industries may apply; andMust place participants on payroll (must make CPP, EI, and vacation pay contributions).Ineligible Employers:Federal, provincial, territorial or municipal governments;Crown corporations;Hospitals;Post-secondary institutions; andMajor financial sector employers.Eligible Candidates:Registered as a full- or part-time domestic student in a recognized Canadian post-secondary institution;Master's or PhD students are eligible;International students are ineligible.Registered in any program of study;Canadian citizens, permanent residents, or protected persons;Registered in a class with work-integrated learning (WIL) component as part of their study plan;Must send a signed document from the post-secondary institution indicating the student is registered in a program/course where a work-integrated learning component is part of their study plan (e.g. co-op document, letter, etc.);Ideally, the documents should state the school term, the program enrolled, start and end dates,  etc; andTranscripts are generally not acceptable.Cannot be a family member of the employer; andCannot be part of another Student Work Placement Program simultaneously.Note: Apprenticeships are ineligible for program funding.Placement Details:Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between:Winter 2025 - January 1, 2025, to April 30, 2025: No funding AvailableSummer 2025 - May 1, 2025 to August 31, 2025: CLOSEDFall 2025 - September 1, 2025 to December 31, 2025: OPENFull-time or part-time;Eligible forms of Work-Integration Learning:Internships;Field placements;Part-time/short-term intensive hands-on practical experience in a setting relevant to their subject of study.Co-operative education;Alternating academic terms and paid work terms.Apprenticeships;Note: Apprenticeships in a skilled trade are not eligible under this program;Community and industry research/projects;Research that occurs primarily in workplaces, includes consulting projects, design projects, and community-based research projects.Entrepreneurship;Engage in the early-stage development of business start-ups and/or to advance external ideas that address real-world needs for academic credit.Mandatory practicum/clinic placement; andWork experience under the supervision of an experienced registered or licensed professional (e.g. preceptor) in any discipline that requires practice-based work experience for professional licensure or certification.Community service-learning.Meaningful community service with classroom instruction and critical reflection to enrich the learning experience and strengthen communities.No maximum participants per company;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2022, 2023, or 2024, use the number of students hired in the year prior to that first time you accessed SWPP support;If you participated in SWPP for the first time in 2024, use the number of students hired in 2023;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2022, Summer 2023), you must count them in both fiscal years.Work from home placements are eligible;Placements will be counted in the term they start in;Employers can still receive funding for placements with start dates outside the academic term; andEmployers cannot postpone placements and will need to ensure placement(s) occur before the agreement end date or request an agreement extension.

      Grant Criteria 
      The Training-on-the-Job program provides a subsidy for training wages to employers for up to 9 months coverage worth up to 100% of the cost of hiring an individual who is no longer able to return to their regular job and employer due to a workplace injury.Grant Value:Negotiated amount up to 100%Note: While the grant value above is noted at $0, it is because the rate fluctuates per applicant.Turnaround Time: 2 weeksEligible Applicants:Willing to hire a new employee for a permanent position;Have WCB Alberta coverage unless their industry is exempt. (in that case we can do a work assessment)Eligible Trainees:Must be a registered individual with WCB Alberta;Has endured a permanent workplace injury and are experiencing a barrier to employment;May be located within or outside of Alberta at the time of hire.Program Details:The percentages of reimbursement vary and depends on the related skills and abilities the new employee brings to the position;Amounts are negotiated with the case manager or service provider. In addition to wage subsidy, WCB may also provide support with: Coordination and cost coverage of external courses and training if required.Arrangement and cost coverage of ergonomic assessments and workplace modifications that may be needed; andThe cost of any adaptive equipment needed for the new hire to carry out the required tasks.Albertan business will receive WCB protection for the costs of any injury or re-injury that might occur during the program;Canadian businesses outside of Alberta will need to demonstrate other insurance;Employers receive support with prescreening and recruitment of the new hire; andEmployers who are seeking assistance with bringing a permanently injured worker back to work may consider the Workplace Assessment (WA) stream of the TOJ program;WA is designed to help the employee learn new skills outside of their date-of-accident position;Employers receive assistance in: Developing a suitable training plan (if applicable);Coordinating external training, job coaching, or ergonomic assessments (if applicable); andReceive a subsidy for training wages on a declining scale.For a 9 month WA period, WCB-Alberta could subsidize:1st two months at 100%;3rd and 4th months at 75%;5th and 6th month at 50%; and The last 3 months at 25%.This is negotiable and should reflect the skills the worker is expected to learn over the training period and
as per the training plan when applicable.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:WCB often seeks entry-level jobs that provide workers with room for growth (i.e. sedentary and light entry-level positions usually work best).Process Best Practices:For a faster application, employers are recommended to contact a WCB representative at TOJ@wcb.ab.ca to discuss the position they are looking to fill; andIf an employer does not have WCB coverage and does not belongs to a WCB mandatory industry, they can apply for a Workplace Assessment.Forms:Program website: click hereApplication portal: click here
