      Grant Criteria 
      This program offers funding of up to 50% of eligible expenses to a maximum of $250,000 for projects that are aimed at commercializing products or processes in a variety of key economic sectors including food processing, life sciences, manufacturing, digital arts and culture, and more. The goal of the program is to help eligible organizations commercialize the results of university or public research in a new market outside Quebec.Grant Value: Up to $250,000 per projectUp to 50% of eligible expenses for priority sectors; and Up to 35% of eligible expenses for strategic sectors.Turnaround Time: around 3-4 months.Eligible Applicants:Incorporated for-profit businesses;Social enterprises and non-profits organizations (NPOs);Co-ops;Headquartered and registered in Quebec City, Saint-Augustin-de-Desmaures or L-Ancienne-Lorette;Has a product or process that has reached the commercialization phase; The first significant sale of the product/process is expected approximately within 24 months;Has proof of a) ownership of the intellectual property, or b) of the rights of exclusive use of the selected product or process; ANDOperates in one of the following priority sectors; ORAgri-food, food processing and healthy foods;Digital arts and interactive entertainment, financial technologies, artificial intelligence, smart city or other digital products and technologies (excluding services and consulting);Optics-photonics, advanced electronics, measurement and control technologies;Life sciences, biotechnologies, and health technologies;Clean technologies: water, air, soil treatment, eco-mobility, energy efficiency, renewable energies, green chemistry, residual materials, enabling technologies and sustainable development.Operates in one of the following strategic sectors:Arts, culture and heritage;Insurance and financial services;Shops located on commercial arteries;Manufacturing, materials, industrial processing, robotics and industry 4.0;Urban security; andTourism.Ineligible Applicants:Social enterprises, NPOs, and co-ops that do not demonstrate sound democratic governance;Applicants who have not been discharged from a bankruptcy judgment; andApplicants who have outstanding debts with the City of Quebec.Eligible Expenses:Professional fees, consulting services, and studies;Costs and working capital necessary for the implementation of the project;Salaries for human resources assigned to the project at an hourly rate; andPurchase or rental of goods, equipment, and assets related to the project.Ineligible Expenses:Funding for regular business operations;Financing of charitable activities and payment for volunteers;Payment of a debt or the repayment of existing loans;Replacement of government support or existing programs;Expenses incurred before the date of submission of a complete application;Any expense relating to the relocation of a business or part of its production outside the agglomeration of Quebec, unless the City of Quebec consents in writing; andFederal and provincial taxes (GST and QST).Project Details:Projects must be carried out as part of a structured commercialization plan aimed at growth and improving profitability;The location of the project is not restricted to the agglomeration of Quebec though the company must still be headquartered there; Projects must support an applicant's goal of commercializing the results of university or public research, or to commercialize in a market outside of Quebec, the results of R&D developed in the private sector; Projects developed through this program cannot be supported by the "Vitrine Technologique" program as well, since pre-commercial validation must be completed before submitting an application to the Valo-Capitale program; Ineligible projects include those that are discriminatory, controversial or that risk creating a negative image for the City of Quebec;One-time projects of an event nature are also ineligible.Assessment Criteria:Quality and soundness of the business model;Financial capacity of the applicant to complete the project and achieve its objectives;Viability and coherence of the submitted project (relevance of the project, viability of the financial plan, and strength of  the partners involved);Organizational management capacity;Distinctive and innovative character of the project;Economic benefits and impact on employment in the agglomeration of Quebec;Demonstration of the need for financial assistance;Innovative nature of the product or process;Market potential of the product or process; andSupport structure.

      Best Practices & Forms
      Eligible Best Practices:This program cannot fund expenses that are incurred prior to submitting a complete application and applicants should avoid beginning their project before receiving an approval.Process Best Practices:The application form requires various text entries that should be prepared in advance in a document that can be saved and edited before submitting; andThe application form requests applicant information details and description, a project description (timeline, objectives, target market, and partners), a budget plan, and additional information to evaluate the project's ability to meet the assessment criteria.Forms:Program website (French): click hereApplication form (French): click here

        February 11, 2026The program is now open for new employers to apply for Summer 2026 placements.Hiring Request submissions for the Summer 2026 Internship cohort will open on February 23, 2026, for previous employers.
      

      Grant Criteria 
      This federal program provides up to $7,000 for businesses in Canada seeking the ability to hire keen current Canadian students in meaningful positions. Eligible employers should have a maximum of 500 employees across Canada, and the ability to teach new hires entrepreneurial skills.Grant Value: 50% up to $5000 per student per term; OR70% up to $7000 for students from any the following under-represented groups: Women studying in STEM;Persons with disabilities; Indigenous persons;Newcomers to Canada; andFirst-year students.Turnaround Time: 15 business daysEligible Employers:For-profit and non-profits organizations, social enterprises and band councils;Has between 1- 499 employees;Has the capability to pay the balance of student wages not covered by the program;Must be able to attend the mandatory employer onboarding webinar; andPlease check the webinar registration for available sessions.Employers in all industries may apply.Eligible Participants:Current full-time or part-time students (can also be on co-op):Eligible programs include but are not limited to:College/university certificates and diplomas;Bachelor's degree;Master's degree; andEarned doctorate.Can be currently employed by applicant employer;Canadian Citizens, Permanent Residents, or Protected Refugee status; The VFC job board is temporarily paused but the program is offering a simplified Internship Bulletin Board to post position;Studying any discipline; andStudents previously funded by VFC must have completed previous VFC training.Internship Details:Positions focused on innovative or entrepreneurial positions, including but not limited to:Marketing;Business;Computer Science;Research; andThe program may consider more areas on a case-by-case basis.Note: Apprenticeships for trades are ineligible because the program is looking to fund internships that develop transferable skills across sectors and industries.Full-time or part-time;Placements must be "net new," meaning that the SWPP student is incremental to the employer's "baseline" of student hires. An employer's "baseline" is the number of students they hired without SWPP support the year prior to participating in SWPP;Net new baselines must be calculated each year (if you participate in SWPP every year, your net new baseline will increase accordingly).Include co-op and non-co-op students in your initial baseline calculation. Do not include high school students, recent graduates, or international students, as they are not included in the SWPP program;If a student placement crosses over the fiscal year (ie: January - April), they count toward the earlier fiscal year;If you hire a student for separate placements in different fiscal years (ie: Summer 2024, Summer 2025), you must count them in both fiscal years.The employee must be on payroll; Minimum wage: $18/hour or minimum wage for the relevant province (suggested wage: $15 to $20 per hour);Maximum placement duration: 20 weeks;No minimum hours per week;No more than 50% of employee working hours can be allocated towards admin or industry-specific technical work (objective is for intern to develop transferable skills across industries);Wage subsidy will apply to gross wages between:Summer 2026 - OPENING SOONHiring Request Opens February 23, 2026, and Closes March 13, 2026;Terms of placement must be negotiated between the participant and the employer;Work-from-home arrangements / remote positions are permitted but must receive virtual supervision and coaching;Maximum placements per company:First-time employers with 1-2 staff can apply for 1 placement;First-time employers with 3+ staff or returning employers with 1-2 staff can apply for 2 placements;Returning employers with 3-25 staff can apply for 3 placements; andReturning employers with 26+ staff can apply for 5 placements.The same intern-employer match can apply for 2 consecutive semesters;There is no limit on the number of non-consecutive semesters for the same intern-employer match; andParticipants are encouraged to complete an optional 10-hour Intern Training program provided by VFC;Participants will gain access to self-paced programming within the first week of the start date; andCompletion will be required for those looking to be eligible for future VFC programs.

If the organization is dependent on funding to hire your student, please make the employment offer "dependent on funding”;The name of the participant cannot be changed after submission of a Hiring Request. If the name needs to be changed, employers will need to submit a NEW Hiring Request;Any Hiring Requests submitted before employer eligibility approval will not be accepted;The following areas may have flexibility in adjudication:500 employee cap: Larger employees may be considered on a case by case basis, Focus of internship: Other activities above and beyond the list above may be considered'The program is able to provide HR support with finding, interviewing, and hiring the candidate; andReceive 50% of subsidy within 6 weeks of internship start date; the remainder will be administered at the end of the internship.Application Process:Complete employer application;Register for and attend employer eligibility webinar;Upon approval, employers either have identified the participant or will need to post on VFC's Internship Bulletin Board;When eligible participants are identified:Employers submit a Hiring RequestParticipants submit a Student Application;Upon approval, funding contract, offer of employment, and digital wage subsidy worksheet will have to be submitted; and50% of funding will be sent within 6 weeks of the placement start date.Note: Hiring Request submission will hold the funding spot in queue during review, but funding is not secure until funding contract has been submitted successfully.Forms:Program website: click hereEmployer application form: click hereStudent application form: click hereHiring request form: click hereEmployer Eligibility Guide: click hereInternship Bulletin Board: click here
